docs.title: Home
docs.text:
GASPALS is a character template. It starts from the Game Animation Sample (GASP): motion matching locomotion, traversal and the sample's characters. On top of that it adds overlay layering in the style of the Advanced Locomotion System (ALS): the character holds a rifle, a torch or a box while every locomotion animation keeps playing underneath. Around that core sit the systems most third- and first-person games need: a camera system, cover, equipment, first person with aim down sights, ragdoll and takedowns. The systems run on both movement back ends (Mover and the Character Movement Component; a few features are Mover-only) and work in multiplayer.

Everything is a Blueprint inside one content plugin, mounted as /GASPALS. There is no C++ module to compile.

New in 1.2

A new cover system, first person rebuilt around data assets, one Mover pawn with ragdoll and takedowns, an on/off switch for every system, and settings for what used to be fixed values. See the release notes; if you built on 1.0, follow Upgrading to 1.2.

docs.title: GASPALS
docs.text:
Epic's Game Animation Sample, extended with ALS-style overlay layering and a set of modular, networked gameplay systems. Unreal Engine 5.8, Blueprint only.

Get started Tutorials Reference

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• Motion matching locomotion

    The Game Animation Sample's motion matching on two pawns: one on Mover with Network Prediction, one on the Character Movement Component. Walk, run, sprint, crouch, strafe, slide, jump and traversal.

    Mover and CMC pawns

  • Overlay layering

    ALS-style overlay poses blended per body part with curves, on top of motion matching. Item and stance poses, three body styles, aim sweeps and hand IK.

    Overlay system

  • Cover

    Soft cover by walking into walls, sticky cover on a button, cover run to the crosshair, corner turns, vault over cover, and aim from cover that picks the least exposed pose.

    Cover system

  • First person

    True first person on the full body, generated at runtime from your third-person meshes. Three modes, aim down sights, first-person overlays, and per-character eye offsets.

    First person system

  • Equipment

    Data-driven items: a data asset per item links the overlay poses, the attach sockets and the actor to spawn. Rifle, pistol, revolver (hidden from the menu by default), bow, torch, binoculars, box and barrel included. Selection menu and hand IK.

    Equipment system

  • Camera

    Gameplay Cameras with a Blueprint camera director: third person with three distances, first person, top-down and side-scroller, shoulder swap, crouch and cover offsets, crosshair and aim ray.

    Camera system

  • Ragdoll and interactions

    Networked ragdoll with get-up animations, takedowns and shoves between characters, and demo tools to shoot and spawn characters.

    Ragdoll and interactions

  • Retargeted characters

    Manny, Quinn and the MetaHuman Kellan run every system through runtime retargeting from the animation skeleton. Add your own character with an IK Retargeter and a few settings.

    Characters and visual overrides

docs.title: Requirements at a glance
docs.text:
• Unreal Engine 5.8.
  • No C++. The plugin has no code module; a Blueprint-only project can use it.
  • Engine plugins used by the content are listed in GASPALS.uplugin and are enabled with it.
  • Project settings: a few settings live in the project's config files (collision channels, data-driven console variables, navigation, gameplay tags, Network Prediction). The template project has them; Installation gives the lines to copy into your own project.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
These pages explain how GASPALS works, so you can change it with confidence.

Page Read it to understand Architecture The pawn, the system components, the interfaces between them, initialization and the per-frame data flow. Mover and CMC pawns The two movement back ends, how they differ, and which to build on. Animation pipeline How motion matching, overlay layering, aim offset, IK and cover lowering combine into the final pose. Characters and visual overrides How one animation skeleton drives Manny, Quinn, a MetaHuman or your own character. Networking What each system replicates and the patterns to follow. Turning systems on and off The on/off switch of each system, which components you can remove from a pawn, and the interfaces the systems use to talk to each other.

docs.title: Animation pipeline
docs.text:
Each pawn runs one character Anim Blueprint. It is the Game Animation Sample's motion matching Anim Blueprint with GASPALS layering added: overlay poses blended per body part on top of locomotion, an aim offset, procedural IK and cover lowering.

Anim Blueprint Used by /GASPALS/Blueprints/SandboxCharacter_Mover_ABP SandboxCharacter_Mover /GASPALS/Blueprints/SandboxCharacter_CMC_ABP SandboxCharacter_CMC

Both are animated on the UEFN mannequin skeleton. Other characters (Manny, Quinn, the MetaHuman Kellan, or your own) copy or retarget that pose; see Characters and visual overrides.

docs.title: The pose, step by step
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    MM[Locomotion<br>motion matching or hybrid] --> LB
    OP[Overlay pose layer<br>ALI_OverlayPose] --> LB
    OB[Overlay body layer<br>ALI_OverlayBody] --> LB
    LB[ABP_LayerBlending<br>per-bone blends by curves] --> AO[Additive leans<br>and aim offset]
    AO --> Slot[DefaultSlot<br>montages: traversal, interactions, get-up]
    Slot --> Root[Offset root bone]
    Root --> Proc[Procedural layers<br>foot placement, leg IK, hand IK, full body IK]
    Proc --> Hist[Pose history<br>for motion matching]
    Hist --> Cover[CR_Humanoid_CoverLower<br>cover lowering]
    Cover --> Out((Output pose))

  1. Locomotion. Two locomotion setups exist, selected per pawn by a console variable:

    • Full motion matching: the motion matching node picks frames from the pose search databases to match the character's trajectory.
    • State machine / blend stack hybrid: a state machine (idle, locomotion and in-air loops, transitions, idle breaks, and on the Mover pawn the slide) whose states pick animations with choosers and play them through a blend stack.

    DDCvar.LocomotionSetupMover (default 1, hybrid) and DDCvar.LocomotionSetupCMC (default 0, full motion matching) choose the setup. The result is cached as the locomotion pose. 2. Overlays. Two linked anim layers produce the overlay poses: ALI_OverlayPose (what the hands hold: rifle, torch, box...) and ALI_OverlayBody (the body style: default, masculine, feminine). The Blueprints that implement them are linked at runtime by the overlay and equipment systems. An Inertialization node after each layer smooths the switch when a new layer is linked. 3. Layer blending. ABP_LayerBlending (a linked anim graph) blends the overlays onto the locomotion pose bone chain by bone chain: legs, pelvis, spine, head, each arm and hand, in local or mesh space, as additive or override. The weights come from curves on the overlay poses, so each overlay pose decides how much of the body it takes over (see below). 4. Leans and aim offset. Additive leans from the lateral acceleration, then the aim offset layer turns the spine toward the aim direction. 5. Montages. The DefaultSlot plays montages: traversal, takedowns and shoves, ragdoll get-ups. 6. Root and procedural. The offset root bone keeps the feet planted while the capsule turns. The procedural layers run foot placement and leg IK, the hand IK Control Rig (CR_Humanoid_HandIK), and on the Mover pawn a full-body IK pass for character interactions. 7. Pose history records the final pose for motion matching's next search. 8. Cover lowering. CR_Humanoid_CoverLower lowers the pelvis in cover. It runs last so it acts on the final pose.

The Mover Anim Blueprint adds a few steps the CMC one does not have:

Step Mover Anim Blueprint CMC Anim Blueprint After layer blending Procedural_PreLayering: ground alignment while sliding none Leans AdditiveLeans layer A lean additive node in the AnimGraph Before the montage slot A Ragdoll state machine: the ragdoll poses while ragdolling, then a blend out from the ragdoll pose none (the CMC ragdoll is driven by AC_RagdollSystem) After the montage slot Dead Blending none Procedural Procedural_Feet (the CR_Biped_FootPlacement Control Rig, then hand IK) and Procedural_FullBody (full-body IK for takedowns and shoves) One Procedural layer: the Foot Placement node, leg IK, then hand IK

docs.title: Layering curves
docs.text:
Overlay poses carry curves that say how strongly each body part follows the overlay. The pose Anim Blueprints write them from a curve map on each pose (see Overlay system), and ABP_LayerBlending reads them:

Curve Effect layering_legs, layering_pelvis How much the overlay drives the legs and pelvis. 0 keeps the locomotion legs. layering_spine, layering_spine_add Spine override and additive weight. layering_head, layering_head_add Head override and additive weight. layering_arm_l, layering_arm_r Arm weight. layering_arm_l_add, layering_arm_r_add Additive arm weight (arm swing kept on top). layering_arm_l_ls, layering_arm_r_ls Local-space arm weight. Below 1 the arm blends in mesh space, so it keeps its orientation while the spine moves. layering_hand_l, layering_hand_r Hand (finger) weight. enable_handik_l, enable_handik_r Hand IK weight toward the item's IK sockets. enable_cr_aimoffset, disable_cr_aimoffset_pitch, disable_cr_aimoffset_yaw Aim offset Control Rig on or off, and per axis.

A rifle ready pose, for example, takes the legs, pelvis, spine, arms and hands (layering_* at 1), keeps the head free, and turns the left hand IK on so the support hand stays on the handguard.

docs.title: Aim offset and weapon aim
docs.text:
When the character aims, the upper body follows the aim direction in two steps:

  1. The aim rotation drives the spine aim offset. For the player you control it is the live control rotation, on both pawns, so the weapon turns in the same frame as the camera. For remote copies it is smoothed in the character Anim Blueprint with a critically damped spring.
  2. In the overlay Anim Blueprint, the aim pitch is mapped to 0..1 and blends the weapon's aim sweep animations, which raise and lower the arms.

The camera has no rotation smoothing of its own, so any body lag shows against the crosshair: when turning slowly, a smoothed weapon trails each small mouse step and seems to step into place. That is why the player you control has no smoothing by default. Remote copies keep it, because their aim arrives in network steps.

Setting Asset (category GASPALS > Anim > Aim / Overlay > Aim) Default Aim Smoothing Time Local Both character Anim Blueprints 0 (none) Aim Smoothing Time Remote Both character Anim Blueprints 0.2 s Aim Sweep Interp Speed Local ABP_OverlayPose_Base (the ABP_Overlay_<Item> children inherit it) 0 (none) Aim Sweep Interp Speed Remote The same 10

0 means no smoothing: the spring and the sweep interpolation follow the aim at once. Raise the local values only if you want a heavier weapon feel; the weapon then lags the crosshair while turning.

New overlay children

Variables added to ABP_OverlayPose_Base do not reach the class defaults of existing children. When you create an ABP_Overlay_<Item> by duplicating an existing one, the values come along; when you add a new setting to the base, set it on every child.

docs.title: Legs and foot placement
docs.text:
The overlay legs are blended in (layering_legs, layering_pelvis), so carry and ready stances such as the rifle's bent-knee stance show in the legs. Foot placement then plants the feet:

  • Mover pawn: CR_Biped_FootPlacement (Control Rig). Its leg IK measures the leg bone lengths from the posed skeleton every frame, so skeletons with scaled leg bones (the UEFN mannequin's thighs and calves carry a 1.12 scale) keep their real leg length.
  • CMC pawn: the engine's Foot Placement node, then leg IK.

On the Mover pawn the foot placement path follows the engine console variable a.AnimNode.FootPlacement.Enable (on by default: the biped Control Rig; off: plain leg IK). DDCvar.FootPlacementMode is stored by the Mover Anim Blueprint but has no effect. To keep the locomotion legs for an overlay, lower its layering_legs and layering_pelvis curves.

docs.title: Threads and update order
docs.text: The Anim Blueprints use the thread-safe update (BlueprintThreadSafeUpdateAnimation): the game thread only copies the pawn's state (Update_PropertiesFromCharacter, which reads Get_PropertiesForAnimation from the pawn through BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn), and the worker thread computes the rest. DDCVar.ThreadSafeAnimationUpdate.Enable (default on) selects the path; GASPALS' overlay Anim Blueprints read it once at start and run their update on exactly one of the two paths.

docs.title: Console variables that change the animation
docs.text:
Variable Default Effect DDCvar.LocomotionSetupMover 1 Mover Anim Blueprint: 0 full motion matching, 1 state machine / blend stack hybrid. DDCvar.LocomotionSetupCMC 0 CMC Anim Blueprint: 0 full motion matching (work in progress), 1 hybrid. DDCVar.ExperimentalStateMachine.Enable false Experimental state machine path of the CMC Anim Blueprint. DDCvar.MMDatabaseLOD 0 Pose search databases: 0 dense, 1 sparse, 2 extreme sparse (cheaper, less precise). DDCvar.FootPlacementMode 1 Stored by the Mover Anim Blueprint, no effect (the Mover's foot placement follows a.AnimNode.FootPlacement.Enable). DDCvar.OffsetRootBone.TranslationRadius 0 How far the root bone may drift from the capsule. DDCVar.ThreadSafeAnimationUpdate.Enable true Thread-safe animation update.

The full list, with what reads each one, is in Console variables.

docs.title: First person
docs.text: First person uses its own Anim Blueprint (ABP_FirstPerson_UEFN) on generated first-person meshes. It copies the third-person pose and adds camera, aim down sights and arm aim Control Rigs. See First person system.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
GASPALS is built from three layers:

  1. The pawn owns movement, input and the meshes, and exposes its state through an interface.
  2. System components (camera, cover, equipment, first person, overlay, ragdoll, traversal, debug tools) sit on the pawn. Each one is self-contained: it reads what it needs from the pawn and its own settings, handles its own input actions, and asks the other systems for state through small interfaces, never through their classes. Each can be switched off (Turning systems on and off).
  3. Anim Blueprints pull the pawn's state every frame and turn it into a pose, with layers linked in by the systems.
flowchart TB
    subgraph Framework
        GM[GM_Sandbox<br>pawn and character lists] --- PC[PC_Sandbox<br>pawn and character switch, teleport]
    end
    subgraph PawnBox[Pawn: SandboxCharacter_Mover / _CMC]
        Move[Movement<br>CharacterMover or CMC]
        Meshes[UEFN mesh, first-person logic mesh,<br>VisualOverride child actor]
        Systems[System components<br>Camera, Cover, Equipment, FirstPerson,<br>Overlay, Traversal, Ragdoll, VisualOverride]
        Iface[BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn<br>Get_PropertiesForAnimation / Camera / Traversal]
    end
    ABP[Character Anim Blueprint] -->|pull every frame| Iface
    Director[Camera director] -->|pull every frame| Iface
    Systems -->|link anim layers,<br>attach items| ABP
    Systems -->|read state| Iface
    GM -->|spawns| PawnBox

docs.title: The pawns
docs.text:
Pawn Base class Movement SandboxCharacter_Mover Pawn Mover (CharacterMoverComponent) with Network Prediction; physics-based ragdoll (Physics Control), takedowns and shoves, debug tools SandboxCharacter_CMC Character Character Movement Component; ragdoll through AC_RagdollSystem

The pawns share the same systems, except a few Mover-only features (slide, the physics-driven ragdoll, takedowns and the debug tools); they differ in how movement, prediction and replication work. See Mover and CMC pawns.

Each pawn has:

  • a UEFN mannequin mesh running the character Anim Blueprint (the animation source for every character);
  • a hidden first-person logic mesh (SkeletalMesh_FP) running the first-person Anim Blueprint;
  • a VisualOverride Child Actor component for retargeted characters;
  • a Gameplay Camera component (and a legacy spring arm camera used only when Gameplay Cameras are turned off);
  • a Motion Warping component for traversal;
  • the system components below.

docs.title: System components
docs.text:
Component System Initialized with AC_OverlaySystem Overlay poses and body styles the third-person mesh AC_EquipmentSystem Items in hand pawn, third- and first-person meshes, the visual meshes to attach to AC_CameraSystem Perspective, camera attachment, crosshair pawn, visual meshes, Gameplay Camera component AC_RagdollSystem Ragdoll (CMC pawn) pawn, mesh, capsule PhysicsControl, AC_PostABPTick Physical animation and ragdoll strengths (Mover pawn) (set up by the pawn at BeginPlay) AC_DebugTools Demo shot, spawn / rotate, teleport, fly (Mover pawn) (reads its owner when used) AC_FirstPersonSystem First-person meshes and visibility for the pawn, the visible character and the held item the active body and the first-person logic mesh AC_CoverSystem_Mover / _CMC Cover pawn AC_TraversalLogic, AC_TraversalTracer Vault, hurdle, mantle (reads the pawn on every attempt) AC_VisualOverrideManager Visible character (reads the game mode's list) AC_SmartObjectAnimation Using benches and other smart objects (interaction range, box size and object types under GASPALS > Interaction > Trace) (finds the movement component) AC_FoleyEvents Footstep and movement sounds (called by animation notifies)

Components that react to input bind their own input actions (AC_CameraSystem handles the perspective keys, AC_EquipmentSystem the equipment menu, and so on), so adding a component adds its controls. They only receive input when the pawn is player controlled.

docs.title: Initialization
docs.text:
Systems are initialized by the pawn, through the interface BPI_ModularSystems and its event InitializeModularSystems. The pawn calls it at the end of BeginPlay, and AC_VisualOverrideManager calls it again whenever the visible character changes, because the meshes change.

sequenceDiagram
    participant P as Pawn
    participant FP as AC_FirstPersonSystem
    participant O as AC_OverlaySystem
    participant E as AC_EquipmentSystem
    participant C as AC_CameraSystem
    participant R as AC_RagdollSystem (CMC)
    participant Cv as AC_CoverSystem
    P->>FP: UpdateFirstPersonVisuals > SetActiveBody (build FP meshes)
    P->>O: Overlay_Initialize > InitializeSystem(mesh)
    P->>E: Equipment_Initialize > InitializeSystem(pawn, meshes, visual meshes)
    P->>C: InitializeSystem(pawn, visual meshes, camera)
    P->>R: Ragdoll_Initialize > InitializeSystem(pawn, mesh, capsule)
    P->>FP: FirstPerson_InitializePrimitives
    P->>Cv: InitializeSystem(pawn)
    P->>Cv: bind OnCoverVaultReady → traversal

Because the event can run several times, every InitializeSystem is written to be safe to call again. Follow the same rule in your own systems. The _Initialize steps are small pawn functions that find the component by class and skip it when the pawn doesn't have one, so those components can be removed (Turning systems on and off).

When a player possesses the pawn, a client RPC runs SetupCamera (activates the Gameplay Camera for the player controller, or the legacy spring arm camera when DDCVar.NewGameplayCameraSystem.Enable is off) and SetupInput (adds every mapping context of Input Mapping Contexts, default IMC_Sandbox), then BPFL_GASPALS.CheckConsoleVariables, which shows an on-screen warning listing the DDCvar.* console variables the project does not declare.

docs.title: Per-frame data flow
docs.text:
Data is pulled. The pawn implements BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn with getters that assemble its state into structs:

Getter Struct Read by Get_PropertiesForAnimation S_CharacterPropertiesForAnimation: input state, movement state and mode, stance, rotation mode, gait, direction, transform, velocity, acceleration, aim rotation, ground, in cover... Character Anim Blueprints, overlay and first-person Anim Blueprints, cover, the bow Get_PropertiesForCamera S_CharacterPropertiesForCamera: perspective, style, mode (free, strafe, aim), shoulder, stance Camera director Get_PropertiesForTraversal S_CharacterPropertiesForTraversal: capsule, mesh, motion warping, mode, gait, speed AC_TraversalLogic Get_AimRay The crosshair aim ray (origin, direction, aimed point, trace channel and distance), forwarded from AC_CameraSystem Cover (cover target, aim from cover) Get_PropertiesForRagdoll, Get_MMIResult, Get_MMIAnimContexts Ragdoll and interaction data Mover Anim Blueprint (implemented by the Mover pawn)

The Anim Blueprints copy the struct on the game thread (Update_PropertiesFromCharacter) and compute the pose on a worker thread.

Writes go the other way through layer linking: the overlay and equipment systems call LinkAnimClassLayers on the meshes to swap the Anim Blueprints that implement the overlay layers (ALI_OverlayPose, ALI_OverlayBody, ALI_OverlayFirstPerson).

docs.title: Input to movement
docs.text:
Mover pawnCMC pawn

Input actions set the pawn's input state (PlayerInputState: wants to sprint, walk, strafe, aim, crouch). Each frame, Mover calls the pawn's ProduceInput, which builds the input command: move direction (after the cover system's remap), cover data from EvaluateCover, control rotation, gait, rotation mode, crouch request. Mover then simulates the movement modes with that command on the owner and the server, and the pawn caches the simulated result for animation and camera (CacheInputsFromMover).

Input actions set CharacterInputState and add movement input. AC_PreCMCTick runs the pawn's pre-movement update before the Character Movement Component each frame: cover (UpdateCoverCMC), rotation and the speed settings for the current gait. The CMC then moves the character and replicates it as usual.

docs.title: Game framework
docs.text:
Class Role GM_Sandbox Game mode. Default pawn SandboxCharacter_CMC; Pawn Classes Soft (CMC, Mover) cycled by DDCvar.PawnClass; Visual Overrides Soft (Kellan, Manny, Quinn) cycled by DDCvar.VisualOverride. Respawns all players in place when the pawn class changes. GM_Sandbox_Ragdoll Child of GM_Sandbox for RagdollLevel; spawns SandboxCharacter_Mover. PC_Sandbox Player controller: next pawn (N), next character (M), teleport (J; through the pawn's AC_DebugTools when it has one); hides the touch joystick when a gamepad is used.

There is no global game mode in the project settings: each level sets it in its World Settings.

docs.text: You want to Do this Use GASPALS as your game's base Start from the template or copy the plugin; see Use GASPALS in your own project. Change a pawn's behavior Make a child Blueprint of a sample pawn and override functions, or edit the sample. Use the systems on another pawn Add the systems to your own pawn. Show another character Add a retargeted character.

docs.title: Characters and visual overrides
docs.text:
Every GASPALS pawn is animated on one skeleton: the UEFN mannequin. The motion matching databases, overlay poses, traversal montages and Control Rigs are all built for it. To show a different character, GASPALS does not re-author any of that: it hides the mannequin and puts a visual override on top, a separate actor whose meshes copy the mannequin's pose through an IK Retargeter, every frame.

The template ships three visual overrides:

Character Blueprint Skeleton Retargeter Manny BP_RetargetedCharacter_Manny SK_Mannequin (UE5) RTG_UEFN_to_UE5_Mannequin Quinn BP_RetargetedCharacter_Quinn SK_Mannequin (UE5) RTG_UEFN_to_UE5_Mannequin Kellan (MetaHuman) BP_RetargetedCharacter_Kellan metahuman_base_skel RTG_UEFN_to_Metahuman_nrw

All are in /GASPALS/Blueprints/RetargetedCharacters and derive from BP_RetargetedCharacter_Base.

In the demo, press M to cycle: UEFN mannequin, Kellan, Manny, Quinn, and back.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph Pawn[Pawn: SandboxCharacter_Mover or _CMC]
        UEFN[Hidden UEFN mesh<br>character Anim Blueprint<br>motion matching, overlays, IK]
        FPLogic[Hidden UEFN first-person<br>logic mesh]
        CA[Child Actor component<br>VisualOverride]
        Mgr[AC_VisualOverrideManager]
        FPS[AC_FirstPersonSystem]
    end
    subgraph Visual[Visual override actor]
        Body[SkeletalMesh<br>ABP_Retarget_*]
        Cloth[Clothing, face, hair]
        FPM[Generated first-person meshes]
        Setup[First Person Setup<br>DA_FirstPersonSetup_*]
    end
    Mgr -->|spawns class| CA --> Visual
    UEFN -->|RetargetPoseFromMesh| Body
    Body -->|leader pose or<br>post-process copy| Cloth
    Setup -.->|read by| FPS
    FPS -->|builds| FPM
    FPLogic -->|first-person overlay<br>retarget| FPM
  1. The pawn keeps its UEFN mannequin mesh. It runs the full character Anim Blueprint and all gameplay animation. When a visual override is active, it is hidden but keeps ticking.
  2. AC_VisualOverrideManager (on the pawn) holds the override class in its replicated VisualOverride variable. When it changes, ApplyVisualOverride sets the class on the pawn's VisualOverride Child Actor component, hides the pawn's third-person body mesh, and re-runs InitializeModularSystems so every system picks up the new meshes.
  3. The override actor has a body mesh (SkeletalMesh) running a small retarget Anim Blueprint (ABP_Retarget_UE5, ABP_Retarget_Kellan): a Retarget Pose From Mesh node reading the parent skeletal mesh (the pawn's hidden mannequin), then the hand IK Control Rig. Clothing follows the body by leader pose, or by its own post-process Anim Blueprint for meshes on another skeleton (the MetaHuman hoodie and shoes).
  4. First person is handled by the pawn's AC_FirstPersonSystem; the character carries no first-person component. The character tells it what to draw through two interfaces that BP_RetargetedCharacter_Base implements: GetFirstPersonSetup (BPI_FirstPersonCharacter) returns the First Person Setup set on each character (a PDA_FirstPersonSetup asset such as DA_FirstPersonSetup_Manny), and GetVisualBodyMesh (BPI_VisualOverride) returns the body mesh (SkeletalMesh). The component builds the first-person meshes on the character actor and retargets the first-person overlay pose from the pawn's hidden first-person logic mesh with the setup's Retargeter. Mode, arm, camera and motion settings are the pawn's and apply to every character.

The override body ticks after the pawn mesh (the base class adds a tick prerequisite on the body from GetVisualBodyMesh), so the retargeted pose is never a frame behind.

docs.title: Which meshes the systems use
docs.text:
The pawn function GetVisualMeshes returns the visible third-person mesh and the first-person lead mesh: the override's meshes when one is active, the pawn's own otherwise. The systems are initialized like this:

System Works on Overlay (anim layers) The pawn's UEFN mesh. The override gets the overlay through retargeting. Equipment Links the overlay layers on the pawn's UEFN meshes; attaches the items to the visual meshes (sockets overlay_*) and computes hand IK in the visual mesh's hand bones. Camera Attaches to the visual meshes: root in third person, the VB Camera virtual bone in first person. Cover, traversal, ragdoll The pawn (capsule, movement, UEFN mesh). The override shows the result. First person The pawn's AC_FirstPersonSystem, with the override's First Person Setup; the first-person meshes are created on the override actor.

Ragdoll simulates on the pawn's UEFN mesh with its physics asset; the override needs no physics asset for it.

docs.title: Choosing the character
docs.text:
The list of overrides is on the game mode, not on the pawn: GM_Sandbox > Visual Overrides Soft (soft class references), in this order by default: Kellan, Manny, Quinn.

The data-driven console variable DDCvar.VisualOverride selects the entry for every pawn in the world:

Value Character -1 (project default) No global character: each pawn shows its Default Visual Override (none by default, so the UEFN mannequin; see Per pawn). 0, 1, 2... The entry at that index in Visual Overrides Soft.

M (IA_NextVisualOverride) asks the server (PC_Sandbox.NextVisualOverride, then GM_Sandbox.CycleVisualOverride) to add one to the variable, wrapping back to -1. You can also type DDCvar.VisualOverride 1 in the console. The value lasts for the editor session, so it carries over between Play sessions.

To start with a given character, set the variable's default in Project Settings > Engine > Data Driven CVars.

docs.title: Per pawn
docs.text:
Each pawn's AC_VisualOverrideManager has two settings (GASPALS > Characters > General, editable per instance):

Setting Default Use Follow Global Visual Override true Use GM_Sandbox's list and DDCvar.VisualOverride as above. Off: the pawn always uses Default Visual Override and ignores M. Default Visual Override None (UEFN mannequin) The character this pawn shows whenever it does not take a character from the global list: Follow Global Visual Override is off, the game mode is not GM_Sandbox (or a child), or DDCvar.VisualOverride is -1 (or not declared in your project; an orange message at play start then lists the missing console variables, see Installation).

Use it for pawns with a fixed look (an NPC that is always Kellan), or to use the characters in your own game mode. With Follow Global Visual Override on, the default also stands in for the -1 entry of the cycle: a pawn whose default is Manny shows Manny at -1, then Kellan, Manny and Quinn as M cycles.

Requirements of the manager

  • The global selection needs GM_Sandbox (or a child) and the DDCvar.VisualOverride variable (copy the project settings from Installation). Without them the pawn uses its Default Visual Override.
  • The pawn needs a Child Actor component tagged VisualOverride, attached directly to its third-person mesh, and must implement BPI_ModularSystems (the manager re-runs InitializeModularSystems after every change). The sample pawns have both.
  • Setting Visual Override on the manager component in a pawn's Details panel does nothing by itself: the override is applied when the value replicates, not from a default.
  • The selection is made on the server; clients receive the character class through replication.

docs.title: Requirements for a character
docs.text:
Requirement Why An IK Retargeter from IK_UEFN_Mannequin to the character's IK Rig, with a Curve Remap op Third-person pose and first-person overlays. The curve op carries the hand IK curves. A VB Camera virtual bone from root to head First-person camera. root, head, hand_l, hand_r bones Camera attachment, first-person head, equipment hand IK. UE-standard spine, clavicle and neck names (spine_01..spine_05, clavicle_l/r, neck_01) The first-person overlay Control Rigs. Other skeletons can use the TrueFirstPerson mode. The seven overlay_* sockets on the Skeleton Where equipment is attached: overlay_rifle, overlay_pistol, overlay_bow, overlay_box, overlay_barrel, overlay_binoculars, overlay_torch. A first-person setup (PDA_FirstPersonSetup) set as the character's First Person Setup First-person meshes, retargeter and eye offset. Without one, the body mesh is reused in first person with the head hidden, and a warning is shown. The body mesh returned by GetVisualBodyMesh Camera, equipment and first person use it. The base class returns SkeletalMesh; override the function if your body is another component.

The UE5 mannequin and MetaHuman skeletons in the plugin already have the virtual bone and the sockets. The step-by-step guide is Add a retargeted character.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text: One IK retarget costs about 0.16 ms per character (measured in the editor). First person adds a second retarget for the overlay and keeps the hidden first-person logic mesh ticking. The visible body mesh only animates when rendered.

docs.title: Characters on the UEFN skeleton
docs.text: A character that is itself on the UEFN skeleton (another outfit for the mannequin) needs no retargeting: give it a copy-pose Anim Blueprint that copies the pose with Copy Pose From Mesh instead (duplicate ABP_Retarget_UE5, retarget it to the UEFN skeleton and replace the Retarget Pose From Mesh node). Turn the node's Use Attached Parent option on, so it reads the pawn's hidden mannequin, and Copy Curves on, so the hand IK curves reach the character; with it off, the hand IK curves read 0. Its first-person setup needs no Retargeter. The plugin ships no copy-pose Anim Blueprint (the sample characters are all retargeted).

docs.title: Networking
docs.text: Every GASPALS system works on a listen server with clients. This page summarizes what replicates and how, so you can extend the systems without breaking it. Blueprint-only replication follows a few patterns, used throughout.

docs.title: Patterns
docs.text:
Owner predicts, server confirms. The owning client applies a change immediately, then tells the server with a reliable Server RPC. The server sets a replicated variable, and other machines apply it in its RepNotify. Equipment, overlays and the camera perspective work this way.

Movement goes through the movement component. On the Mover pawn, anything that affects movement is part of the input command the owner sends: cover data, crouch, gait, ragdoll requests. Mover simulates it on the owner and the server and replays it on simulated proxies, so no extra replication is needed. On the CMC pawn, the owner shapes its acceleration, which the CMC replicates (p.EnableCharacterAccelerationReplication=1), and extra state travels in RPCs and replicated variables.

Montages play where they must. Root-motion montages (traversal, interactions, get-ups) are played on the server and the owner. Mover syncs a server-played montage to simulated proxies; the CMC replicates root-motion montages itself.

Cosmetics on every machine. Visual reactions (ragdoll physics profiles, sounds, first-person visibility) run on every machine from replicated state or mode changes, not from RPCs.

docs.title: By system
docs.text: System What replicates How Locomotion (Mover) Movement, crouch, gait, rotation mode Mover input commands with Network Prediction (DefaultNetworkPrediction.ini). Simulated proxies get the inputs (bSyncInputsForSimProxy). Locomotion (CMC) Movement, crouch The CMC. The input state (CharacterInputState) is sent to the server with an RPC and replicated to others. Cover (Mover) Cover state Part of the Mover input (S_MoverCustomInputs_Cover). Cover (CMC) Cover state, facing Owner-shaped acceleration, plus a 20 Hz server RPC (ServerUpdateCover) and replicated cover state applied on other machines. Aim from cover Result only Runs on the owner; others see position, crouch and facing. Equipment Selected item Replicated with RepNotify; every machine spawns the item locally. Client sends a reliable Server RPC. Overlay Overlay pose and body Replicated with RepNotify; reliable Server RPC from clients. Camera Perspective Server RPC; replicated to other machines (skip owner). Style and shoulder are local. First person Nothing Owner-only meshes; other players see the third-person character. Traversal The traversal action Owner predicts, reliable Server RPC with the result, server plays it; Mover and CMC sync the montage to others. The server does not replay it for a pawn it controls locally, so a listen-server host, a standalone player or a server AI starts each traversal once. Ragdoll (CMC) Start and stop, impulses Reliable Server RPC, then a reliable multicast. An impulse applied on the server (ApplyRagdollImpulse) is multicast so every machine pushes its own copy of the ragdoll; one applied on a client pushes only its local copy. Ragdoll (Mover pawn) Enter, exit, roll, get-up choice Mover input (S_MoverCustomInputs_Ragdoll), with the injury state replicated. Remote ragdolls are pulled toward the replicated capsule. Takedowns, shoves The interaction Client predicts its own montage and asks the server, which validates and multicasts. Visual override The character class Replicated with RepNotify on the manager component. Pawn switch The pawn class Server RPC from the controller; the game mode respawns players.

docs.title: Testing multiplayer
docs.text:
1. Open the options menu next to the Play button and, under Multiplayer Options, set Number of Players to 2 and Net Mode to Play As Listen Server.
  2. Test on both pawns (N), since they replicate differently.
  3. Watch the client and the server windows: equipment, overlays, cover, traversal and ragdoll should look the same on both.
  4. For the Mover pawn, np.PrintReconciles 1 prints prediction corrections. A handful at events like a takedown is expected; continuous corrections are not.
  5. Use Network Emulation (in the editor's Play settings) with some latency and packet loss to see how the prediction holds up.

docs.title: Rules for your own additions
docs.text:
• Mover: change movement only through the input command and transitions. QueueNextMode from gameplay code runs on one machine only.
  • Never call RPCs every frame for continuous state; send it in the movement input (Mover) or at a fixed rate (the CMC cover sends 20 times a second).
  • Components that use RPCs or replicated variables need Component Replicates on the pawn's component. The camera, traversal, equipment, overlay and visual override components have it on in both sample pawns (set on the pawn's component, not the class default): if you build your own pawn, turn it on for them too. AC_CoverSystem_CMC and AC_DebugTools replicate by default and need nothing.
  • Make cosmetic reactions run from replicated state so late joiners see them too.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text: • The CMC pawn shows small corrections (2 to 4 cm) at sticky cover edge stops and corners.

docs.title: Mover and CMC pawns
docs.text:
GASPALS ships the same character on two movement back ends. Both run the same systems (camera, cover, equipment, first person, overlays, traversal), the same Anim Blueprint design, and both work in multiplayer.

SandboxCharacter_Mover SandboxCharacter_CMC Base class Pawn Character Movement CharacterMoverComponent (Mover 2.0) with Network Prediction CharacterMovementComponent Movement logic Movement modes (Blueprint classes) and transitions Pawn functions before the CMC update (UpdateMovement_PreCMC) Prediction Input commands simulated on owner and server; rollback and resimulation The CMC's client prediction and server corrections Slide Yes (BP_MovementMode_Slide) No Ragdoll Mover Ragdoll mode with a Physics Control component AC_RagdollSystem Ragdoll input X ragdolls; on a floor, X or Space gets up The same Takedowns and shoves Yes No Debug tools AC_DebugTools (demo shot, spawn / rotate, teleport, fly) Teleport only (player controller) Foot placement CR_Biped_FootPlacement Control Rig Foot Placement node and leg IK Default locomotion setup State machine / blend stack hybrid Full motion matching Capsule radius 30, half height 86 radius 40, half height 86 Cover adapter AC_CoverSystem_Mover AC_CoverSystem_CMC Engine status Mover is experimental in 5.8 Production

docs.title: Switching pawns
docs.text:
The game mode spawns the pawn chosen by DDCvar.PawnClass:

Value Pawn (GM_Sandbox) -1 (default) Default Pawn Class: SandboxCharacter_CMC 0 SandboxCharacter_CMC 1 SandboxCharacter_Mover

Press N in game to cycle, or type DDCvar.PawnClass 1 in the console. Every player is respawned in place. With an empty Pawn Classes Soft, N keeps the current pawn class. GM_Sandbox_Ragdoll (RagdollLevel) uses SandboxCharacter_Mover.

To start a project on the Mover pawn, set the Default Pawn Class of your game mode, or the default of DDCvar.PawnClass to 1.

docs.title: The Mover pawn
docs.text:
Mover splits movement into modes. Each mode is a Blueprint (or native) class registered by name on the CharacterMover component:

Mode name Class Use Walking BP_MovementMode_Walking Ground movement: gait speeds, acceleration, turning. Falling BP_MovementMode_Falling In the air. Flying B_MovementMode_Flying Traversal montages and the debug fly toggle (Z). Sliding BP_MovementMode_Slide Slide. Cover BP_MovementMode_Cover Movement along cover. Traversing native Flying mode Registered, not used. Ragdoll BP_MovementMode_Ragdoll Physics ragdoll (X).

Transitions move between modes (into cover, into and out of a slide, the ragdoll requests). See Movement.

Every frame Mover asks the pawn for an input command (ProduceInput), simulates the modes with it, and on a remote machine replays the same commands. Anything that changes movement must therefore go through the input command: the cover system adds its data to it (S_MoverCustomInputs_Cover), the pawn adds its ragdoll enter and exit requests. Changing a mode directly from gameplay code (QueueNextMode) only affects the local machine.

docs.title: The CMC pawn
docs.text:
The CMC pawn is a classic Character. Its movement settings are changed every frame before the Character Movement Component runs, from the pawn's gait (walk, run, sprint, crouch) and direction:

Speeds (forward, strafe, backward) Value Walk Speeds 200, 180, 150 Run Speeds 500, 350, 300 Sprint Speeds 700, 700, 700 Crouch Speeds 225, 200, 180

Acceleration, ground friction and braking are set the same way, per gait, from the pawn's GASPALS > Movement > CMC settings (Gait Max Acceleration, Gait Ground Friction, Braking Deceleration...; see Movement), so changing them on the Character Movement component has no effect.

AC_PreCMCTick makes this update (and the cover update) run after the controller and before the CMC. The CMC pawn starts with strafing on.

docs.title: Which one to build on
docs.text:
• CMC if you want the mature, well-documented Character pipeline and the widest compatibility with marketplace content.
  • Mover if you want the newer movement framework: modular modes, deterministic prediction and rollback, and an easier path to custom movement such as wall running or climbing. Mover is still experimental in UE 5.8, so expect engine changes.

Both pawns share every GASPALS system except a few Mover-only features (slide, the physics-driven ragdoll, takedowns and shoves, and the debug tools; see Known limitations), so systems you add should be tested on both.

docs.title: Ragdoll, interactions and debug tools
docs.text: The Mover pawn is also a physics-driven character: a Physics Control component (kinematic by default, physical animation optional), a Ragdoll movement mode with get-up animations, and takedowns and shoves between characters. See Ragdoll and interactions. Its AC_DebugTools component adds the sandbox's demo and debug tools (shoot into ragdoll, spawn or rotate characters, teleport, fly); see Debug tools. These work in every game mode; RagdollLevel is set up to try them.

docs.title: Settings reference
docs.text: The pawn variables, functions and interfaces are listed in Pawns and Anim Blueprints, and the movement modes in Movement modes.

docs.title: Turning systems on and off
docs.text: Every GASPALS system can be turned off on a pawn without touching its graphs, and some of them can be removed from the pawn completely. The systems don't reference each other's classes: they ask each other for state through small interfaces, so a system that is off (or missing) simply answers "inactive" and the others carry on.

docs.title: The switches
docs.text:
Each system component has a bEnable<System> setting in its General category, on by default. Select the component on your pawn (not the class default: a pawn keeps the value of its own component) and untick it.

The switch is read when the game starts. It is not meant to be toggled during play.

System Setting Off means Camera AC_CameraSystem > Enable Camera System A fixed third-person view with the default style and shoulder. The perspective, style and shoulder keys do nothing, there is no crosshair, and the ragdoll no longer changes the view. The camera itself (Gameplay Camera, camera asset and director, including the crouch, cover and in-air offsets) keeps working. First person AC_FirstPersonSystem > Enable First Person FirstPerson is removed from the available perspectives (the perspective key skips it) and no first-person meshes are built. Cover AC_CoverSystem > Enable Cover No cover. At a low wall, jump mantles instead of the cover vault. Traversal AC_TraversalLogic > Enable Traversal No vaults, hurdles or mantles: jump is a plain jump. In cover, jump does nothing (the cover vault is a traversal action). Equipment AC_EquipmentSystem > Enable Equipment Nothing in hand, even if an item is selected on the component, and the equipment keys do nothing. Overlay AC_OverlaySystem > Enable Overlay The default overlay pose and body; the overlay keys do nothing. Ragdoll (CMC pawn) AC_RagdollSystem > Enable Ragdoll The ragdoll key does nothing, and nothing else can start a ragdoll on that pawn. Debug tools (Mover pawn) AC_DebugTools > Enable Debug Tools Fly, the demo shot, spawn / rotate and teleport do nothing.

Third-person only

For a third-person-only game, turn off Enable First Person (or delete AC_FirstPersonSystem, see below), or remove FirstPerson from the camera's Allowed Perspectives.

docs.title: Removing a component from your pawn
docs.text:
These components can be deleted from a pawn (or left out of your own pawn) without breaking anything:

Component Without it AC_EquipmentSystem Nothing can be held. AC_OverlaySystem The character Anim Blueprint's default layers. AC_FirstPersonSystem No first person: the perspective key skips it. Items still attach in third person. AC_RagdollSystem (CMC pawn) No ragdoll. AC_DebugTools (Mover pawn) No debug tools.

The sample pawns reach these components only through small pawn functions, most of them in the GASPALS > Integration category: Equipment_Initialize, Overlay_Initialize, FirstPerson_InitializePrimitives, UpdateFirstPersonVisuals, GetVisualFirstPersonMesh, Ragdoll_Initialize, Ragdoll_IsActive and Ragdoll_RequestGetUp (CMC pawn), DebugTools_ToggleFly, DebugTools_Shoot and DebugTools_SpawnOrRotate (Mover pawn). Each one finds the component by class and does nothing when it isn't there. Follow the same pattern in your own pawn: never use the component variable directly for these systems, or the pawn stops compiling when the component is deleted.

The camera, cover and traversal components stay on the pawn: the pawn's movement and animation functions read them directly. Use their switches instead.

docs.title: How the systems talk to each other
docs.text:
Each system has one interface, named after it and kept in its folder (BPI_CameraSystem in CameraSystem, and so on). A system finds the one it needs on its owner ("the first component that implements this interface"), so it works with any component that implements it, and gets the inactive answer when there is none or when that system is switched off.

Interface Implemented by Asked by BPI_CameraSystem AC_CameraSystem Cover (first-person cover camera, aim, shoulder), first person (is the view first person), traversal BPI_CameraSystemListener AC_FirstPersonSystem Called by the camera after every perspective change BPI_FirstPersonSystem AC_FirstPersonSystem Camera (camera bone, first-person availability), camera director (scale rig), equipment (create and remove the item's first-person copies) BPI_FirstPersonCharacter BP_RetargetedCharacter_Base First person (the character's first-person setup) BPI_VisualOverride BP_RetargetedCharacter_Base The pawn and first person (the character's body mesh) BPI_CoverSystem AC_CoverSystem_Base (both cover components) Camera director (cover camera offsets) BPI_TraversalSystem AC_TraversalLogic Cover BPI_EquipmentSystem AC_EquipmentSystem Ragdoll (which get-up to play), first-person Anim Blueprint (ADS, hand targets, motion profile) BPI_OverlaySystem AC_OverlaySystem Equipment (re-link the stance when the hands are empty) BPI_RagdollSystem AC_RagdollSystem (Character pawn), the Mover pawn itself Camera (is the character ragdolling), debug tools (shot), the TriggerRagdoll anim notify (start a ragdoll, push a bone), the Character pawn's jump input (get up: RequestGetUp, through the pawn's Ragdoll_RequestGetUp) BPI_RagdollSystemListener AC_CameraSystem Called when the ragdoll starts or ends (ragdoll perspective): by AC_RagdollSystem on the Character pawn, by the Mover pawn itself on the Mover BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn both sample pawns Teleport (TeleportCharacter, used by the debug tools), plus the pawn functions the animation and systems read

The listener interfaces are separate because they are implemented by another system's component (the first-person system listens to the camera, the camera to the ragdoll); a listener must not be mistaken for the system itself.

BPI_FirstPersonCharacter and BPI_VisualOverride are not system interfaces: the retargeted character actor implements them, and the pawn and its first-person system ask the active character through them.

BPFL_GASPALS > Get Ragdoll System returns the actor's component that implements BPI_RagdollSystem, or the actor itself when it does (the Mover pawn ragdolls in its own graph). To make the debug shot and the ragdoll notify work on your own pawn, implement BPI_RagdollSystem on its ragdoll component or on the pawn, and TeleportCharacter from BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn for the teleport and rotate tools. Implement its RequestGetUp too to support the get-up keys (X or Space while ragdolling on a floor); unimplemented, it returns false and the keys do nothing.

The camera keeps a list of listeners rather than looking for them: AC_FirstPersonSystem registers itself when the game starts. If you add your own first-person or camera-driven component, implement BPI_CameraSystemListener and register it with RegisterCameraListener.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
• Installation

    Open the template project, or add the plugin to your project with the settings it needs.

  • Quick start

    A ten-minute tour of every feature in the demo levels.

  • Controls

    Every key and gamepad button, per pawn.

  • Project tour

    Where the pawns, systems, animations and levels live.

After that, read Architecture to see how the pieces connect, then pick a tutorial.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
The pawns add one input mapping context when a player possesses them: IMC_Sandbox (/GASPALS/Input/Mappings/IMC_Sandbox, priority 0), the only mapping context in the plugin. Every control below comes from it, except the debug flying key. The input actions (IA_*) are in /GASPALS/Input. In DefaultLevel, the input wall (BP_InputWall, widget W_InputWall) lists the keyboard bindings; GASP's Controls editor utility widget (Widgets/Controls) lists the keyboard and controller bindings.

Gamepad buttons are named after the Xbox controller: A is the bottom face button, B the right one, X the left one and Y the top one; LB / RB are the shoulder buttons, LT / RT the left and right triggers, L3 / R3 the stick clicks. View is the small button left of the Xbox button (Back on older pads), Menu the one right of it (Start), and the D-pad directions are written D-pad up, down, left and right.

docs.title: Movement
docs.text:
Action Keyboard and mouse Gamepad Notes Move W A S D Left stick Camera relative. Look Mouse Right stick Sprint Shift (hold) LB (hold) Sprinting while crouched stands up. Walk Ctrl (toggle) D-pad left (toggle) Ignored while sprinting. Crouch C (toggle) B Sprint, then crouch to slide (Mover pawn). Jump, vault, mantle Space A Tries a traversal first (vault, hurdle or mantle over what is ahead), then jumps. Crouched: stands up. Held: keeps trying to traverse. Strafe Middle Button (toggle) L3 (toggle) The CMC pawn starts strafing. Aim Right Button (hold) LT (hold) Aim pose and aim camera; aims from cover. Move in world space Arrow keys CMC pawn only (twin-stick style movement for the fixed cameras).

Sprint, walk, crouch, strafe and aim can each be hold or toggle: Toggle Crouch, Toggle Walk, Toggle Sprint, Toggle Aim and Toggle Strafe in the pawn's class defaults (GASPALS > Input > Hold Toggle). The defaults are the ones in the table.

docs.title: Systems
docs.text: Action Keyboard and mouse Gamepad Notes Cover Q X Tap: sticky cover on the wall in front or under the crosshair, or leave it. Hold: cover run to distant cover (it finishes after release; pressing again cancels). Sprinting leaves cover. See Cover. Equipment menu T (hold) RB (hold) Hold to open (the game slows down), scroll to choose, release to equip. Overlay pose menu V (hold) Menu (hold) Default, Injured, HandsTied. Same hold-scroll-release flow. Overlay body menu B (hold) (not mapped) Default, Masculine, Feminine. Menu next / previous Mouse wheel up / down D-pad up / down While a menu is open. Interact E Y Sit on a bench (smart object). On the Mover pawn: shove a character in front, or with aim held, spawn or rotate a character (demo).

docs.title: Camera
docs.text: Action Keyboard and mouse Gamepad Notes Next perspective 1 View Third person, top-down, side-scroller, first person, and back (the camera's Allowed Perspectives). Next camera style 2 (not mapped) Starts on medium, then far, debug view and close (third person); four variants of the fixed cameras. Switch shoulder Alt R3 Third person. Aim in fixed cameras Mouse cursor Right stick Top-down and side-scroller.

docs.title: Ragdoll and interactions
docs.text:
Action Keyboard and mouse Gamepad Pawn Notes Ragdoll X D-pad right Both CMC: the AC_RagdollSystem ragdoll. Mover: the Ragdoll movement mode. Get up X or Space D-pad right or A Both While ragdolling, once the body rests on a floor. A press in mid-air does nothing; press again after landing. Takedown Left Button RT Mover From a standstill, near another Mover character. With aim held: shoot (demo), which ragdolls the character hit. Shove E Y Mover With aim held: spawn or rotate a character (demo).

Takedown and shove work on SandboxCharacter_Mover in every level; RagdollLevel has target characters and physics obstacles to try them on. The demo shot, spawn and rotate come from the pawn's debug tools; see Debug tools.

docs.title: Demo and debug
docs.text:
Action Key Notes Next pawn N Cycles the pawn class (CMC and Mover in DefaultLevel) and respawns every player in place. Next character M Cycles the visual override: UEFN mannequin, Kellan, Manny, Quinn. Teleport J Teleports the pawn to the point you look at (up to 100 m). On the Mover pawn it goes through its debug tools (Teleport Max Distance on AC_DebugTools). Debug flying Z Mover pawn: toggles a flying mode (debug tools). Keyboard only; a raw key in the Mover pawn, not part of IMC_Sandbox.

N and M are handled by the player controller (PC_Sandbox), J by the controller and the Mover pawn's debug tools, Z by the Mover pawn's debug tools. None of these keys has a gamepad binding.

docs.title: Change the controls
docs.text: Edit IMC_Sandbox, or create your own mapping context with the same input actions and list it in the pawn's Input Mapping Contexts (class defaults, GASPALS > Input). The systems listen to the input actions themselves (the cover, camera, equipment and overlay components handle their own actions), so any context that maps the same IA_* assets works. See Add or rebind inputs.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
There are two ways to use GASPALS:

  • Open the template project (GASPALS.uproject). Everything is already configured. Use this to explore the demo, and as the starting point of a new game.
  • Add the plugin to an existing project. Copy the plugin folder, then copy a few project settings that a plugin cannot carry by itself.

GASPALS comes as a project download (the whole template project) and a plugin-only download (just the Plugins/GASPALS folder). Option A needs the project download; option B works with either.

Upgrading from 1.0

Replace the plugin folder as described in Updating GASPALS, then follow Upgrading to 1.2 in the release notes: the collision channels moved, and several assets were renamed or replaced.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Engine Unreal Engine 5.8 Code None. GASPALS is a content plugin with no C++ module; the project can be Blueprint only. Engine plugins Declared in GASPALS.uplugin and enabled with GASPALS (see below). GASPALS itself is enabled in the project's .uproject: the template project does this, and option B below shows how. Packaging A C++ toolchain (Visual Studio 2022 on Windows). GASPALS needs engine plugins that are off by default, so the packaging tool builds a small game target even for a Blueprint-only project. Running in the editor needs no compiler. Disk space The plugin holds the Game Animation Sample animation set and a MetaHuman, so expect several gigabytes. Engine plugins enabled by GASPALS Area Plugins Animation PoseSearch (motion matching), Chooser, BlendStack, AnimationWarping, MotionWarping, CurveExpression, FullBodyIK, RigLogic, MovieSceneAnimMixer, PhysicsControl Movement Mover, ChaosMover, MoverExamples (Mover brings NetworkPrediction) Interaction and AI GameplayInteractions, SmartObjects, StateTree, GameplayStateTree Characters and UI HairStrands, LiveLink (MetaHuman), ModelViewViewModel, DrawDebugLibrary Editor tools only EditorScriptingUtilities, GeometryScripting

The camera system uses Gameplay Cameras, which is enabled by default in 5.8.

docs.title: Option A: open the template project
docs.text:
1. Extract the project download. The project folder contains GASPALS.uproject, Config/ and Plugins/GASPALS/.
  2. Right-click GASPALS.uproject > Switch Unreal Engine version if it is not associated with 5.8, then open it. The project has no code, so it opens without compiling.
  3. The first launch compiles shaders and builds the motion matching databases. This takes a while once.
  4. The editor opens /GASPALS/Levels/DefaultLevel, the main demo. Press Play and continue with the Quick start.

docs.title: Option B: add GASPALS to your project
1. Copy the plugin
docs.text:
Close the editor, then copy the folder Plugins/GASPALS (from either download) into your project's Plugins folder (create it if needed):

YourProject/
├── YourProject.uproject
├── Config/
└── Plugins/
    └── GASPALS/
        ├── GASPALS.uplugin
        ├── Content/
        └── Docs/

Then enable GASPALS in your project. With the editor closed, add it to the Plugins array of your .uproject:

YourProject.uproject
"Plugins": [
    { "Name": "GASPALS", "Enabled": true }
]

(Or open the project, tick GASPALS under Project in Edit > Plugins and restart.) GASPALS is not enabled by default on purpose: enabling it in the project file is what makes the packaging tool build a game target with its engine plugins. Without that, a packaged game closes at start ("Unable to load plugin 'GASPALS' ... missing dependency").

Open the project. The engine enables the plugins GASPALS depends on. In the Content Browser, enable Settings > Show Plugin Content to see the GASPALS Content folder.

docs.title: 2. Copy the project settings
docs.text:
Some settings live in the project's config files, not in the plugin: collision channels and profiles, data-driven console variables, navigation, and a few engine settings. Without them, traversal finds no obstacles, the camera system and the locomotion setup fall back to defaults, and cover runs do not path on clients.

The Project settings reference explains each line. The short version: add these blocks to your project's Config/DefaultEngine.ini (merge with existing sections of the same name).

Config/DefaultEngine.ini
[/Script/Engine.CollisionProfile]
+Profiles=(Name="ObstaclePreset",CollisionEnabled=QueryAndPhysics,bCanModify=True,ObjectTypeName="Obstacle",CustomResponses=((Channel="WorldStatic",Response=ECR_Ignore),(Channel="WorldDynamic",Response=ECR_Ignore),(Channel="Pawn",Response=ECR_Ignore),(Channel="Camera",Response=ECR_Ignore),(Channel="Vehicle",Response=ECR_Ignore),(Channel="Destructible",Response=ECR_Ignore)),HelpMessage="Moving Obstacles for Physics Obstacle Course")
+Profiles=(Name="TraversalObjectPreset",CollisionEnabled=QueryAndPhysics,bCanModify=True,ObjectTypeName="WorldDynamic",CustomResponses=((Channel="Traversable")),HelpMessage="Traversable Level Blocks")
+Profiles=(Name="CharacterCapsule",CollisionEnabled=QueryAndPhysics,bCanModify=True,ObjectTypeName="Pawn",CustomResponses=((Channel="Visibility",Response=ECR_Ignore),(Channel="Cover",Response=ECR_Ignore),(Channel="Camera",Response=ECR_Ignore)),HelpMessage="Pawn capsule of the sample characters: ignores Visibility, Camera and Cover so those traces pass through characters")
+DefaultChannelResponses=(Channel=ECC_GameTraceChannel15,DefaultResponse=ECR_Ignore,bTraceType=True,bStaticObject=False,Name="Traversable")
+DefaultChannelResponses=(Channel=ECC_GameTraceChannel16,DefaultResponse=ECR_Ignore,bTraceType=True,bStaticObject=False,Name="Mouse")

Also copy these two files from the template's Config/ folder (or merge them if you already have them):

File Contents Needed for DefaultNetworkPrediction.ini Network Prediction settings: independent ticking, interpolated simulated proxies, input send counts. The Mover pawn in multiplayer. DefaultGameplayTags.ini Gameplay tags: Foley.Event.*, MotionMatching.*, SmartObject.*, StateTree.* and redirects. Foley sounds, motion matching database tags, the smart object and NPC demos.

Collision channels after the merge

GASPALS adds four channels in the last slots (ECC_GameTraceChannel15 to 18: Traversable, Mouse, Obstacle, Cover), so they don't take the slots a project fills first. Blueprints store a channel by its position among the custom channels, though, so if your project already has custom channels, open the pawns' components after the merge and pick the channels again by name: Traversable Trace Channel (AC_TraversalLogic), Cover Trace Channel (AC_CoverSystem) and, on the Mover pawn, Ragdoll Obstacle Object Types. The +EditProfiles lines give the engine profiles a Cover response; if your project already edits one of those profiles, add the Cover response to your own line instead (only the first edit of a profile is used). See Project settings.

Rendering settings for the MetaHuman

The demo MetaHuman (Kellan) needs the skinning settings of the template's [/Script/Engine.RendererSettings] section: r.GPUSkin.Support16BitBoneIndex=True, r.GPUSkin.UnlimitedBoneInfluences=True, r.SkinCache.CompileShaders=True and r.SkinCache.DefaultBehavior=0. Copy them too if you keep Kellan.

docs.title: 3. Packaging settings
docs.text:
In Config/DefaultGame.ini:

Config/DefaultGame.ini
[/Script/UnrealEd.ProjectPackagingSettings]
+MapsToCook=(FilePath="/GASPALS/Levels/DefaultLevel")

Replace the map with your own levels.

If your project also enables a game feature plugin (the Game Features plugin) and packaging fails with exit code 25 (unknown cook failure), add a GameFeatureData asset type to scan:

Config/DefaultGame.ini
[/Script/Engine.AssetManagerSettings]
+PrimaryAssetTypesToScan=(PrimaryAssetType="GameFeatureData",AssetBaseClass="/Script/GameFeatures.GameFeatureData",bHasBlueprintClasses=False,bIsEditorOnly=False,Directories=((Path="/Game/Unused")),SpecificAssets=,Rules=(Priority=-1,ChunkId=-1,bApplyRecursively=True,CookRule=AlwaysCook))

Don't add it otherwise: without the Game Features plugin, every editor start reports that the GameFeatureData class can't be loaded.

docs.title: 4. Restart and check
docs.text:
1. Restart the editor so the collision channels and console variables load.
  2. Open /GASPALS/Levels/DefaultLevel and press Play. You control the CMC pawn (press N to switch to the Mover pawn). Run at a low block and press Space to vault: if the character only jumps, the collision channels are not set up (see the warning above).
  3. Set a game mode and default map for your own levels: see Use GASPALS in your own project.

docs.title: Updating GASPALS
docs.text:
GASPALS is a template: you are expected to change its assets. To take a newer version later, keep your changes in your own assets where you can (child Blueprints, your own data assets and levels) and replace the plugin folder. Assets you edited inside Plugins/GASPALS need merging by hand.

Then read the release notes of the new version. Each version lists the renamed, removed and re-typed assets and the project settings to update; from 1.0, follow Upgrading to 1.2.

docs.title: Project tour
docs.text:
All GASPALS content is in the plugin, mounted as /GASPALS (in the Content Browser: Plugins > GASPALS Content, with Show Plugin Content on). The top level splits in two: Systems holds the GASPALS systems, and the other folders hold the Game Animation Sample foundation they build on.

/GASPALS
├── Systems/              GASPALS systems (one folder each) and shared helpers
├── Blueprints/           pawns, character Anim Blueprints, movement modes, game mode, controller, data
├── Characters/           UEFN mannequin (animation skeleton, all animations), UE5 mannequins
├── MetaHumans/           the MetaHuman Kellan and shared MetaHuman assets
├── Input/                input actions, the mapping context, the mobile touch interface
├── Levels/               demo levels and the grey-box kit
├── Audio/                foley system and sounds
├── Widgets/              editor panels of the demo (Game Animation Widget, controls, read me)
├── IsolatedExamples/     self-contained examples (look at points of interest)
└── Misc/                 animation curve compression settings

docs.title: Systems
docs.text:
Each system is a folder with its component, its interface (BPI_<System>), data and assets. They are independent: a pawn uses the ones it needs.

Folder Main assets Page Systems/CameraSystem AC_CameraSystem, CameraAsset_SandboxCharacter, CameraDirector_SandboxCharacter, Rigs/ (camera rigs and chooser tables), Data/ (enums, offset rig struct), W_Crosshair, CameraShake_Basic Camera Systems/CoverSystem AC_CoverSystem_Base, _Mover, _CMC, W_CoverMarker, enums Cover Systems/EquipmentSystem AC_EquipmentSystem, Data/ (data assets, chooser, enum), Actors/ (item actors), Assets/ (prop meshes and materials), UI/ Equipment Systems/FirstPersonSystem AC_FirstPersonSystem, PDA_FirstPersonSetup, Setups/ (one first-person setup per body), ABP_FirstPerson_UEFN, ABP_FirstPerson_Host, CR_FirstPerson_*, Motion/ (first-person motion profiles), Tools/ (EUB_SplitFirstPersonMesh) First person Systems/OverlaySystem AC_OverlaySystem, ABP_LayerBlending, OverlayPose/, OverlayBody/, FirstPerson/, UI/ Overlay Systems/RagdollSystem AC_RagdollSystem (CMC ragdoll), BPI_RagdollSystem, BPI_RagdollSystemListener Ragdoll Systems/DebugTools AC_DebugTools (the Mover pawn's demo shot, spawn / rotate, teleport, fly) Debug tools Systems/TraversalSystem AC_TraversalLogic, AC_TraversalTracer, BP_TraversalTester Traversal Systems/ (root) BPFL_GASPALS (function library), BPML_GASPALS (macro library), BPI_ModularSystems (initialization interface) Shared reference

docs.title: Blueprints
docs.text: Asset or folder What it is SandboxCharacter_Mover, SandboxCharacter_CMC The two pawns. See Mover and CMC pawns. SandboxCharacter_Mover_ABP, SandboxCharacter_CMC_ABP The character Anim Blueprints. See Animation pipeline. GM_Sandbox, GM_Sandbox_Ragdoll, PC_Sandbox Game modes (pawn and character lists, pawn switching) and the player controller. BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn, BPI_SandboxCharacter_ABP, BPI_VisualOverride Interfaces between the pawn, its Anim Blueprint, the visible character and the systems. AC_VisualOverrideManager Spawns the visible character (Manny, Quinn, Kellan). AC_PreCMCTick, AC_PostABPTick Tick-order helpers: run pawn logic before the CMC, or after the Anim Blueprint. MovementModes/ Mover movement modes (Walking, Falling, Flying, Slide, Cover, Ragdoll) and transitions. RetargetedCharacters/ The visual overrides and their retarget Anim Blueprints. AI/ NPC controller and StateTrees. SmartObjects/ Bench smart object and the player's smart object component. AnimNotifies/, AnimModifiers/ Notifies (foley, early transitions, motion warping, ragdoll) and animation modifiers from the Game Animation Sample.

docs.title: Characters
docs.text: Folder Contents Characters/UEFN_Mannequin The animation skeleton. Animations/ holds the full animation set: locomotion (Idle, Walk, Run, Sprint, Crouch, Jump, Slide...), Traversal/ montages, Interactions/ (takedowns, shoves, bench), Ragdoll/ and GetUp/, Poses/, AimOffset/, and MotionMatchingData/ (pose search databases, schemas, channels). Rigs/ has the IK Rig, physics asset and full-body IK rig. Characters/UE5_Mannequins Manny and Quinn meshes, their IK Rig and the RTG_UEFN_to_UE5_Mannequin retargeter. RagdollLevel Ragdoll, physical animation, takedowns, physics obstacles. NPCLevel AI characters using smart objects. LookAtPOI_Level The look-at example. docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This tour takes about ten minutes and touches every system. It uses keyboard and mouse; most actions also have a gamepad button, listed with every key in Controls.

docs.title: 1. Open the demo level
docs.text:
The template project opens /GASPALS/Levels/DefaultLevel at start (in your own project, open it from the Content Browser). Press Play (Alt+P). For a bigger view, use Play > New Editor Window.

You start as the CMC pawn (SandboxCharacter_CMC), shown as the UEFN mannequin. The level is a grey-box sandbox: blocks of many heights, walls for cover, teleporters, a target dummy and an input wall that lists the controls.

docs.title: 2. Move around
docs.text:
• Walk, run (default) and sprint (hold Shift). Stop suddenly, turn around, run in circles: motion matching picks starts, stops, pivots and turns from a large animation set.
  • Toggle walking with Ctrl, crouch with C, strafe with the middle mouse button.
  • Press N to switch to the Mover pawn (SandboxCharacter_Mover). It uses the newer Mover movement with Network Prediction. Sprint, then press C: the Mover pawn slides.

docs.title: 3. Traverse
docs.text: Run at a low block and press Space: the character vaults, hurdles or mantles depending on the block's height and depth. Blocks of the traversable kind (LevelBlock_Traversable) are spread across the level. Try them walking, running and sprinting; the animation adapts.

docs.title: 4. Take cover
docs.text:
• Walk into a high wall: the character takes cover and moves along it. A standing character does not take low cover by walking into it: crouch first (C) and it takes cover crouched behind the wall, or use sticky cover (next point).
  • Point the crosshair at a wall and tap Q: a marker shows on the wall and the character snaps to it (sticky cover). Hold Q while aiming at a wall farther away: the character runs there.
  • In sticky cover, hold the move key toward the end of the wall: the character stops at the edge, and walks around an outside corner.
  • Hold Right Button in cover: the character aims from cover, stepping out or standing up only as far as needed to see the target. Release it to go back.
  • Press Space behind low cover to vault over it.

docs.title: 5. Equip items
docs.text:
Hold T. The game slows down and a menu opens. Scroll to Rifle and release. The character holds the rifle with the matching overlay pose on top of all locomotion. Hold Right Button to aim: the arms follow the camera pitch.

Try the other items: pistol, bow (aim to draw), torch, binoculars, box and barrel. Unequip returns to the default pose. The one-handed revolver is included but hidden from the menu by default (see Equipment).

docs.title: 6. Change overlays
docs.text: Hold V for the overlay pose menu (Default, Injured, HandsTied) and B for the overlay body menu (Default, Masculine, Feminine). These change how the body is held, on top of locomotion and items.

docs.title: 7. Cameras
docs.text:
• Press 1 to cycle the perspective: third person, top-down, side-scroller, first person.
  • Press 2 to cycle the camera style (third person starts on medium, then far, debug view and close).
  • Press Alt to switch the shoulder.

In first person, look down: you see your own body. Equip the rifle and aim: the sights line up with the eye.

docs.title: 8. Characters
docs.text: Press M to cycle the visible character: the MetaHuman Kellan, Manny, Quinn, and back to the UEFN mannequin. Everything still works, including first person and equipment: the characters retarget the mannequin's animation at runtime.

docs.title: 9. Ragdoll
docs.text:
• On either pawn, press X to ragdoll. Once the body rests on the floor, press X or Space to get up (a press in mid-air does nothing).
  • On the Mover pawn (N), Left Button from a standstill near another Mover character does a takedown, E shoves. Hold aim and click to shoot characters, or hold aim and press E to spawn one (the debug tools).
  • Open /GASPALS/Levels/RagdollLevel for the full ragdoll demo: you play the Mover pawn, with target characters and physics obstacles.

docs.title: 10. More levels
docs.text: Level Shows NPCLevel AI characters (both pawns) that walk around and use benches through smart objects and StateTrees. Press E near a bench to sit down yourself. RagdollLevel Ragdoll, physical animation, takedowns and shoves, physics obstacles. LookAtPOI_Level An isolated look-at example: characters that look at points of interest you click.

docs.title: Try multiplayer
docs.text: In the Play options (the three dots next to Play), set Number of Players to 2 and Net Mode to Play As Listen Server. Every system is replicated: equip items, take cover and switch perspectives on the client and watch the other window.

docs.title: Debug views
docs.text: The Game Animation Widget button in DefaultLevel opens an editor panel to change the locomotion setup, camera style, physics profile and debug drawing. The same switches are console variables, listed in Console variables.
