docs.text: Questions and feedback: the Polygon Hive Discord.

docs.title: Locomotion and movement
docs.text:
• Motion matching locomotion from the Game Animation Sample: starts, stops, pivots, turns in place, idle breaks
  • Two locomotion setups: full motion matching, or a state machine / blend stack hybrid
  • Walk, run, sprint, crouch, strafe and aim, with gamepad analog walk and run
  • Hold or toggle, chosen per action (sprint, walk, crouch, strafe, aim) on each pawn
  • Mover pawn with Network Prediction, and Character Movement Component pawn, sharing every system (slide, physics ragdoll, takedowns and debug tools are Mover-only, see Limitations)
  • Slide (Mover) with slope-based speed and an anti-spam cooldown
  • Traversal: vault, hurdle and mantle with ledge detection and motion warping
  • Foot placement, offset root bone, additive leans

Movement · Traversal

docs.title: Animation layering
docs.text:
• ALS-style overlay poses blended per body part (legs, pelvis, spine, head, arms, hands) by animation curves
  • Relaxed, ready and aiming states per item, with aim sweeps that follow the camera pitch
  • Overlay body styles: default, masculine, feminine
  • Hand IK to item sockets
  • Aim offset with short local smoothing and longer remote smoothing

Overlay · Animation pipeline

docs.title: Equipment
docs.text:
• Data-driven items: one data asset links the actor, the overlay poses and the attach sockets
  • Rifle, pistol, revolver (one-handed, hidden from the menu by default), bow (with draw), torch, binoculars, box, barrel
  • Hold-to-open selection menus with slow motion
  • First-person copies of item meshes generated at runtime

Equipment

docs.title: Cover
docs.text:
• Soft cover by walking into walls, sticky cover on a button, upgrade from soft to sticky
  • Low and high cover, automatic crouch, pelvis lowering adapted to the cover height
  • Cover run to the cover under the crosshair, along the navmesh
  • Corner turns, chained around pillars
  • Vault from cover
  • Aim from cover: the least exposed pose that can hit (in place, step out at an edge, stand over low cover)
  • Three facing styles (face the wall, shoulder to the wall, back to the wall) chosen for each of four cases (standing or crouched, soft or sticky), wall distance per case, cover marker
  • First-person cover behaviors

Cover

docs.title: Camera and first person
docs.text:
• Gameplay Cameras with a Blueprint camera director and chooser tables
  • Third person (close, medium, far), first person, top-down, side-scroller
  • Shoulder swap, crouch and cover offsets, ragdoll camera
  • Full-body first person generated at runtime, in three modes
  • Aim down sights, arm aim offset, stable head, per-character eye offset
  • First-person motion: procedural sway, bob, breathing and landing kicks on the hands and item, per item profile
  • Allowed perspectives per pawn (first person only, third person only, or any mix), crosshair at the aim point
  • First-person meshes for retargeted characters, including MetaHuman clothing

Camera · First person

docs.title: Characters
docs.text:
• One animation skeleton (UEFN mannequin) drives any character through runtime retargeting
  • Manny, Quinn and the MetaHuman Kellan included
  • Switch characters at runtime

Characters and visual overrides

docs.title: Physics and interactions
docs.text:
• Networked ragdoll with get-up animations and rolling (Mover)
  • Optional physical animation (Mover): set DDCVar.CharacterPhysics.DefaultProfile to 1 and the body reacts to contacts (0, the default, is kinematic)
  • Takedowns and shoves between characters with multi-character motion matching
  • CMC ragdoll that keeps the running momentum
  • The same ragdoll and get-up keys on both pawns (get up once the body rests on a floor)
  • Ragdolls that settle without jitter
  • Physics obstacle course level
  • Debug tools: shoot characters into ragdoll, spawn or rotate them, teleport, fly

Ragdoll and interactions

docs.title: AI and world
docs.text:
• NPCs with StateTrees that patrol and use smart objects (benches)
  • The player can use smart objects too
  • Look-at points of interest example
  • Grey-box level kit with traversable blocks, teleporters and a target dummy

docs.title: Multiplayer
docs.text:
• Every system replicated, on both pawns, for listen servers and clients

Networking

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Blueprint only, no C++
  • An on/off switch on every system, an interface per system, and components you can delete from a pawn (Turning systems on and off)
  • Every system Blueprint categorized, described and commented
  • Console variables for runtime switches and debug drawing
  • On-screen warnings for setup problems: missing console variables, an empty input mapping, camera perspectives, overlay maps and incomplete first-person setups
  • Complete Blueprint reference

docs.title: Release notes
docs.text: What changed in this release of GASPALS, and how to upgrade a project built on the previous version (1.0).

docs.title: 1.2 (October 2026)
docs.text:
GASPALS for Unreal Engine 5.8. This release turns the sample into a set of modular systems that work on both pawns: a new cover system, a rebuilt first-person system driven by data assets, one Mover pawn with ragdoll and takedowns, per-system switches and interfaces, and settings for everything that used to be a fixed value in a graph. If you built on 1.0, read Upgrading to 1.2 first.

Highlights

  • Cover: soft and sticky cover, cover runs along the navmesh, corner turns, vaulting and aiming from cover, a cover marker, on both pawns and in multiplayer.
  • First person: one component on the pawn generates the first-person meshes of the pawn, the active character and the held item from a setup data asset per body. Three modes, aim down sights, procedural hand and item motion.
  • One Mover pawn with the ragdoll, physics control, takedowns, shoves and debug tools.
  • Modular systems: every system has an on/off switch, every system but the debug tools has its own interface, and most components can be deleted from a pawn.
  • Configurable: perspectives, crosshair, camera offsets, trace channels, input contexts, hold or toggle, movement tuning, menus and widgets are settings.

docs.title: Pawns and movement
docs.text:
Added

  • One Mover pawn. SandboxCharacter_Mover has the ragdoll movement mode, the Physics Control component and its profiles, takedowns and shoves, hit reactions and injury states, and the debug tools, in every game mode.
  • System switches: Enable Camera System, Enable First Person, Enable Cover, Enable Traversal, Enable Equipment, Enable Overlay, Enable Ragdoll (CMC) and Enable Debug Tools, read at start. See Turning systems on and off.
  • Deletable components: the equipment, overlay, first-person, CMC ragdoll and debug tools components can be removed from a pawn without breaking it.
  • System interfaces, one per system folder: BPI_CameraSystem, BPI_CameraSystemListener, BPI_FirstPersonSystem, BPI_CoverSystem, BPI_TraversalSystem, BPI_EquipmentSystem, BPI_OverlaySystem, BPI_RagdollSystem and BPI_RagdollSystemListener. The pawn interface BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn gains Get_AimRay (aim ray, trace channel and distance) and TeleportCharacter.
  • Input Mapping Contexts on both pawns (context and priority); an empty map shows a warning.
  • Console variable check: at play start the local player sees one orange message listing the GASPALS DDCvar.* console variables the project does not declare (BPFL_GASPALS.CheckConsoleVariables). A missing DDCvar.VisualOverride or DDCvar.PawnClass now means no override and the game mode's default pawn, instead of the first list entry.
  • Hold or toggle per action on both pawns: Toggle Crouch / Walk / Sprint / Aim / Strafe (defaults unchanged).
  • CMC pawn: auto-strafe and target lock with the same settings as the Mover pawn (the auto-strafe state replicates), and movement tuning that used to be fixed values: Gait Max Acceleration, Gait Ground Friction (with sprint speed ranges), Braking Deceleration, Stopping Braking Friction and Falling Rotation Rate.
  • Sprint Max Angle from Facing on both pawns.
  • Mover modes: Slide Cooldown (stops slide spam), Slide Enter Speed / Slide Exit Speed on the Slide mode; Just Landed Deceleration / Duration on the Walking mode; Falling Rotation Rate on the Falling mode; a Cover movement mode and transition.

Changed

  • GM_Sandbox_Ragdoll, RagdollLevel, DefaultLevel and the ragdoll notifies use SandboxCharacter_Mover.
  • In cover the gait is Walk unless crouched, and Sprint during a cover run. The Mover slide never starts in cover.
  • The CMC pre-tick runs after the controller, so cover and movement read this frame's input.

Fixed

  • The Mover ragdoll mode reads the pawn's capsule size instead of fixed values.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
Added

  • IA_CoverSticky and IA_CoverRun, both on Q by default. Map IA_CoverRun to its own key to split them.
  • X (IA_Ragdoll) ragdolls the Mover pawn, the same key as on the CMC pawn (it replaces R). While ragdolling, X again or Space (gamepad D-pad right or A) gets up, on both pawns.
  • Gamepad bindings for cover (X: tap for sticky cover, hold for a cover run), the takedown (RT; with LT held, the demo shot), the equipment menu (hold RB), the overlay pose menu (hold the Menu button) and the next perspective (View button).

Changed

  • Ragdoll input is the same on both pawns, and the character only gets up once the body rests on a floor (a press in mid-air does nothing; press again after landing). Before, the Mover ragdoll pawn ragdolled with R (IA_TriggerRagdoll), X did nothing on Mover pawns and only Space got up, and the CMC pawn toggled with X even in mid-air while Space did nothing.
  • The DefaultLevel input board (W_InputWall, keyboard) and the Controls editor utility widget (keyboard and controller) list the current bindings: cover and cover run, interact, ragdoll and get-up, camera perspective, style and shoulder, the menus, the Mover-only takedown, demo shot, spawn / rotate and debug flying, teleport, next pawn and next character.
  • IA_Crouch, IA_Walk and IA_Strafe fire on press and on release (for hold mode).
  • Gamepad: walk moved from RB to D-pad left and ragdoll from X to D-pad right, so X is cover and RB the equipment menu.
  • Mover debug flying moved from the gamepad left stick click to Z (keyboard only); the left stick click only toggles strafe.
  • On the Mover pawn, Left Button is a takedown and E a shove; with aim held they are the demo shot and spawn or rotate.

Removed

  • IA_Traverse (traversal runs from IA_Jump), IA_TriggerRagdoll (R on the Mover ragdoll pawn; X replaces it), the unused IMC_GASPALS_* contexts, and the ... (2) duplicate input assets and mobile HUD textures.

docs.title: Camera
docs.text:
Added

  • Allowed Perspectives: first person only, third person only, or any mix; the perspective input cycles them, and the start and ragdoll views fall back when not allowed (with a warning; the ragdoll-view warning stays silent while Camera Perspective During Ragdoll is at its ThirdPerson class default, and the ragdoll keeps the current view).
  • Third Person Camera Bone: the bone the camera follows in every perspective but first person.
  • Show Crosshair, Crosshair Widget Class, Aim Trace Channel and Aim Trace Distance.
  • Camera Offset Rigs per pawn (crouch, right shoulder, low cover, cover edges, first-person scale, in air, sliding, traversing, ragdoll); clearing an entry turns that offset off. Pass Movement Mode To Camera feeds the movement-mode rigs.
  • RegisterCameraListener: components implementing BPI_CameraSystemListener hear every perspective change.

Changed

  • The crosshair is a dot at the aim point for the local player, in every perspective; the widget only draws it.
  • The ragdoll camera works on both pawns. Only the owning player's copy switches; the perspective replicates.
  • The ragdoll camera switches to third person by default (Camera Perspective During Ragdoll is ThirdPerson), so players in first person, top-down or side-scroller watch the ragdoll from behind.
  • The style input (2) cycles every entry of E_CameraStyle, so styles you add join the cycle.
  • Allow Camera Control During Ragdoll is renamed Allow Camera Switch: it lets the perspective and shoulder inputs work during a ragdoll (looking around was never blocked).
  • The first-person field of view comes from CameraRig_FP_Base; the first-person scale applies only in Split mode (CameraRig_FP_Scale). The first-person camera follows the body setup's Camera Bone.
  • CameraShake_Basic moved to /GASPALS/Systems/CameraSystem.
  • The camera's first-person warnings name AC_FirstPersonSystem.

Fixed

  • The CMC pawn's Gameplay Camera component no longer auto-activates (as on the Mover pawn): only the player's pawn runs a camera system, activated when a player possesses it, so placed and remote CMC pawns no longer evaluate their own camera every frame. This also removes an engine ensure ("precision loss while converting matrix to GPU format") when playing LookAtPOI_Level.

Removed

  • Enable First Person Rendering, Enable First Person Field Of View, First Person Field Of View, Enable First Person Scale and First Person Scale (see Changed).
  • The old camera copy /GASPALS/Blueprints/Cameras and CameraRig_FP_Offset_Crouch (the first-person camera follows the head).

docs.title: Cover
docs.text:
Added

  • A new cover system: AC_CoverSystem_Base with the AC_CoverSystem_Mover and AC_CoverSystem_CMC adapters (the sample pawns keep the component name AC_CoverSystem). See Cover.
  • Soft (auto) and sticky cover, low cover with Auto Crouch Low Cover, High Cover Height measured from the feet, stops at edges, gentle bends and chained corner turns.
  • Cover run along the navmesh: hold the cover run button; a tap prefers sticky cover; a started run finishes after the button is released.
  • Vault from cover, and aim from cover (Enable Cover Aim) with the least exposed pose that can hit.
  • Pelvis lowering behind low walls, once the character has reached the wall (Cover Lower Settle Tolerance).
  • Cover camera offsets and shoulder switch (Enable Cover Camera Offsets, Enable Cover Shoulder Switch), and first-person behaviors (First Person Sticky Cover, First Person Auto Cover).
  • The cover marker (Show Cover Marker, Cover Marker Widget Class, Draw Size, Wall Offset) and Cover Trace Channel.
  • Switches and tuning: Enable Auto Cover, Enable Sticky Cover, Enable Cover Run, Engage Rule, Move Into Cover, wall distances per stance and cover type, facing, side input threshold, probes, re-entry cooldowns, cover run timing, and Enable Debug (draws the cover traces).
  • Multiplayer on both pawns. Cover is on by default.

Removed

  • The previous AC_CoverSystem class and the pawn-level cover variables (see Upgrading to 1.2).

docs.title: Traversal
docs.text:
Added

  • Traversable Trace Channel and Room Check Trace Channel.
  • Traversal > Check settings per pawn: trace radius, half heights, speed and reach ranges, air reach.
  • First Person Traversal Turn Speed / Threshold, and traversal from cover (the cover vault).

Changed

  • AC_TraversalLogic replicates on the Mover pawn.

Fixed

  • Traversal no longer starts twice for a pawn the server controls locally (listen-server host, standalone, server AI).
  • Mover pawn: the 2 m mantle no longer ends low inside the ledge.

docs.title: Equipment
docs.text:
Added

  • Revolver: a one-handed item (DA_Equipment_Revolver, BP_Equipment_Revolver, the M9 mesh) using the Pistol1H overlay in third person and the new ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Pistol1H in first person (high-ready hold, one-handed aim down sights).
  • Left Hand Bone / Right Hand Bone, Equipment Menu Widget Class and Menu Time Dilation on the equipment component.
  • Hidden Equipment: slots left out of the menu and skipped when scrolling (default: Revolver). They can still be selected from Blueprints.
  • Per item (PDA_Equipment): Hand IKSocket, ADSSocket, ADSEnter Speed / ADSExit Speed, ADSHand Offset, First Person Motion Profile and Create First Person Copy.

Changed

  • Item actors have a single mesh; the pawn's first-person system makes their first-person copies (owner only, no collision).
  • The equipment component owns the menu highlight; the menu widget only displays it.
  • Menu order (the order of Enum_Equipment): Unequip, Rifle, Pistol, Revolver, Bow, Torch, Binoculars, Box, Barrel.
  • The Revolver is hidden from the menu for now (see Hidden Equipment); remove it from that list to use it.

Fixed

  • The menu opens for the pawn's own player controller (not player 0). A client sends its selection once instead of twice. Unequipping resets the hand IK targets. Destroying the pawn with the menu open removes the menu and restores the world speed.

Removed

  • The hand-made _FP item meshes and first-person tags, ABP_Equipment_HandIK, and the switcher widgets' CycleState. DestorySpawnedActors is renamed DestroySpawnedActors.

docs.title: Overlays and animation
docs.text:
Added

  • Overlay Pose Layers and Overlay Body Layers maps: a new stance or body style is a map row (a value with no row prints a warning). Overlay Pose / Body Menu Widget Class and Menu Time Dilation on the overlay component.
  • Ready Hold Time Idle / Moving and Aim Min Time per overlay.
  • Aim Smoothing Time Local / Remote on the character Anim Blueprints and Aim Sweep Interp Speed Local / Remote on the overlays.

Changed

  • The legs layer is enabled: overlay stances show in the legs (layering_legs, layering_pelvis).
  • Overlay changes are instant.
  • The local player's weapon aim follows the view in the same frame (Local values 0, the Mover uses the live control rotation): no lag and no stepping when turning.

Fixed

  • A stance set on the pawn shows at spawn and comes back after unequipping.
  • Injured and HandsTied are real overlays.
  • Mover foot placement measures the leg bone lengths, so knees no longer bend or twist under overlay leg poses.

docs.title: First person
docs.text:
Added

  • AC_FirstPersonSystem, on the pawn only. It generates the first-person meshes of the pawn, of the active retargeted character and of the held item. See First person.
  • Setup data assets (PDA_FirstPersonSetup): Full Meshes, Arms Meshes, Body Meshes, Retargeter, Eye Offset, Camera Bone, Head Bone, and the advanced Pipeline Anim Class, Retarget Host Anim Class and Mesh Suffix. One per body: DA_FirstPersonSetup_UEFN (both pawns), _Manny, _Quinn, _Kellan.
  • First Person Mode: FirstPersonOverlay (default), FirstPersonOverlaySplit and TrueFirstPerson (also the automatic fallback for a body without a retargeter), set on the pawn for every body.
  • Settings: arm pitch limits, First Person Camera Follow Lean, First Person Full Body View, First Person Camera Vertical Smoothing, First Person Max Root Yaw Lag.
  • First-person motion: procedural hand and item motion (look and move sway, bob, breathing, jump and landing kicks) that fades while aiming; the camera never moves. Profiles (PDA_FirstPersonMotion: Unarmed, Pistol, Rifle, Bow, Heavy), per item or per pawn, a global First Person Motion Intensity and a disable_fp_motion montage curve. See Tune first-person motion.
  • MetaHuman clothing support, the template Anim Blueprint ABP_FirstPerson_Host for other skeletons, the editor tool EUB_SplitFirstPersonMesh, and on-screen setup warnings.
  • BPI_FirstPersonCharacter (GetFirstPersonSetup): a visual override hands its first-person setup to the pawn's first-person system through it. BP_RetargetedCharacter_Base implements it with its First Person Setup.
  • Generated meshes are AC_FirstPersonSkeletalMesh / AC_FirstPersonStaticMesh components, which remove themselves cleanly when the body or the item changes.

Changed

  • No component tags: the third-person mesh and everything attached under it is the third-person body.

Removed

  • AC_FirstPersonRendering (replaced by AC_FirstPersonSystem), first-person components on characters and items, ABP_FirstPerson_UE5, the unused ABP_FirstPerson_CopyPose and the CR_FirstPerson_StableBones rigs.

docs.title: Characters
docs.text:
Added

  • Default Visual Override and Follow Global Visual Override per pawn (fixed characters, game modes other than GM_Sandbox).
  • First Person Setup on retargeted characters, BPI_VisualOverride (GetVisualBodyMesh), and first-person arms and no-arms meshes for Manny, Quinn and Kellan.

Changed

  • Switching character hides only the pawn's third-person body. The body mesh no longer has to be the first child of the root.
  • The CMC pawn's manager component is named AC_VisualOverrideManager, like on the Mover pawn. Kellan's Blueprint is renamed BP_RetargetedCharacter_Kellan.

Fixed

  • Loading Kellan no longer reports load errors or LOD warnings.

Removed

  • The unused ABP_CopyPose_UEFN (a copy-pose Anim Blueprint for characters on the UEFN skeleton; see Characters to make one).

docs.title: Ragdoll and interactions
docs.text:
Added

  • Ragdoll settle (Mover): Ragdoll Settle Speed, Delay and Blend Time; a ragdoll lying still no longer shakes its hands.
  • Obstacle course: Ragdoll on Obstacle Hit, Ragdoll Obstacle Object Types, Ragdoll Obstacle Trace Radius.
  • CMC: characters without a player get up by themselves once the ragdoll rests (Auto Get Up, Auto Get Up Delay 3 s, Auto Get Up Max Speed), as on the Mover pawn.
  • CMC ragdoll entry: Inherited Velocity Scale (a running character keeps its momentum), Left Leg Bones / Right Leg Bones (the legs collide with each other).
  • BPI_RagdollSystem (RequestRagdoll, ApplyRagdollImpulse, IsRagdollActive, RequestGetUp) on the CMC component and the Mover pawn. RequestGetUp ends the ragdoll and plays the get-up only while ragdolling on a floor; both pawns' ragdoll and jump inputs call it (the CMC pawn through Ragdoll_RequestGetUp).
  • Bench interaction settings: trace start and end distance, half extent and object types.

Changed

  • DDCVar.CharacterPhysics.DefaultProfile is 0: outside ragdoll the Mover body is kinematic, so hands no longer catch on walls. Set it to 1 for the physical animation profile.
  • AC_RagdollSystem is for the CMC pawn only (the Mover pawn ragdolls through its movement mode).
  • Same ragdoll and get-up keys on both pawns, and get-up only on a floor (see Input).

Fixed

  • CMC: leaving ragdoll restores the capsule and mesh collision the pawn had before and puts the mesh back on the capsule.
  • Mover: ragdoll entry, exit and takedowns restore the capsule's own collision profile.
  • Mover, packaged game: the ragdoll physics profiles no longer stop applying about a minute after start. The PhysicsControl component holds its Physics Control Asset through a soft reference only, so the asset was garbage-collected; the pawn now keeps the loaded asset in LoadedPhysicsControlAsset from BeginPlay.

docs.title: Debug tools
docs.text:
Added

  • AC_DebugTools on the Mover pawn (/GASPALS/Systems/DebugTools): demo shot (aim + Left Button), spawn or rotate (aim + E), teleport (J) and debug flying (Z), with Enable Debug Tools, Shot Trace Distance, Shot Impulse, Spawn Trace Distance, Max Spawned Characters and Teleport Max Distance. See Debug tools.

Removed

  • The former ragdoll pawn's demo functions and its separate crosshair.

docs.title: Multiplayer
docs.text:
Fixed

  • The Mover pawn's camera and traversal components and the CMC pawn's visual override manager replicate. The camera perspective replicates both ways, and a client's character change reaches every machine.
  • Possession setup, input state and character switching (M) use reliable RPCs.
  • CMC: a ragdoll impulse (ApplyRagdollImpulse on the server) pushes the body on every machine, not only on the server.
  • CMC: other machines no longer log an error every frame in the top-down and side-scroller views.
  • Cover lowering looks the same on every machine.

docs.title: Project
docs.text:
Added

  • GASPALS.uplugin declares the engine plugins the content uses, with the docs and support links.
  • A Cover trace channel (default Block; every engine profile answers it like Visibility).
  • Placed CMC and Mover characters and a navigation volume in DefaultLevel.
  • A Credits and license page, and a plugin README.md with the requirements, install steps and the documentation link.

Changed

  • The GASPALS collision channels moved to the last slots (ECC_GameTraceChannel15 to 18) so they don't clash with a project's own channels.
  • The project file is GASPALS.uproject. Packaging settings point at /GASPALS paths, and the Win64 package builds.
  • GASPALS is no longer enabled by default: the project enables it in its .uproject. That is what makes packaging build a game target with GASPALS's engine plugins; before, a package of a project without other code plugins used the stock game executable and closed at start ("missing dependency").
  • Every system Blueprint has categories (<System>|<Feature>), descriptions and commented graphs.
  • The editor opens DefaultLevel at start (it opened RagdollLevel).

Fixed

  • No plugin asset references missing /Game content.

Removed

  • The LookAtPOI example's About videos, which were never shipped, and their media assets; the About pages keep their text.

docs.title: Upgrading to 1.2
docs.text:
From GASPALS 1.0:

  1. Collision: copy the new collision block from Installation (the channel slots moved and Cover was added). If your project has its own channels, pick these again by name: Traversable Trace Channel (AC_TraversalLogic), Cover Trace Channel (AC_CoverSystem) and Ragdoll Obstacle Object Types (Mover pawn). Components with Custom collision need a Cover response (Ignore when they ignore Visibility).
  2. Config: copy the console variables (DDCVar.CharacterPhysics.DefaultProfile is now 0), bAllowClientSideNavigation=True, and the /GASPALS maps-to-cook and touch interface paths. Add the GameFeatureData asset scan rule only if your project enables the Game Features plugin (see Installation).
  3. SandboxCharacter_Mover_Ragdoll is removed: point child Blueprints, casts, placed actors and game modes at SandboxCharacter_Mover. Its demo functions are now AC_DebugTools; its ragdoll key is X.
  4. Cover: the previous AC_CoverSystem class is gone. Use AC_CoverSystem_Mover or AC_CoverSystem_CMC; the cover settings and Enable Cover live on the component. Custom pawns need the cover hooks and Get_AimRay, see Add the systems to your own pawn. Custom pawns implementing BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn must also implement its new TeleportCharacter.
  5. First person: AC_FirstPersonRendering became AC_FirstPersonSystem, on the pawn only (set Default Setup). For each character, create a PDA_FirstPersonSetup with its first-person meshes, retargeter, bones and eye offset, and set it as First Person Setup. Remove first-person components, rendering tags and hand-made _FP item meshes from characters and items. Set the first-person mode and settings on the pawn only. Replace ABP_FirstPerson_UE5 and the StableBones rigs with a Retargeter in the setup (the host Anim Blueprint handles other skeletons).
  6. Camera: the first-person field of view and scale settings and Enable First Person Rendering are gone. Use Allowed Perspectives, CameraRig_FP_Base for the field of view and Split mode for the scale. The old copy in /GASPALS/Blueprints/Cameras is deleted: point references at /GASPALS/Systems/CameraSystem (CameraDirector_SandboxCharacter, CameraAsset_SandboxCharacter, E_CameraMode and E_CameraStyle in Data, the rigs in Rigs, third-person rigs named CameraRig_TP_*). CameraRig_FP_Offset_Crouch is deleted (the first-person camera follows the head).
  7. Renames: BP_RetargetedCharacter_Kellan (was BP_RetargeterCharacter_Kellan), the CMC pawn's AC_VisualOverrideManager (was BP_VisualOverrideManager), DestroySpawnedActors (was DestorySpawnedActors), CameraShake_Basic in Systems/CameraSystem, AC_CameraSystem.UpdateCameraAttachment (was UpdateCameraAttachement), AC_OverlaySystem.SelectNewOverlayPose (was Select|NewOverlayPose).
  8. Ragdoll: AC_RagdollSystem.InitializeSystem no longer takes IsMoverCharacter; remove the component from Mover-based pawns. BPI_RagdollSystem gained RequestGetUp: implement it on your own implementers to support the get-up keys (unimplemented, it returns false). If you copied the Mover pawn's Physics Control setup, keep a hard reference to the loaded Physics Control Asset, as LoadedPhysicsControlAsset does.
  9. Menus: the switcher widgets' CycleState is gone. Custom menus read the highlighted entry from the equipment or overlay component and are set through the ... Menu Widget Class settings.
  10. Input: map IA_CoverSticky and IA_CoverRun in your own contexts; IA_Traverse, IA_TriggerRagdoll and the IMC_GASPALS_* contexts are deleted; IA_Crouch, IA_Walk and IA_Strafe also fire on release, so check your own handlers.
  11. Removed Anim Blueprints: ABP_CopyPose_UEFN and ABP_FirstPerson_CopyPose are deleted (they were unused), and so is ABP_Equipment_HandIK (see Equipment); replace any reference to them in your own content.
  12. Camera: Allow Camera Control During Ragdoll is now Allow Camera Switch (bAllowCameraSwitch); set it again on your pawns if you changed it.
  13. Equipment enum: the new Revolver sits after the Pistol in Enum_Equipment, so Bow, Torch, Binoculars, Box and Barrel have values one higher than in 1.0. Pins, data assets and chooser cells resolve by name; re-check anything that stores the equipment as a raw byte number.
  14. Enable GASPALS in your project: the plugin is no longer enabled by default. Enable it in Edit > Plugins or add { "Name": "GASPALS", "Enabled": true } to your .uproject (see Installation); a packaged game needs it.
  15. Feel: the overlay legs layer, instant overlay changes, unsmoothed local aim and the kinematic Mover body change how the sample feels; the settings above bring the old behavior back where you need it.

docs.title: Console variables
docs.text:
GASPALS uses data-driven console variables: variables declared in Project Settings > Engine > Data Driven CVars (stored in DefaultEngine.ini) that Blueprints read with Get Console Variable Int/Float/Bool Value. Some Blueprints also listen to changes (OnDataDrivenCVarChanged), so typing a new value in the console applies it immediately.

Change one at runtime from the console (`):

DDCvar.PawnClass 1
DDCvar.VisualOverride 0
DDCvar.Traversal.DrawDebugLevel 3

In the editor, the values persist for the editor session (across Play sessions). The demo levels also have an editor panel to set them: press the Game Animation Widget button in DefaultLevel or RagdollLevel to open it (it is an editor utility widget, so it only exists in the editor).

They are project settings

The variables are declared in the project's config, not in the plugin. If a project lacks them, an orange on-screen warning at play start lists the missing ones. DDCvar.PawnClass and DDCvar.VisualOverride then fall back to -1 (the game mode's default pawn, no override); every other read returns 0 or false, which changes behavior (for example the old spring-arm camera instead of Gameplay Cameras). Copy them as described in Installation.

docs.title: Game setup
docs.text: Variable Type Default Read by Values DDCvar.PawnClass Int -1 GM_Sandbox Index into the game mode's Pawn Classes Soft. -1 (or out of range): the game mode's Default Pawn Class. In GM_Sandbox: -1 and 0 = SandboxCharacter_CMC, 1 = SandboxCharacter_Mover. Changing it respawns every player in place. N cycles it. DDCvar.VisualOverride Int -1 GM_Sandbox, AC_VisualOverrideManager Index into the game mode's Visual Overrides Soft. -1: no override (UEFN mannequin). 0 Kellan, 1 Manny, 2 Quinn. M cycles it. DDCVar.NewGameplayCameraSystem.Enable Bool true Both pawns (SetupCamera) true: Gameplay Cameras (CameraAsset_SandboxCharacter and the camera director). false: the old spring arm camera. Read when the pawn is possessed, so restart Play after changing it. DDCvar.CameraStyle Int 1 AC_CameraSystem Third-person camera distance: 0 close, 1 medium, 2 far, 3 debug view. Also picks the top-down and side-scroller rig variant. DDCvar.ControlStyle Int 0 Mover pawn 0 standard, 1 twin stick. Twin-stick aiming is not wired up: IA_TwinStick_AimDirection has no mapping in IMC_Sandbox, so add a gamepad right-stick mapping before using 1.

docs.title: Locomotion and animation
docs.text: Variable Type Default Read by Values DDCvar.LocomotionSetupMover Int 1 SandboxCharacter_Mover_ABP 0 full motion matching, 1 state machine / blend stack hybrid. DDCvar.LocomotionSetupCMC Int 0 SandboxCharacter_CMC_ABP 0 full motion matching (work in progress), 1 hybrid. DDCVar.ExperimentalStateMachine.Enable Bool false SandboxCharacter_CMC_ABP Experimental state machine path of the CMC Anim Blueprint. DDCvar.MMDatabaseLOD Int 0 Both character Anim Blueprints Pose search databases: 0 dense, 1 sparse, 2 extreme sparse. Sparser is cheaper and less precise. DDCvar.StrafeStyle Int 1 Mover pawn Directions used while strafing: 0 forward, back, left, right; 1 forward and back; 2 forward only. Also changes when sprint is allowed while strafing. DDCvar.AimStyle Int 0 Mover pawn The same direction sets while aiming. DDCvar.AnalogInputStyle Int 1 Mover pawn 0 single gait (always run); 1 walk or run by stick deflection (run above 0.7). DDCvar.FootPlacementMode Int 1 SandboxCharacter_Mover_ABP Stored by the Mover Anim Blueprint but not used: the foot placement follows a.AnimNode.FootPlacement.Enable. DDCvar.OffsetRootBone.TranslationRadius Float 0 Both character Anim Blueprints How far the root bone may drift from the capsule. DDCVar.ThreadSafeAnimationUpdate.Enable Bool true Character, layer blending and overlay Anim Blueprints Run the animation update on worker threads. Overlay Anim Blueprints read it once at start. docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Adapter A small component that connects a shared system core to one movement back end. AC_CoverSystem_Mover and AC_CoverSystem_CMC are the cover adapters. Aim sweep Additive animations that raise and lower a weapon's arms with the aim pitch (AO_<Item>_<Stance>_Sweep). ALS Advanced Locomotion System, a community locomotion framework. GASPALS borrows its overlay layering: per-body-part blending driven by animation curves. Anim layer interface (ALI) An interface of linked animation layers. A character Anim Blueprint calls the layer; another Anim Blueprint that implements the interface is linked at runtime to provide the pose. GASPALS uses ALI_OverlayPose, ALI_OverlayBody and ALI_OverlayFirstPerson. Camera director The Blueprint (CameraDirector_SandboxCharacter) that tells Gameplay Cameras which camera rig to run each frame. GASPALS picks the rig from the perspective, style and character state with chooser tables. Auto cover (soft cover) Cover taken by walking into a wall, kept while staying close, left by moving away. Chooser table (CHT) An asset of the Chooser plugin that picks a result (an animation, a montage, a camera rig) from a table of conditions. GASPALS uses them for traversal montages, equipment poses, get-ups and camera rigs. CMC The Character Movement Component, Unreal's classic character movement. SandboxCharacter_CMC uses it. Component template The copy of a component inside a Blueprint (shown in its Components panel). Its values override the component class defaults for that Blueprint. GASPALS settings are tuned on the pawns' component templates. Cover run Holding the cover button while aiming at distant cover: the character sprints there along a navmesh path and takes sticky cover. Data-driven console variable (DDCVar) A console variable declared in Project Settings (Data Driven CVars) rather than in code. GASPALS uses them for runtime switches and debug drawing. Data asset (DA, PDA) An asset that holds settings and references. A primary data asset class (PDA_*) defines the fields; each data asset (DA_*) fills them, for example one per equipment item or per first-person body. Equipment item Something the character holds: a data asset (DA_Equipment_*), an actor (BP_Equipment_*) and overlay poses. First-person modes TrueFirstPerson (the third-person pose seen from the eyes), FirstPersonOverlay (first-person arm poses on the full body) and FirstPersonOverlaySplit (separate arms and body meshes). First-person setup A PDA_FirstPersonSetup data asset per body (DA_FirstPersonSetup_*): the first-person meshes, the retargeter, the camera and head bones and the eye offset that AC_FirstPersonSystem uses for that body. Game Animation Sample (GASP) Epic Games' sample project for motion matching locomotion and traversal. GASPALS starts from it. Layering curves Animation curves (layering_*, enable_*) that set how much of each body part an overlay pose takes over. Hold or toggle How a sprint, walk, crouch, strafe or aim button behaves: held (active while the button is down) or toggled (press to switch on, press again to switch off). Set per action on each pawn. Logic mesh A UEFN mannequin mesh on the pawn that runs the animation for other meshes to copy. The pawn's own mesh runs the character Anim Blueprint; it is hidden while a visual override shows another character, which retargets its pose. The hidden first-person logic mesh (SkeletalMesh_FP) runs the first-person Anim Blueprint. Motion matching Animation selection by searching a database of poses for the frame that best matches the character's current pose and future trajectory (the PoseSearch plugin). Mover Unreal's newer movement component framework with Network Prediction. SandboxCharacter_Mover uses it. Its behavior is split into movement modes (Walking, Falling, Cover, Slide...) and transitions between them. Network Prediction The engine plugin that runs Mover's simulation on clients and server with prediction and correction. Its project settings are in DefaultNetworkPrediction.ini. Overlay A pose layered over locomotion: what the hands hold (overlay pose) and the body style (overlay body). Retargeting Transferring animation from one skeleton to another with an IK Rig and IK Retargeter. GASPALS retargets from the UEFN mannequin to Manny, Quinn and MetaHumans at runtime. Shove and takedown Paired animations between two Mover characters, matched with multi-character motion matching. The victim's animation ends in a ragdoll, and the victim gets up as usual. Sticky cover Cover taken with the cover button. It holds the character to the wall until it is left on purpose. System switch The Enable <System> setting on each system component (Enable Cover, Enable Equipment...). Off, the system stays on the pawn but does nothing, and the other systems carry on. Traversal Vault, hurdle and mantle moves over obstacles, chosen by a chooser table and played as montages with motion warping. UEFN mannequin The mannequin skeleton of Unreal Editor for Fortnite. GASPALS animates on it. Visual override A separate actor that shows a different character on top of the pawn, driven by the pawn's logic mesh. Manny, Quinn and Kellan are visual overrides. VB Camera A virtual bone from root to head that carries the first-person camera position.

docs.title: Input actions
docs.text: Input actions are in /GASPALS/Input, mapped in /GASPALS/Input/Mappings/IMC_Sandbox (the context the pawns add). Gamepad buttons use the Xbox names (see Controls). "Mover" is SandboxCharacter_Mover, "CMC" is SandboxCharacter_CMC.

docs.title: Locomotion
docs.text:
Action Keys Handled by Mover CMC IA_Move W A S D, left stick Pawn Read in ProduceInput (camera relative) Add Movement Input (camera relative) IA_Move_WorldSpace Arrow keys Pawn Not used Add Movement Input in world X/Y IA_Look_Mouse Mouse Pawn Yaw and pitch Yaw and pitch IA_Look_Gamepad Right stick Pawn Yaw and pitch (scaled by frame time) The same IA_Look_Gamepad_FixedCamera Right stick Pawn, AC_CameraSystem Aim direction in fixed cameras The same IA_Sprint Shift, LB Pawn Hold; stands up from crouch Hold IA_Walk Ctrl, D-pad left Pawn Toggle (not while sprinting) Toggle IA_Crouch C, B Pawn Toggle (on the ground or sliding) Toggle (not falling) IA_Strafe Middle Button, L3 Pawn Toggle Toggle (starts on) IA_Aim Right Button, LT Pawn Hold Hold IA_Jump Space, A Pawn Cover vault, traversal, else jump (crouched: stand up; sliding: stand up). Held: retries traversal. In the Ragdoll mode: get up (RequestGetUp, only on a floor). Cover vault, traversal, else jump. Ragdolling: get up (Ragdoll_RequestGetUp, only on a floor).

IA_Sprint, IA_Walk, IA_Crouch, IA_Strafe and IA_Aim have a Pressed and a Released trigger, so they fire on press and on release. Whether each one holds or toggles is the pawn's Toggle Sprint / Walk / Crouch / Strafe / Aim setting (GASPALS > Input > Hold Toggle); the table shows the defaults.

docs.title: Systems
docs.text: Action Keys Handled by Does IA_CoverSticky Q, X (gamepad) Pawn, which calls AC_CoverSystem Started: RequestStickyCover; released: ReleaseStickyCover. IA_CoverRun Q, X (gamepad) Pawn, which calls AC_CoverSystem Started: RequestCoverRun; released: ReleaseCoverRun. Held past Sticky Tap Time: run to the targeted cover. IA_Equipment T, RB AC_EquipmentSystem Hold (Hold trigger, 0.1 s): equipment menu; release to equip. IA_Overlay_Pose V, Menu AC_OverlaySystem Hold (Hold trigger, 0.1 s): overlay pose menu. IA_Overlay_Body B AC_OverlaySystem Hold (Hold trigger, 0.1 s): overlay body menu. IA_Select_Next / IA_Select_Previous Wheel up / down, D-pad up / down Equipment and overlay components Move the highlight of an open menu. IA_Camera_Perspective 1, View AC_CameraSystem Next allowed perspective (blocked during a ragdoll unless Allow Camera Switch is on; does nothing with one allowed perspective). IA_Camera_Style 2 AC_CameraSystem Next style. IA_Camera_SwitchShoulder Alt, R3 AC_CameraSystem Toggle the shoulder. IA_Interact E, Y AC_SmartObjectAnimation; Mover pawn, AC_DebugTools Use a smart object (bench). Mover pawn: shove, or with aim held spawn/rotate a character (debug tools).

docs.title: Ragdoll and interactions
docs.text: Action Keys Handled by Does IA_Ragdoll X, D-pad right AC_RagdollSystem (CMC pawn), Mover pawn Ragdoll; while ragdolling, get up (RequestGetUp: only once the body rests on a floor, a press in mid-air does nothing). The jump input gets up too. IA_Takedown Left Button, RT Mover pawn, AC_DebugTools Takedown; with aim held, demo shoot (debug tools).

docs.title: Demo
docs.text:
Action Keys Handled by Does IA_NextPawn N PC_Sandbox Next pawn class (server RPC to the game mode). IA_NextVisualOverride M PC_Sandbox Next character. IA_TeleportToTarget J PC_Sandbox; AC_DebugTools on the Mover pawn Teleport to the point under the view (up to 100 m).

The Mover pawn also toggles a debug flying mode with Z (keyboard only, through its AC_DebugTools). This is a raw key node in the Mover pawn's Event Graph, not an input action.

docs.title: Unused
docs.text: Asset Note IA_TwinStick_AimDirection Read by the Mover pawn's twin-stick mode but not mapped.

docs.title: By design
docs.text:
• Blueprint only. No C++ module. Everything can be changed in the editor; nothing needs compiling to run in the editor.
  • One animation skeleton. All animation, overlays, montages and Control Rigs are authored on the UEFN mannequin. Other characters are shown through runtime retargeting (about 0.16 ms per character).
  • Mover and Gameplay Cameras are experimental engine plugins in Unreal Engine 5.8. The Mover pawn and the camera system may need changes with future engine versions.
  • Pawn features differ slightly: slide, the physics-driven ragdoll, takedowns and shoves, and the debug tools are Mover-only; the simpler component ragdoll (AC_RagdollSystem) is CMC-only. Both use the same ragdoll and get-up keys.
  • Demo framework. GM_Sandbox, PC_Sandbox, the menus and the editor widgets are a demo setup, meant to be replaced or extended by your game.

docs.title: Systems
docs.text: System Limitation Cover No peek (lean out without aiming). Pose lowering expects UEFN bone names. Cover runs need a navmesh to avoid obstacles. Small corrections at sticky edge stops on the CMC pawn in multiplayer. First person TrueFirstPerson weapons can clip into walls and lag one frame. Split mode's body receives the hidden body's shadow. Only rifle, pistol, revolver and bow have first-person poses. Overlay Stances and item poses share one layer, so they cannot combine. Overlay changes are instant (no transition animation). Equipment Menus change global time dilation (the whole world slows down while one is open). Torch, binoculars, box and barrel have no first-person pose. Camera New styles or modes need chooser rows. Offsets apply in third person only; in first person the camera follows the head, so it lowers when crouching without an offset. Traversal Only the Traversable channel counts, and only obstacles a chooser row matches are traversed. Obstacles under 70 cm wide are jumped. Input Some actions have no gamepad binding: the overlay body menu, the camera style, debug flying, teleport, next pawn and next character. The Mover debug flying toggle is on Z (keyboard only).

docs.title: Known issues
docs.text:
These are open in the current version:

  • Unused animation: OverlaySystem/Transitions/Stand_Transition is kept in the plugin but nothing plays it.
  • Mover pawn hovers at spawn: a Mover pawn spawned above the floor (a PlayerStart's capsule is a little taller than the character's, so about 7 cm in the sample levels) stays at that height until its first move input. Mover's walking mode only snaps to the floor while the character moves. Place PlayerStarts so the capsule rests on the floor to avoid it.
  • Packaged log lines: loading CR_UEFN_Mannequin_FullBodyIK in a packaged build logs LogStreaming errors about its editor-only data (ControlRigEditorAsset). The rig is Epic's; the game loads and runs normally.
  • Bench interaction log line: the first interaction of each pawn logs "The State Tree asset is not set ... Cannot initialize". The engine's Run State Tree node registers the StateTree component before it assigns the asset; the interaction then starts normally. Harmless.

docs.title: Project settings
docs.text: A plugin carries content, not project configuration. These settings live in the project's Config/*.ini files. The template project has them all; a project that adds the GASPALS plugin needs to copy them. The copy-ready block is in Installation.

docs.title: Collision
docs.text: Project Settings > Engine > Collision. Stored in DefaultEngine.ini, section [/Script/Engine.CollisionProfile].

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
Slot Name Kind Default response Used for ECC_GameTraceChannel15 Traversable Trace Ignore Traversal finds obstacles to vault, hurdle and mantle with this channel. Level geometry that should be traversable blocks it. ECC_GameTraceChannel16 Mouse Trace Ignore Mouse click traces of the look-at example level (PC_LookAtPOI). The GASPALS systems do not trace it (the fixed-camera cursor aim uses Visibility). ECC_GameTraceChannel17 Obstacle Object Ignore Moving obstacles of the physics obstacle course in RagdollLevel; the Ragdoll profile blocks it. ECC_GameTraceChannel18 Cover Trace Block What counts as cover: every cover probe (wall search, sticky entry, cover height, aim edges, the cover target under the crosshair) traces it. Every collision profile answers it like Visibility; set an object to Ignore Cover to keep it from being cover.

GASPALS uses the last four slots so that projects whose own channels start at slot 1 can merge the settings without a clash.

Channels in Blueprints are stored by position

A Blueprint stores a trace channel as TraceTypeQueryN, where N counts the custom trace channels in slot order (Visibility and Camera are 1 and 2). In this project Traversable is TraceTypeQuery3, Mouse 4 and Cover 5; Obstacle is ObjectTypeQuery7. If your project already has custom channels, these numbers shift after the merge: open the pawn's components and pick the channels again by name in Traversable Trace Channel (AC_TraversalLogic) and Cover Trace Channel (AC_CoverSystem), and the obstacle types in Ragdoll Obstacle Object Types on the Mover pawn. Object types set on components with a Custom collision setup are also stored by slot.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
Profile Object type Notes TraversalObjectPreset WorldDynamic Blocks everything, including Traversable. Use it on meshes the character can vault, hurdle or mantle. The demo levels use the LevelBlock_Traversable Blueprint instead, which sets the same response on its mesh. ObstaclePreset Obstacle Moving obstacles of the obstacle course: ignores world, pawns and camera; blocks the Ragdoll profile. CharacterCapsule Pawn Capsule of the Mover pawn: ignores Visibility, Camera and Cover, so the camera, visibility and cover traces pass through characters. The CMC pawn's capsule uses a custom setup with the same responses. Ragdoll (edited) PhysicsBody The engine profile, edited to ignore Camera and Cover and block Obstacle. Engine profiles (edited) Pawn, Spectator, CharacterMesh, Trigger, InvisibleWall, InvisibleWallDynamic, NoCollision, WaterBodyCollision ignore Cover; OverlapAll and OverlapAllDynamic overlap it, the same as their Visibility response.

Custom collision and the Cover channel

Components with a Custom collision setup store their own responses, and a new channel takes its default response (Block). Triggers or volumes that ignore Visibility should ignore Cover too, or they block cover probes. The GASPALS content is already set up this way.

docs.title: Data-driven console variables
docs.text:
Project Settings > Engine > Data Driven CVars. Section [/Script/Engine.DataDrivenConsoleVariableSettings].

These are console variables declared by the project, which Blueprints read with Get Console Variable * Value and can react to when they change. GASPALS uses them for runtime switches (camera style, pawn class, character) and debug drawing. If they are missing, an orange on-screen warning at play start lists them; DDCvar.PawnClass and DDCvar.VisualOverride fall back to -1 (default pawn, no override), and the other reads return 0 or false, which changes behavior: for example DDCVar.NewGameplayCameraSystem.Enable false switches the pawns to the old spring-arm camera, and DDCVar.ThreadSafeAnimationUpdate.Enable false moves the animation update to the game thread.

The list, with what each one does, is in Console variables.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
[/Script/NavigationSystem.NavigationSystemV1]
bAllowClientSideNavigation=True

The cover run builds its path on the owning client. Without client-side navigation, clients get no path and run in a straight line. Levels also need a NavMeshBoundsVolume (with the navmesh built) for the cover run to path around obstacles.

docs.title: Motion matching
docs.text:
[/Script/PoseSearch.PoseSearchSettings]
AvailabilitiesBufferSize=230

Buffer size for the pose search availabilities, from the Game Animation Sample.

docs.title: Physics
docs.text:
[/Script/Engine.PhysicsSettings]
bSubstepping=True
MaxSubstepDeltaTime=0.016667
MaxSubsteps=16

Physics substepping keeps ragdolls and physical animation stable at low frame rates.

docs.title: Engine
docs.text:
[/Script/Engine.Engine]
NearClipPlane=1.000000

A 1 cm near clip plane. First person with aim down sights puts the rear sight a few centimeters from the camera; the default (10 cm) clips it.

docs.title: Console variables set at startup
docs.text:
[ConsoleVariables]
p.EnableCharacterAccelerationReplication=1
net.SubObjects.DefaultUseSubObjectReplicationList=1
fx.Niagara.ForceLastTickGroup=1
Variable Why p.EnableCharacterAccelerationReplication The CMC replicates the owner's acceleration to simulated proxies. Motion matching on remote CMC characters reads it, and the CMC cover movement relies on it. net.SubObjects.DefaultUseSubObjectReplicationList Replicated subobjects use the registered subobject list (Mover and Network Prediction). fx.Niagara.ForceLastTickGroup Niagara effects tick last, after the animation, so effects attached to bones follow the final pose.

docs.title: Rendering
docs.text:
The template's [/Script/Engine.RendererSettings] section matches the Game Animation Sample (Lumen, virtual shadow maps, Nanite, TSR...). Four lines matter for the characters:

Setting Why r.GPUSkin.Support16BitBoneIndex=True MetaHuman meshes have more than 256 bones per section. r.GPUSkin.UnlimitedBoneInfluences=True MetaHuman meshes use more than 8 influences per vertex. r.SkinCache.CompileShaders=True Skin cache shaders, used by MetaHuman deformers and grooms. r.SkinCache.DefaultBehavior=0 Skin cache off unless a mesh asks for it (inclusive mode).

docs.title: Network Prediction
docs.text:
DefaultNetworkPrediction.ini (whole file):

[/Script/NetworkPrediction.NetworkPredictionSettingsObject]
Settings=(PreferredTickingPolicy=Independent,ReplicatedManagerClassOverride=None,FixedTickFrameRate=60,bForceEngineFixTickForcePhysics=True,SimulatedProxyNetworkLOD=Interpolated,FixedTickInterpolationBufferedMS=100,IndependentTickInterpolationBufferedMS=100,IndependentTickInterpolationMaxBufferedMS=250,FixedTickInputSendCount=6,IndependentTickInputSendCount=6,MaximumRemoteInputFaultLimit=6)

The Mover pawn runs Network Prediction with independent ticking (each client simulates at its own frame rate) and interpolated simulated proxies. Without this file the engine defaults apply, which changes how remote Mover characters move.

docs.title: Gameplay tags
docs.text: DefaultGameplayTags.ini declares the tags the content uses: Foley.Event.* (footsteps, jumps, landings, ragdoll impacts), MotionMatching.* (database tags), SmartObject.ObjectType.* and StateTree.* (NPC and bench demos), a few Abilities.* and GameplayCue.* tags from the Game Animation Sample, and some redirects. Copy the file, or merge its +GameplayTagList lines into yours.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
[/Script/Engine.InputSettings]
DefaultPlayerInputClass=/Script/EnhancedInput.EnhancedPlayerInput
DefaultInputComponentClass=/Script/EnhancedInput.EnhancedInputComponent
DefaultTouchInterface=/GASPALS/Input/TIS_MobileControls.TIS_MobileControls

GASPALS uses Enhanced Input only (the engine default in 5.8). The touch interface is optional.

docs.title: Maps and modes
docs.text:
[/Script/EngineSettings.GameMapsSettings]
EditorStartupMap=/GASPALS/Levels/DefaultLevel.DefaultLevel
GameDefaultMap=/GASPALS/Levels/DefaultLevel.DefaultLevel

The editor and the game both start in DefaultLevel. There is no global default game mode: each GASPALS level sets its game mode in its World Settings (GM_Sandbox for DefaultLevel and NPCLevel, GM_Sandbox_Ragdoll for RagdollLevel, GM_LookAtPOI for the look-at example). Set your own maps here (Project Settings > Project > Maps & Modes).

docs.title: Packaging
docs.text:
DefaultGame.ini:

Setting Why +PrimaryAssetTypesToScan=(PrimaryAssetType="GameFeatureData", ...) Only for projects that enable the Game Features plugin: without the entry their cook fails (UAT exit code 25, unknown cook failure). Leave it out otherwise; without that plugin, every editor start reports that the GameFeatureData class can't be loaded. GASPALS itself doesn't need it. +MapsToCook=(FilePath="/GASPALS/Levels/DefaultLevel") The demo level is cooked. Replace with your levels.

Packaging also needs a C++ toolchain (Visual Studio 2022 on Windows): the engine plugins GASPALS enables are not on by default, so the packaging tool builds a game target for the project even though it has no code.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Start with the basics: are the project settings copied, and does the problem happen in the template's DefaultLevel? If it works there, compare your level, pawn or character with the sample.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix No GASPALS Content folder in the Content Browser Plugin content is hidden, or GASPALS is not enabled Enable Settings > Show Plugin Content in the Content Browser. If the folder is still missing, enable GASPALS in Edit > Plugins (or in the .uproject, see Installation) and restart. The camera is a plain spring arm; no shoulder, crouch or cover offsets DDCVar.NewGameplayCameraSystem.Enable missing or false Copy the data-driven console variables. Restart Play after changing it. An orange message lists missing console variables at play start The project does not declare those DDCvar.* data-driven console variables; the systems fall back to defaults (no visual override, the game mode's default pawn) Copy the console variables from Installation. Characters never change with M The level's game mode is not GM_Sandbox or a child Use GM_Sandbox or derive from it. Errors about missing gameplay tags, no foley sounds DefaultGameplayTags.ini not copied Copy it. Packaging fails with exit code 25 The project enables the Game Features plugin but scans no GameFeatureData asset type Add the entry from Installation. "Failed to load class /Script/GameFeatures.GameFeatureData" on every editor start A GameFeatureData scan entry without the Game Features plugin Remove the entry from Config/DefaultGame.ini, or enable Game Features if you use it. Packaging asks for a compiler The plugins GASPALS uses are not on by default Install Visual Studio 2022 with the game development workload. The packaged game closes at start; its log says "Unable to load plugin 'GASPALS'" and names a missing dependency GASPALS isn't enabled in the project's .uproject, so the package uses the stock game executable without GASPALS's engine plugins Enable GASPALS in the project (see Installation) and package again. Traversal, cover or the obstacle course stop working after merging the collision settings Your project has its own custom channels, so the channel positions the Blueprints store changed Pick the channels again by name: Traversable Trace Channel, Cover Trace Channel, Ragdoll Obstacle Object Types (see Project settings). The player has no controls; InputMappingContexts is empty on this pawn The pawn's Input Mapping Contexts map is empty Add IMC_Sandbox (or your context) in the pawn's class defaults.

docs.title: Locomotion and traversal
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Pressing jump at an obstacle only jumps It does not block the Traversable channel, Traversable Trace Channel points at another channel, or it is too narrow See Make objects traversable; check the setting on the pawn's AC_TraversalLogic. No slide The CMC pawn has none; on the Mover pawn, slides need sprint speed (over 380) and wait for the 0.75 s cooldown Sprint, then crouch. The character keeps strafing The CMC pawn starts with strafe on Toggle strafe (middle mouse), or change CharacterInputState > Wants To Strafe on the pawn. The Mover pawn suddenly flies Z is the Mover debug flying toggle Press Z again, or turn off Enable Debug Tools on the Mover pawn's AC_DebugTools component. Feet slide or float on a new character Retargeting Check the IK Retargeter's chains and retarget pose.

docs.title: Cover
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix No cover at all on your pawn Enable Cover was turned off on its component (it is on by default) Turn it on in the pawn's cover component. Cover never triggers on some walls The wall ignores the Cover channel Use a preset that blocks Visibility (they all block Cover), or set its Cover response to Block. Characters take cover on foliage or fences Those objects block Cover Set their Cover response to Ignore (Build a cover level). The cover button does nothing Enable Sticky Cover off, nothing within Sticky Cover Reach, first person with First Person Sticky Cover = Disabled (or SwitchToThirdPerson on a pawn whose Allowed Perspectives has no third person), or sprint held (sprinting leaves cover) Check the settings and the cover marker (it shows on valid cover). Cover run goes straight into obstacles No navmesh Add a NavMeshBoundsVolume and build paths. Cover run fails on clients only Client-side navigation is off bAllowClientSideNavigation=True (project settings). Mover and CMC behave differently in cover Their cover components are tuned separately Compare the component settings; the cover reference shows where the samples differ.

docs.title: Equipment and overlays
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Selecting a new item leaves the hands empty The slot has no row in CHT_Equipment, or its data asset has no Spawned Actor Add the chooser row; set Spawned Actor in the data asset. The item floats near the feet The attach socket is missing on the skeleton Add the overlay_* sockets to the character's Skeleton. The support hand does not reach the item No HandIK socket on the item mesh (or the socket named in the item's Hand IKSocket), or the pose's enable_handik_* curve is 0 Add the socket; set the curve in the pose's curve map. The item is not in the hands in first person Create First Person Copy is off in the item's data asset, or the pawn has no AC_FirstPersonSystem Turn Create First Person Copy on; keep AC_FirstPersonSystem on the pawn. Other players' arms snap when they aim up or down The overlay child's Aim Sweep Interp Speed Remote is 0 Set Remote to 10 on the child (keep Local at 0: interpolating the owner's arms makes the weapon lag and step). The Overlay Pose set on the pawn does not show An item is equipped at spawn; its pose wins Start with Selected Equipment Unequip, or pick the stance later. OverlayPoseLayers has no anim layer class for the selected OverlayPose (or OverlayBodyLayers) The enum value has no row in the map Add the row on AC_OverlaySystem (and on the pawn's component if it overrides the map).

docs.title: First person
docs.text:
The pawn's AC_FirstPersonSystem prints setup problems on screen, in orange, for the local player, for 10 seconds. Each message starts with GASPALS First Person (<body name>):, where the body is the pawn or the visible character. The fields named below are in the body's first-person setup (PDA_FirstPersonSetup): Default Setup on the pawn's AC_FirstPersonSystem, or First Person Setup on a retargeted character.

Message (abridged) Fix no first-person setup Set First Person Setup on your BP_RetargetedCharacter_Base child (duplicate DA_FirstPersonSetup_Manny), or implement BPI_FirstPersonCharacter (GetFirstPersonSetup) on your visual override. Until then the body mesh is reused in first person with the head hidden. no third-person Skeletal Mesh Component found On a character, implement BPI_VisualOverride (GetVisualBodyMesh) to return the body mesh; on a pawn, set Third Person Mesh Name on AC_FirstPersonSystem to the body component's name. no first-person mesh was generated Fill Full Meshes (or Arms Meshes and Body Meshes for FirstPersonOverlaySplit) in the body's setup. the first-person skeleton has no camera bone Add a virtual bone from root to head named VB Camera in the Skeleton editor, or set Camera Bone in the setup to your camera bone. the first-person skeleton has no head bone Set Head Bone in the setup to the skeleton's head bone. this skeleton is not the UEFN mannequin and its first-person setup has no Retargeter ... so TrueFirstPerson is used Set Retargeter in the setup to an IK Retargeter from the UEFN mannequin to this skeleton, or keep TrueFirstPerson for this character. FirstPersonOverlaySplit needs both ArmsMeshes and BodyMeshes Fill both Arms Meshes and Body Meshes in the setup. Symptom Cause Fix A character is in TrueFirstPerson although the pawn uses an overlay mode Its skeleton is not the UEFN mannequin and its setup has no Retargeter Set Retargeter in the character's first-person setup. The camera sees the inside of the head or the chest Eye offset Tune Eye Offset in the body's first-person setup ((0, 12, 0) for UE5 and MetaHuman heads). ADS sights do not line up Eye offset or the item's ADS socket Fix the eye offset first, then the socket. The rear sight is clipped Near clip plane NearClipPlane=1 in the project settings. The camera does not follow the body on a retargeted character CR_FirstPerson_BodyCamera not compiled after an edit Open and compile the Control Rig.

docs.title: Characters
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The character is a frame behind the pawn GetVisualBodyMesh does not return the body mesh, so it does not tick after the pawn mesh Override GetVisualBodyMesh in the character Blueprint to return its body component. The hands do not grip items on a retargeted character The hand IK curves do not reach the retargeted mesh Add a Curve Remap op (copy all source curves) to the IK Retargeter. MetaHuman clothing tears or stays in bind pose A follower with its own skeleton uses leader pose Leave its anim class empty and keep its post-process Anim Blueprint.

docs.title: Camera
docs.text:
AC_CameraSystem prints its setup warnings on screen, in orange, for the local player. Each starts with Camera System:.

Message or symptom Cause Fix CameraPerspective is not available ... Starting in the first available perspective The start view (Camera Perspective) is not in Allowed Perspectives, or it is FirstPerson on a pawn without AC_FirstPersonSystem Add it to Allowed Perspectives, or pick an allowed start view. FirstPerson is in AllowedPerspectives, but the pawn has no AC_FirstPersonSystem First person needs the first-person system on the pawn Add AC_FirstPersonSystem to the pawn, or remove FirstPerson from Allowed Perspectives. CameraPerspectiveDuringRagdoll is not available; the ragdoll keeps the current view The ragdoll view you picked is not in Allowed Perspectives Add it to the list, pick an allowed one, or turn Change Perspective During Ragdoll off. 1 does nothing Allowed Perspectives has one entry, or camera switching is off (during a ragdoll, unless Allow Camera Switch is on) Add perspectives to the list. See Camera. No crosshair Show Crosshair is off, or Crosshair Widget Class is empty Turn it on and set the widget class on the pawn's AC_CameraSystem.

docs.title: Ragdoll
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Takedown or shove does nothing The target must be a Mover character within 2 m in front of you, walking, with nothing in between; with aim held, the same keys are the debug shot and spawn Release aim and face the character from about 1.5 m. See Takedowns and shoves. The debug shot doesn't ragdoll a CMC character A standing CMC character's mesh has no collision, so the shot trace can't hit it Expected; shoot a Mover character. The ragdoll won't get up The character only gets up once the body rests on a floor; a press in mid-air does nothing Press X or Space again after landing. On your own pawn, implement RequestGetUp from BPI_RagdollSystem (Ragdoll).

docs.title: Multiplayer
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix A system works on the host but not for clients The component does not replicate Turn on Component Replicates on the pawn's component (see Networking). Remote Mover characters stutter Network Prediction settings missing Copy DefaultNetworkPrediction.ini. Remote CMC characters animate stiffly Acceleration not replicated p.EnableCharacterAccelerationReplication=1. Corrections during Mover play Something changed movement outside the input command Route movement changes through ProduceInput and transitions; np.PrintReconciles 1 lists corrections.

docs.title: Camera reference
docs.text:
The camera component on both pawns, and the camera director that picks the rigs.

How to read these tables

Settings are the values you tune: select the component in your pawn Blueprint (or open the asset) and look in the Details panel under the category shown. Runtime state is written by the system while it runs; read it, do not set it. Functions marked pure have no execution pins. The descriptions are the same as the Details panel tooltips. Default is the class default; where a sample pawn sets a different value on its component, the description says so ().

docs.title: Camera > Crosshair
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Show CrosshairbShowCrosshair Boolean true Show the crosshair dot (W_Crosshair) for the local player. When off, the dot is collapsed; aiming, cover targeting and the cover marker (bShowCoverMarker on the cover system) still work. Aim Trace DistanceAimTraceDistance Float 10000 Length of the crosshair aim ray in cm (GetCrosshairAim), also used by cover aim. Without a hit the aim point is the ray end. Default 10000 (100 m). Aim Trace ChannelAimTraceChannel ETraceTypeQuery Visibility Trace channel of the crosshair aim ray (GetCrosshairAim). Cover aim reads it too (AC_CoverSystem_Base.GetAimTraceSettings), so the crosshair and cover line-of-fire checks always agree. Default Visibility. Crosshair Widget ClassCrosshairWidgetClass UserWidget class W_Crosshair Crosshair widget created for the local player and kept on the aim point. Default W_Crosshair, a plain dot in its DefaultColor. Any widget works: the camera positions it, the widget picks its own look.

docs.title: Camera > Fixed Camera
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Fixed Camera Mouse Aim TypeFixedCameraMouseAimType E_FixedCameraMouseAimType MouseTraceWithPositionFallback Setting: how the character aims in the fixed cameras (top-down, side-scroller). MouseTraceWithPositionFallback: face the world point under the cursor, else the cursor's screen position. MouseScreenPosition: the cursor position relative to the screen center.

docs.title: Camera > General
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Camera StyleCameraStyle E_CameraStyle Style_2 Camera style. Cycled with the style input (2), or set through the DDCVar.CameraStyle console variable. Is Camera Right ShoulderbIsCameraRightShoulder Boolean false True when the third-person camera sits over the right shoulder. Toggled by the switch-shoulder input. Third Person Camera BoneThirdPersonCameraBone Name root Bone or socket of the visible character mesh the camera attaches to in every perspective but first person (third person, top-down, side-scroller). Default root. Enable Camera SystembEnableCameraSystem Boolean true Turns the camera system on or off (read at start, default only). Off: fixed third-person view with the default style, no perspective, style or shoulder input, no crosshair, no ragdoll perspective switch. The view itself (GameplayCamera, camera asset and director) stays.

docs.title: Camera > Perspective
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Camera PerspectiveCameraPerspective E_CameraPerspective ThirdPerson Active camera mode: third person, first person, or one of the two fixed cameras (top-down, side-scroller). Sent to the server on change. (replicated) Allowed PerspectivesAllowedPerspectives Array of E_CameraPerspective ThirdPerson, TopDown, SideScroller, FirstPerson Views this pawn offers, in perspective-key order. Default ThirdPerson, TopDown, SideScroller, FirstPerson (all). First-person only: FirstPerson. Third-person only: ThirdPerson (and remove AC_FirstPersonSystem from the pawn if you like). One entry = the perspective key does nothing. FirstPerson also needs AC_FirstPersonSystem on the pawn; first-person meshes are only built when FirstPerson is available.

docs.title: Camera > Ragdoll
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Allow Camera SwitchbAllowCameraSwitch Boolean false Setting: when true, the perspective and shoulder inputs work while ragdolling. Looking around is never blocked. Only used when bChangePerspectiveDuringRagdoll is on. Default false. Change Perspective During RagdollbChangePerspectiveDuringRagdoll Boolean true Setting: when true the camera switches to CameraPerspectiveDuringRagdoll while ragdolling and back afterwards. Camera Perspective During RagdollCameraPerspectiveDuringRagdoll E_CameraPerspective ThirdPerson Setting: perspective used while ragdolling. Only applies if bChangePerspectiveDuringRagdoll is true.

docs.title: Camera > Rigs
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Camera Offset RigsCameraOffsetRigs S_CameraOffsetRigs Offset rigs the camera director layers on the main rig: crouch, right shoulder, cover low, cover edges, first-person scale, and per movement mode (in air, sliding, traversing, ragdoll; needs bPassMovementModeToCamera). Clear an entry to turn that offset off. Read by CameraDirector_SandboxCharacter every frame. Pass Movement Mode to CamerabPassMovementModeToCamera Boolean true Pass the pawn's real movement mode to the camera director (S_CharacterPropertiesForCamera.MovementMode): the director then stacks the InAir, Sliding, Traversing and Ragdoll offset rigs, and chooser rows can match on the mode. Off = constant OnGround. The CMC pawn reports OnGround, InAir, Traversing and Ragdoll; Sliding only exists on the Mover pawn. Default true. Runtime state (4 variables) Variable Type Default Description Crosshair WidgetCrosshairWidget UserWidget ref Crosshair widget created on the local player's screen. Removed when the pawn is destroyed. Parent Mesh FPParentMeshFP SkeletalMeshComponent ref First-person lead mesh. In first person the camera attaches to the active body's Camera Bone (default VB Camera). Player ControllerPlayerController PlayerController ref Player controller of the owning pawn, used for crosshair and cursor aim. Camera ListenersCameraListeners Array of ActorComponent ref Components told about perspective changes (BPI_CameraSystemListener.OnCameraViewChanged); they register themselves through BPI_CameraSystem.RegisterCameraListener.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text: Function Inputs Outputs Description GetCrosshairAim (pure) AimOrigin (Vector), AimDirection (Vector), AimPoint (Vector), bAimHit (Boolean), AimPlanarDirection (Vector) Where the player aims, for the crosshair and cover targeting. Third/first person: the camera ray through the screen center. Top-down/side-scroller: the ray under the mouse cursor, or with a gamepad a point 3 m out along the stick aim. Returns the ray, the world point it hits (bAimHit) and a planar aim direction. GetFixedCameraAimRotation LookGamepad (Vector2D), LookMouse (Vector2D) AimRotation (Rotator) Updates and returns the aim rotation for the fixed cameras: from the gamepad stick when it moves, else from the mouse cursor. Also sets bCrosshairGamepadAim.Get Mouse Position In ViewportGet Mouse Hit PositionDifferent Mouse Position Setups between Top Down and Side Scroller UpdateCrosshair Local player only, called every tick. Shows the crosshair widget when bShowCrosshair is on and moves it to the current aim point (GetCrosshairAim), or collapses it when off. The widget decides how it looks; the camera never calls the cover system. NotifyCameraListeners Calls OnCameraViewChanged on every registered listener with the current first-person state. CanCyclePerspective (pure) bCanCycle (Boolean) Perspective key gate: camera control is allowed (not during a ragdoll that locks it) and another perspective is available. GetFirstAvailablePerspective (pure) Perspective (E_CameraPerspective) The first AllowedPerspectives entry that is available; ThirdPerson when none is. GetNextAvailablePerspective (pure) Perspective (E_CameraPerspective) The next available perspective after the current one in AllowedPerspectives order, wrapping; the current one when there is no other. OnRagdollEnded Called when the ragdoll ends. Restores camera control and the perspective saved before the ragdoll. OnRagdollStarted Called when the ragdoll starts. Applies the ragdoll camera control setting and optionally switches perspective. InitializeSystem ParentPawn (Pawn ref), ParentMesh (SkeletalMeshComponent ref), ParentMesh_FP (SkeletalMeshComponent ref), GameplayCamera (GameplayCameraComponent ref) Stores the pawn, mesh and camera references, validates the perspectives (an unavailable start perspective falls back), attaches the camera for the current perspective and caches the player controller.Needed for switching visual overrides during runtime UpdatePlayerController Keeps PlayerController current while the camera system is disabled (its Tick does nothing else then), so crosshair aim queries still have a controller. ValidatePerspectives Called by InitializeSystem. A start CameraPerspective that is not available becomes the first available one (the perspective listeners are told). On-screen warnings: FirstPerson listed without AC_FirstPersonSystem; on pawns with AC_RagdollSystem, an unavailable CameraPerspectiveDuringRagdoll.Ragdoll system of the owner: its component (CMC) or the pawn itself (Mover). GetFirstPersonCameraBone (pure) BoneName (Name) First-person camera socket of the active body: the camera bone of the pawn's first-person system (its active body's setup); VB Camera without one. IsPerspectiveAvailable (pure) Perspective (E_CameraPerspective) bAvailable (Boolean) True when Perspective is in AllowedPerspectives and, for FirstPerson, the pawn has an enabled AC_FirstPersonSystem. Read by the perspective key, the start and ragdoll perspectives, AC_FirstPersonSystem (builds first-person meshes only when FirstPerson is available) and cover (sticky cover's switch to third person). GetCameraCrosshairAim AimOrigin (Vector), AimDirection (Vector), AimPoint (Vector), bAimHit (Boolean), AimPlanarDirection (Vector) The crosshair aim ray (GetCrosshairAim). (BPI_CameraSystem) IsCameraRightShoulder bRightShoulder (Boolean) True when the third-person camera is on the right shoulder. (BPI_CameraSystem) IsFirstPersonView bFirstPerson (Boolean) True when the camera is in the FirstPerson perspective and the camera system is enabled. (BPI_CameraSystem) IsFirstPersonViewAllowed bAllowed (Boolean) True when FirstPerson is in AllowedPerspectives and the camera system is enabled (does not check the first-person system). (BPI_CameraSystem) IsFixedCameraView bFixed (Boolean) True in the fixed-camera perspectives (TopDown, SideScroller), where aiming uses the cursor plane. (BPI_CameraSystem) IsThirdPersonViewAvailable bAvailable (Boolean) True when the ThirdPerson perspective can be used (AllowedPerspectives). (BPI_CameraSystem) OnRagdollStateChanged bRagdolling (Boolean) bHandled (Boolean) Called by the ragdoll system on the owner components that implement it when the ragdoll starts or ends. (BPI_RagdollSystemListener) RegisterCameraListener Listener (ActorComponent ref) bHandled (Boolean) Adds a component implementing BPI_CameraSystemListener; the camera calls its OnCameraViewChanged after every perspective change (the camera finds them through this call instead of searching for them). (BPI_CameraSystem) RequestFirstPersonView bFirstPerson (Boolean) bHandled (Boolean) Switch to FirstPerson (true) or ThirdPerson (false). Returns false when the camera system is disabled. (BPI_CameraSystem)
