docs.title: Cover reference
docs.text:
The cover core component and its two movement adapters. Add AC_CoverSystem_Mover to a Mover pawn or AC_CoverSystem_CMC to a Character pawn: both inherit every setting of AC_CoverSystem_Base.

How to read these tables

Settings are the values you tune: select the component in your pawn Blueprint (or open the asset) and look in the Details panel under the category shown. Runtime state is written by the system while it runs; read it, do not set it. Functions marked pure have no execution pins. The descriptions are the same as the Details panel tooltips. Default is the class default; where a sample pawn sets a different value on its component, the description says so ().

docs.title: AC_CoverSystem_Base
docs.text: /GASPALS/Systems/CoverSystem/AC_CoverSystem_Base · parent ActorComponent · implements BPI_CoverSystem_C

docs.title: Cover > Aim
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Enable Cover AimbEnableCoverAim Boolean true Aim from cover: aiming (WantsToAim) in cover steps out to the best aim position instead of leaving cover. Off: aiming leaves cover as before. Cover Aim Keep StandingbCoverAimKeepStanding Boolean true Low cover: once standing to aim over the wall (Over), stay standing while the target can still be hit from there, and only crouch back into cover (InPlace) when the cover spot can hit it, never side-step to an edge. Off: the order cover, edge, stand is re-applied every time. Cover Aim Muzzle Height StandCoverAimMuzzleHeightStand Float 145 Aim from cover: muzzle height (cm above the capsule bottom) used for line-of-fire traces while standing. Adjust for very short or tall characters. Cover Aim Muzzle Height CrouchCoverAimMuzzleHeightCrouch Float 95 Aim from cover: muzzle height (cm above the capsule bottom) used for line-of-fire traces while crouched. Cover Aim Hit ToleranceCoverAimHitTolerance Float 30 Line of fire: a hit this close (cm) to the aim point still counts as a clear shot (the target itself). Cover Aim Cover DepthCoverAimCoverDepth Float 80 A hit of the aim ray within this depth (cm) behind the cover face counts as the cover in use (wall thickness): aiming at your own cover means aiming past it. Cover Aim Min Pose TimeCoverAimMinPoseTime Float 0.25 Aim from cover: minimum time (seconds) in an aim pose before it can change to another one. Cover Aim Blocked DelayCoverAimBlockedDelay Float 0.15 Seconds the current pose must be blocked before the pawn moves to a more exposed pose. Ignores short blocks such as the aim sweeping past an obstacle edge. Cover Aim Return DelayCoverAimReturnDelay Float 0.3 Seconds a safer pose must stay clearly valid before the pawn switches back to it. Cover Aim Return MarginCoverAimReturnMargin Float 10 Clearance (cm) a safer pose needs before the pawn switches back to it: a sphere of this radius must pass the first CoverAimReturnMarginReach of its shot. Stops flicker when a shot grazes the wall top or end. Cover Aim Return Margin ReachCoverAimReturnMarginReach Float 300 Length (cm) of the shot, from the muzzle, checked with the CoverAimReturnMargin sphere: the part near the cover where grazing matters. Beyond it a plain line test is used, so ground targets do not block the return. Cover Aim Edge ClearanceCoverAimEdgeClearance Float 20 Aim from cover: extra distance (cm) past the edge, beyond the capsule radius, when stepping out to aim around it. Cover Aim Slow RadiusCoverAimSlowRadius Float 30 Aim from cover: steering input slows down inside this distance (cm) to the target point. Cover Aim Arrive ToleranceCoverAimArriveTolerance Float 4 Aim from cover: the step-out and return stop within this distance (cm) along the wall. Cover Aim Return TimeoutCoverAimReturnTimeout Float 1 Aim from cover: after releasing aim, the lock ends after this time (seconds) even if the pawn could not get back to the return point.

docs.title: Cover > Camera
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Enable Cover Shoulder SwitchbEnableCoverShoulderSwitch Boolean true Cover shoulder switch: at a cover edge the third-person camera moves to the edge side (a temporary shoulder swap; the player's shoulder setting is untouched). When off, the camera stays on the player's shoulder in cover. Enable Cover Camera OffsetsbEnableCoverCameraOffsets Boolean true Cover camera offsets: in third person, the camera rises behind low cover and pushes past the cover edge the character is at (CameraRig_TP_Offset_CoverLow / CoverEdgeLeft / CoverEdgeRight). When off, the camera keeps its normal framing in cover.

docs.title: Cover > Collision
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Cover Trace ChannelCoverTraceChannel ETraceTypeQuery TraceTypeQuery5 Trace channel of every cover geometry probe: wall search and sticky entry (TraceWall), cover height, aim wall ends and steps, and the cover target under the crosshair. Default Cover, a channel that every collision profile answers like Visibility. Set objects to Ignore Cover to keep them from counting as cover. Pick Visibility if your project has no Cover channel.

docs.title: Cover > Corner Turn
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Corner Turn Hold TimeCornerTurnHoldTime Float 0.3 Sticky cover: how long (s) the player holds toward an edge before the character turns around the corner. Corner Turn AngleCornerTurnAngle Float 100 Sticky cover: largest corner angle (degrees between the two wall normals) the character turns around. Corner Turn Min WidthCornerTurnMinWidth Float 50 Sticky cover: how deep (cm) the wall around a corner must be to turn around it. Thinner ends (e.g. a thin wall) stop at the edge. Corner Remap Release TimeCornerRemapReleaseTime Float 0.15 Seconds the player must release or change the held direction before the corner input remap stops. Ignores single frames without input, so chained corner turns keep going.

docs.title: Cover > Cover Run
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Cover Run RangeCoverRunRange Float 1500 Cover run: how far (cm) the cover under the camera crosshair (or the wall straight ahead) can be for the cover button to run to it. Cover within StickyCoverReach is taken directly. Cover Run Max TimeCoverRunMaxTime Float 2 Cover run: extra seconds allowed on top of the path length at 5 m/s before the run is cancelled (e.g. when blocked on the way). Cover Run Path ToleranceCoverRunPathTolerance Float 60 Cover run: distance (cm) at which the next navmesh path point is followed. Cover Run Arrive DistanceCoverRunArriveDistance Float 80 Cover run: on the last path leg, distance (cm) from the stand point (60 cm in front of the wall) at which the character snaps into sticky cover. Cover Run Arrive SpeedCoverRunArriveSpeed Float 150 Speed (cm/s) the cover run slows down to when it reaches CoverRunArriveDistance and takes sticky cover, so the character does not slide along the wall. Cover Run Brake DecelCoverRunBrakeDecel Float 700 Deceleration (cm/s2) the cover run plans with on its last leg: the run input is scaled down so the speed reaches CoverRunArriveSpeed at CoverRunArriveDistance. Keep it below what the pawn can brake (Mover StoppingDeceleration, CMC braking). Cover Run Expected SpeedCoverRunExpectedSpeed Float 500 Speed (cm/s) used to plan a cover run: the run time limit is the path length divided by this. Default 500. Cover Run Stand OffsetCoverRunStandOffset Float 60 Distance (cm) from the target wall where a cover run stops, before sticky cover snaps the character in. Default 60. Cover Run Crouch Block TimeCoverRunCrouchBlockTime Float 0.4 Seconds after a cover run during which crouch requests are ignored (the run sprint would turn a crouch into a slide). Default 0.4. Cover Run Reentry DelayCoverRunReentryDelay Float 0.2 Minimum delay (s) before cover can be taken again after a cover run ends. Default 0.2.

docs.title: Cover > Debug
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Enable DebugbEnableDebug Boolean false Draw the cover traces for one frame each (wall, cover target, top height, and the aim traces), through GetCoverDebugDrawType. bCoverAimDebug prints the aim pose changes separately. Default false. Cover Aim DebugbCoverAimDebug Boolean false Debug: print every aim pose change on screen and to the log ("Cover aim: Old > New") and draw the aim target.

docs.title: Cover > Detection
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Cover Enter DistanceCoverEnterDistance Float 80 How far from the character (cm) a wall can be to take cover when moving into it. Cover Enter Input DotCoverEnterInputDot Float 0.3 How directly the move input must point into the wall to take cover (dot product: 0 = anything toward the wall, 1 = straight into it). Cover Hold DistanceCoverHoldDistance Float 50 Max distance (cm) between the character and the wall for cover to be kept. Must be larger than the wall distance the cover spring holds (the Wall Distance settings, GetCoverWallDistance). Cover Trace RadiusCoverTraceRadius Float 12 Radius (cm) of the sphere traces used to find cover. High Cover HeightHighCoverHeight Float 148 Walls at least this tall (cm above the character's feet) are high cover; lower walls are low cover (crouch behind them). Measured from the feet, so crouching doesn't change the answer. 148 = the standing probe of the sample characters. Edge Probe OffsetEdgeProbeOffset Float 45 Sideways distance (cm) of the edge, look-ahead and corner probes from the character. Max Cover Turn AngleMaxCoverTurnAngle Float 90 Largest change in wall direction (degrees) the character follows while moving along cover. Bends are followed automatically; corners (e.g. 90 on a table) only while the camera looks at the cover. Sharper changes release cover. Cover Probe PaddingCoverProbePadding Float 20 Extra length (cm) added to the wall probes beyond the wall gap, so a probe still reaches the wall when the character drifts a little. Internal tuning. Default 20. Cover Top Probe HeightCoverTopProbeHeight Float 300 Height (cm) above the cover point where the downward trace that measures the cover height starts; taller walls count as this high. Raise it for levels with very tall cover. Default 300.

docs.title: Cover > Exit
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Cover Exit Input DotCoverExitInputDot Float 0.7 How directly the move input must point away from the wall to start leaving cover (dot product; 0.7 = more than 45 degrees away). Lower values leave cover more easily but can drop cover while strafing around corners. Cover Exit DelayCoverExitDelay Float 0.15 Seconds the player must keep pushing away from the wall before cover is released. Sticky Exit Input DotStickyExitInputDot Float 0.9 How directly the input must point away from the wall to leave sticky cover (dot product; higher = more deliberate). Sticky Exit DelayStickyExitDelay Float 0.35 Seconds the player must keep pulling away before sticky cover is released.

docs.title: Cover > Facing
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Facing Stand AutoFacing_StandAuto E_CoverFacingStyle ShoulderToWall Facing while standing in automatic (soft) cover: FaceWall (towards the wall, offset by the shoulder angles), ShoulderToWall (along the wall, in the last move direction) or BackToWall. Facing Stand StickyFacing_StandSticky E_CoverFacingStyle BackToWall Facing while standing in sticky cover: FaceWall (towards the wall, offset by the shoulder angles), ShoulderToWall (along the wall, in the last move direction) or BackToWall. Facing Crouch AutoFacing_CrouchAuto E_CoverFacingStyle FaceWall Facing while crouched in automatic (soft) cover: FaceWall (towards the wall, offset by the shoulder angles), ShoulderToWall (along the wall, in the last move direction) or BackToWall. Facing Crouch StickyFacing_CrouchSticky E_CoverFacingStyle ShoulderToWall Facing while crouched in sticky cover: FaceWall (towards the wall, offset by the shoulder angles), ShoulderToWall (along the wall, in the last move direction) or BackToWall. Character Rotation Right ShoulderCharacterRotationRightShoulder Float 25 Yaw offset in degrees added to the wall-facing direction while the camera is on the right shoulder (FaceWall style, and the CMC mesh rotation). Character Rotation Left ShoulderCharacterRotationLeftShoulder Float -25 Yaw offset in degrees added to the wall-facing direction while the camera is on the left shoulder (FaceWall style, and the CMC mesh rotation).

docs.title: Cover > First Person
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description First Person Sticky CoverFirstPersonStickyCover E_CoverFirstPersonSticky SwitchToThirdPerson Sticky cover while the camera is in first person: SwitchToThirdPerson (camera goes to third person in sticky cover and back when it ends) or Disabled (no sticky cover in first person). First Person Auto CoverFirstPersonAutoCover E_CoverFirstPersonAuto MovementOnly Auto (soft) cover while the camera is in first person: MovementOnly (wall hug and edges, the body follows the camera) or Disabled (no auto cover in first person).

docs.title: Cover > General
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Enable CoverbEnableCover Boolean true Master switch. When off, the character never takes cover. Enable Auto CoverbEnableAutoCover Boolean true Auto cover: take cover by moving into a wall (or crouching in front of it). When off, only the cover button (sticky cover) takes cover. Needs bEnableCover. Enable Sticky CoverbEnableStickyCover Boolean true Sticky cover: the sticky cover button (IA_CoverSticky) snaps into cover under the crosshair and upgrades auto cover to sticky; the cover run button (IA_CoverRun, the same key by default) runs to far cover when bEnableCoverRun is on. When off, both buttons do nothing and the crosshair does not target cover. Needs bEnableCover. Enable Cover RunbEnableCoverRun Boolean true Cover run: holding the cover run button sprints to cover farther than StickyCoverReach (under the crosshair, up to CoverRunRange). When off, the cover button only takes cover within StickyCoverReach, and the cover marker only shows for cover the button can take from where the character stands (never while already in cover). Needs bEnableStickyCover. Engage RuleEngageRule E_CoverEngageRule Automatic When cover can be taken: Automatic (walk into a wall) or WhileCrouched (only while crouching). Move Into CoverbMoveIntoCover Boolean true When on, the character is moved against the wall when it takes cover (pulled to GetCoverWallDistance; the Mover through the Cover movement mode, the CMC through ShapeCoverMoveInput). When off, it is simply in cover when close enough and out of cover when too far, without being moved. Sticky cover always pulls in. Auto Crouch Low CoverbAutoCrouchLowCover Boolean true Crouch automatically behind low cover.

docs.title: Cover > Marker
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Show Cover MarkerbShowCoverMarker Boolean true Show the Division-style marker on the targeted cover (local player only). Off: nothing on screen shows the cover target (the crosshair stays a plain dot). Cover Marker Widget ClassCoverMarkerWidgetClass UserWidget class W_CoverMarker Widget shown by the cover marker on the targeted wall (a world-space widget component created on first use). Default W_CoverMarker. Cover Marker Draw SizeCoverMarkerDrawSize Vector2D (100, 12) Draw size of the cover marker widget in world units (X wide, Y high). Default (100, 12). Cover Marker Wall OffsetCoverMarkerWallOffset Float 3 Distance in cm between the cover marker and the wall face, so it does not clip into it. Default 3.

docs.title: Cover > Movement
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Wall Distance Stand AutoWallDistance_StandAuto Float 0 Gap (cm) between the capsule and the cover wall in soft (auto) cover while standing. 0 = touching the wall. The wall spring holds it, pushing out at up to WallPushSpeed and pulling in at up to MaxWallPullSpeed; tolerance WallPullDeadZone. Keep the gap plus the capsule radius under CoverHoldDistance. Wall Distance Stand StickyWallDistance_StandSticky Float 0 Gap (cm) between the capsule and the cover wall in sticky cover while standing. 0 = touching the wall. Pulled in at up to StickyPullSpeed, pushed out at up to WallPushSpeed. Wall Distance Crouch AutoWallDistance_CrouchAuto Float 0 Gap (cm) between the capsule and the cover wall in soft (auto) cover while crouched. 0 = touching the wall. Raise it if a crouched pose clips into the wall. Wall Distance Crouch StickyWallDistance_CrouchSticky Float 0 Gap (cm) between the capsule and the cover wall in sticky cover while crouched (sticky low cover crouches automatically). 0 = touching the wall. Wall Spring StrengthWallSpringStrength Float 8 Strength of the spring that holds the character at the wall distance: pull speed (cm/s) per cm of distance error. Wall Pull Dead ZoneWallPullDeadZone Float 2 Distance in cm around the wall distance (GetCoverWallDistance) where the wall spring does nothing, so the character settles instead of creeping back and forth (Mover Cover mode and CMC). Max Wall Pull SpeedMaxWallPullSpeed Float 200 Fastest speed (cm/s) at which soft cover pulls the character toward the wall (when bMoveIntoCover is on). Wall Push SpeedWallPushSpeed Float 100 Max speed (cm/s) the wall spring pushes the pawn away from the wall when it is closer than its WallDistance gap. 0 = never push (the pawn stays wherever it touched the wall). Sticky Pull SpeedStickyPullSpeed Float 600 Fastest speed (cm/s) at which sticky cover pulls the character toward the wall. Stop at EdgesbStopAtEdges Boolean false Soft cover also stops at the ends of the wall. Sticky cover always stops at edges. Cover Side Input ThresholdCoverSideInputThreshold Float 0.2 How much sideways stick input (0..1 along the wall) counts as moving along cover: edge stops and corner turns. Raise it for gamepads with a loose stick. Default 0.2.

docs.title: Cover > Pose
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Cover Lower Max StandCoverLower_MaxStand Float 10 Most the pelvis is lowered (cm) when standing in cover. The amount adapts to the cover height: just enough to keep the top of the capsule CoverLower_HeadClearance under the cover top; 0 behind cover taller than the pawn. Cover Lower Max CrouchCoverLower_MaxCrouch Float 15 Most the pelvis is lowered (cm) when crouched in cover (typically behind low cover). Adapts to the cover height like CoverLower_MaxStand. Cover Lower Head ClearanceCoverLower_HeadClearance Float 5 How far (cm) under the cover top the top of the capsule should be after lowering. Higher = ducks deeper (up to the max). Cover Lower Settle ToleranceCoverLower_SettleTolerance Float 10 How close to its cover distance (GetCoverWallDistance) the pawn must be before the pelvis lowers (cm). The sticky pull slides the pawn to the wall first; lowering during the slide bent the legs. Larger = lowers earlier.

docs.title: Cover > Sticky
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Sticky Cover ReachStickyCoverReach Float 250 How far (cm) along the camera direction the cover button searches for a wall; also how far sticky cover holds on to the wall while pulling the character in. Sticky Tap TimeStickyTapTime Float 0.25 Cover button: presses shorter than this (s) count as a tap. A tap in sticky cover leaves it; in cover, a cover run to other cover only starts once the button is held longer. Sticky Reentry CooldownStickyReentryCooldown Float 0.5 Seconds after leaving cover before sticky or auto cover can grab the character again. Default 0.5.

docs.title: Cover > Traversal
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Vault Facing DotVaultFacingDot Float 0.9 Space in cover while not facing the wall this closely (dot product; 0.9 = within about 25 degrees) first turns the character to face the wall, then starts the traversal. Vault Facing TimeoutVaultFacingTimeout Float 0.75 Longest time (seconds) the character spends turning toward the wall before the traversal is tried anyway. Runtime state (15 variables) Variable Type Default Description Cover Target AimedbCoverTargetAimed Boolean false Output: true when the last FindCoverTarget found a cover point along the crosshair aim (not only near the character). Drives the cover marker. Cover Run ActivebCoverRunActive Boolean false Output: true while the character sprints toward cover (cover run). Read by the character in ProduceInput to force the Sprint gait. Not meant to be set by hand. Cover Run Crouch BlockbCoverRunCrouchBlock Boolean false Output: true during a cover run and shortly after it (unless in cover). Read by the character in ProduceInput to block crouching, so the sprint never turns into a slide. Not meant to be set by hand. Cover Run Button HeldbCoverRunButtonHeld Boolean false True while the cover run button (IA_CoverRun) is held. Cover Run RequestedbCoverRunRequested Boolean false Set by RequestCoverRun; consumed by UpdateCoverRunPress on the next update. Cover Run Press TimerCoverRunPressTimer Float 0 Seconds the cover run button has been held (compared with StickyTapTime). Cover MarkerCoverMarker WidgetComponent ref Runtime: the world-space cover marker widget component, created on demand by GetCoverMarker. Parent PawnParentPawn Pawn ref Set by InitializeSystem: the pawn that owns this cover component. Internal; read by the CMC and Mover cover components. Camera State ProviderCameraStateProvider ActorComponent ref The owner's component implementing BPI_CameraSystem (cached), or None. Traversal State ProviderTraversalStateProvider ActorComponent ref The owner's component implementing BPI_TraversalSystem (cached), or None. Is Character in CoverbIsCharacterInCover Boolean false Output: true while the character is in cover. Read by the character for animation (Get_PropertiesForAnimation). Not meant to be set by hand. Sticky CoverbStickyCover Boolean false Internal state: true while in sticky cover. Cover StateCoverState S_MoverCustomInputs_Cover Internal state: the cover result sent to the Mover every frame (normal, point, in cover, low cover, edges). Cover NormalCoverNormal Vector (0, 0, 0) Output: current wall normal (flattened, pointing away from the wall). Not meant to be set by hand. Cover Press PendingbCoverPressPending Boolean false The current cover button press found a far run target and waits: held past StickyTapTime it runs there, released sooner it does the tap action.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text: Function Inputs Outputs Description CanCoverAimPoseHit (pure) Pose (E_CoverAimPose), AimPoint (Vector), Radius (Float) bCanHit (Boolean) True when the pose is available and its muzzle has a clear line of fire to AimPoint (TestCoverAimLineOfFire with Radius). CanStartCoverAim (pure) bCanStart (Boolean) True when an aim lock can start: aim is requested while in cover, outside a corner turn and a cover run. FindCoverAimPose (pure) AimDirection (Vector), AimPoint (Vector), Radius (Float) Pose (E_CoverAimPose) The least exposed pose that can hit AimPoint, in this order: InPlace (stay in cover), the edge the aim points to, the other edge, Over (stand up). None when no pose can. Radius > 0 asks for a clear margin around the shot. FindCoverAimWallEnd Side (Float) Distance (Float) Distance along the wall from the return point to the wall end on Side (-1 left, +1 right): a line trace 5 cm behind the wall face, from EdgeProbeOffset+40 past the pawn back toward it. No end within reach returns EdgeProbeOffset; an inside corner (the probe starts in the perpendicular wall) counts as no end. FinishCoverAim bForceCrouch (Boolean), CoverInputs (S_MoverCustomInputs_Cover) Cover outputs while the aim lock is active: writes CoverState from the frozen snapshot, with the stepped-out edge cleared so neither movement (Mover input or CMC shaping) stops at it. Low-cover force crouch stays on except when standing to aim over it. GetAimTraceSettings (pure) AimTraceChannel (ETraceTypeQuery), AimTraceDistance (Float) Aim trace channel and length for the cover line-of-fire checks: the values of the pawn's AC_CameraSystem (AimTraceChannel, AimTraceDistance), so cover aim and the crosshair always trace the same way. Without a camera system: Visibility and 10000 cm. GetCoverAimCameraState (pure) bLowCover (Boolean), EdgeSide (Float) bAimLowCover (Boolean), AimEdgeSide (Float) Camera hook (end of GetCoverCameraState): no low-cover camera offset while aiming, and the shoulder side taken from the stepped-out edge. GetCoverAimDirection (pure) AimDirection (Vector), AimPoint (Vector), AimForward (Vector), bFixedCamera (Boolean) Aim of the player camera: planar aim direction, crosshair point, 3D camera forward and whether the camera is fixed (top-down, side-scroller). AI pawns and pawns without a camera system use the base aim rotation. GetCoverAimEdgeDistance Side (Float) Distance (Float), bOpen (Boolean) Distance along the wall from the return point to the wall end on Side (FindCoverAimWallEnd) and whether the step out past it is open (IsCoverAimStepOpen). Impure so its two outputs come from one measurement; called once per side in StartCoverAim. GetCoverAimEdgeOrder (pure) AimDirection (Vector) First (E_CoverAimPose), Second (E_CoverAimPose) The edge the aim points toward (First) and the other edge (Second). GetCoverAimEdgeProbe (pure) Side (Float) Start (Vector), End (Vector) Probe line for the wall end on Side: starts EdgeProbeOffset + 40 past the return point along the wall, 5 cm behind the wall face, and runs back toward the pawn for twice EdgeProbeOffset + 40. GetCoverAimFacing (pure) Facing (Vector) AimFacing (Vector) Facing while aiming from cover: the planar aim direction. Returns Facing unchanged when not aiming from cover. GetCoverAimFallbackPose (pure) Pose (E_CoverAimPose) Pose used when no pose can hit the target as the aim starts: Over in low cover, InPlace in high cover. GetCoverAimMoveInput MoveInput (Vector) AimMoveInput (Vector) Move input while the aim lock is on (end of RemapCoverMoveInput): watches for exit input (UpdateCoverAimExitRequest) and steers along the wall to the pose location (GetCoverAimSteering). Passes MoveInput through when not locked. GetCoverAimMuzzle (pure) Pose (E_CoverAimPose) Muzzle (Vector) Muzzle stand-in for a pose: the pose location, CoverAimMuzzleHeightStand above the floor when standing (Over, or the aim started standing), CoverAimMuzzleHeightCrouch otherwise. GetCoverAimPoseLocation (pure) Pose (E_CoverAimPose) Location (Vector) Where the pawn stands for a pose: the return point, or for an edge pose the point just past the wall end (edge distance + capsule radius + CoverAimEdgeClearance). GetCoverAimPoseRank (pure) Pose (E_CoverAimPose) Rank (Integer) Exposure rank for comparing poses: InPlace 0, edges 1, Over 2, None 3. GetCoverAimPoseSide (pure) Pose (E_CoverAimPose) Side (Float) -1 for EdgeLeft, +1 for EdgeRight, 0 for the poses that stay at the cover spot. GetCoverAimStartPoint (pure) Point (Vector) Return point for a new aim: the previous one when the pawn is still within 2x CoverAimArriveTolerance of it (it came back from the last aim), so repeated aims do not creep along the wall; otherwise the current location. GetCoverAimStartPose (pure) BestPose (E_CoverAimPose) Pose (E_CoverAimPose) First pose of an aim: BestPose, or GetCoverAimFallbackPose when no pose can hit the target. GetCoverAimSteering (pure) MoveInput (Vector) Move input along the wall toward the current pose location: full speed beyond CoverAimSlowRadius, slowing to 25% near it, zero within CoverAimArriveTolerance. The cover movement keeps the wall distance. GetCoverAimTarget (pure) AimForward (Vector), AimPoint (Vector), bFixedCamera (Boolean) Target (Vector) The world point the aim pose has to hit. Camera-independent so the pose cannot feed back into it: a ray along AimForward from standing eye height above the cover spot. When that ray hits your own cover (IsOnCoverAimWall), the target is whatever lies behind it: aiming at your cover means aiming past it. Fixed cameras (top-down, side-scroller) use the cursor point (AimPoint). GetCoverAimWallAxes (pure) WallNormal (Vector), Tangent (Vector) Flattened wall normal and wall tangent of the frozen cover snapshot. Tangent = cross(Z, -normal): +Tangent points to the right edge, -Tangent to the left edge. IsCoverAimPoseAvailable (pure) Pose (E_CoverAimPose) bAvailable (Boolean) True when the cover allows the pose: InPlace always, Over in low cover only, an edge pose when the snapshot is at that edge and the step-out path is open. IsCoverAimPoseSafer (pure) Candidate (E_CoverAimPose), Current (E_CoverAimPose) bSafer (Boolean) True when Candidate is less exposed than Current. With bCoverAimKeepStanding, a pawn standing in Over only goes back to InPlace, never to an edge. IsCoverAimRequested (pure) bRequested (Boolean) True when the player wants to aim from cover: bEnableCoverAim is on, the aim input is held and the pawn may move. IsCoverAimReturned (pure) bReturned (Boolean) True when the pawn is back at its cover spot along the wall (within CoverAimArriveTolerance), and crouched again when the aim started crouched. IsCoverAimStepOpen (pure) Side (Float), Distance (Float) bOpen (Boolean) True when the pawn can step out past the wall end on Side: traces at capsule height and 40 cm lower along the wall, out to Distance + capsule diameter + CoverAimEdgeClearance. IsOnCoverAimWall (pure) Point (Vector) bOnCover (Boolean) True when Point lies on the cover being used: between 10 cm in front of the wall face and CoverAimCoverDepth behind it (face and top of the wall). SelectCoverAimPose AimDirection (Vector), AimPoint (Vector), DeltaSeconds (Float) Picks CoverAimPose for the target each frame while aiming: the first pose of the aim (GetCoverAimStartPose), then keeps a pose that can hit, going back to a safer one when clearly possible (UpdateCoverAimSaferPose), or leaves a blocked one (UpdateCoverAimBlockedPose). StartCoverAim Starts the aim lock: freezes the cover state (CoverAimSnapshot) and the return point, remembers the crouch state and measures both edges once. StopCoverAim Ends the aim lock and clears the pose. SwitchCoverAimPose NewPose (E_CoverAimPose) Changes the aim pose: sets CoverAimPose and restarts the pose timers (CoverAimPoseTimer, CoverAimSaferTimer). Every pose change goes through here. TestCoverAimLineOfFire (pure) Muzzle (Vector), AimPoint (Vector), Radius (Float) bClear (Boolean) True when Muzzle has a clear shot at AimPoint: nothing blocks the line, or the first hit is within CoverAimHitTolerance of the aim point. With Radius > 0 the first CoverAimReturnMarginReach of the shot must also clear a sphere of that radius. UpdateCoverAim DeltaSeconds (Float) bLocked (Boolean) Aim from cover, called from EvaluateCover every frame: starts the lock when aiming in cover (CanStartCoverAim, StartCoverAim); while locked stops when cover is lost, leaves cover on exit input, picks the pose while aiming (SelectCoverAimPose, target from GetCoverAimTarget) and walks back after release (UpdateCoverAimReturn). Returns whether the lock is on. UpdateCoverAimBlockedPose BestPose (E_CoverAimPose), DeltaSeconds (Float) The current pose cannot hit the target: count CoverAimBlockedTimer and switch to BestPose once the pose has been blocked for CoverAimBlockedDelay (and held CoverAimMinPoseTime). Short blocks, like the aim sweeping past an obstacle edge, are ignored. UpdateCoverAimExitRequest MoveInput (Vector) While aiming in cover, input away from the wall (CoverExitInputDot) requests leaving cover (bCoverAimExitRequested); UpdateCoverAim acts on it. UpdateCoverAimReturn DeltaSeconds (Float) Aim released: the pawn walks back to the return point (GetCoverAimMoveInput), and the lock ends once it is there (IsCoverAimReturned) or after CoverAimReturnTimeout. UpdateCoverAimSaferPose SaferPose (E_CoverAimPose), DeltaSeconds (Float) The current pose can hit the target: switch back to SaferPose once it has been safer (IsCoverAimPoseSafer, found with the CoverAimReturnMargin clearance) for CoverAimReturnDelay. IsCameraOnRightShoulder (pure) bIsCameraRightShoulder (Boolean) The camera shoulder through BPI_CameraSystem (right shoulder without a camera system). UpdateCornerTurn MoveInput (Vector), DeltaSeconds (Float) Sticky cover: turns the character around a wall corner once the player holds toward an edge for CornerTurnHoldTime and a side wall within CornerTurnAngle and CornerTurnMinWidth is found. FindCoverTarget bTargetFound (Boolean) Looks along the crosshair or camera ray, within cover run range, for cover to run to and stores the run target. Returns whether one was found. FindFarCoverRunTarget Location (Vector) bFar (Boolean) Looks for a cover-run target under the crosshair (FindCoverTarget) and returns true when one is found farther than StickyCoverReach and cover runs are enabled. IsCoverRunHoldDue (pure) bDue (Boolean) True when the cover run button has been held past StickyTapTime. ReleaseCoverRun Cover run button released (IA_CoverRun Completed or Canceled). RemapCoverMoveInput MoveInput (Vector) RemappedInput (Vector) Remaps the move input in sticky cover: corner turn remap, steering to the cover run target at a braking speed, then the aim steering. Returns the input for the movement code. RequestCoverRun Cover run button pressed (IA_CoverRun Started; the pawn calls it). Holding it past StickyTapTime runs to the targeted cover. Ignored when sticky cover is disabled or not allowed in this view. RunToCoverTarget Location (Vector) bStarted (Boolean) Starts a cover run to the far target under the crosshair, leaving the current cover when it starts. Returns whether the run started. StartCoverRun bRunStarted (Boolean) Starts a cover run to the found cover: builds a navmesh path (straight line without navmesh), sets the time limit and turns bCoverRunActive on. Returns whether it started; always false when bEnableCoverRun is off. UpdateCoverRun Location (Vector), DeltaSeconds (Float), bBlocked (Boolean) Per frame during a cover run: follows the path to the target cover, cancels on a new cover button press, on timeout or when cover is blocked (sprint, aim, traversal, movement mode, engage rule), and takes the cover on arrival. Releasing the button does not cancel it. UpdateCoverRunPress DeltaSeconds (Float) Run button press timer; a run press of its own (the sticky button is not held, so the two actions are on different keys) starts a fresh press and cancels a running cover run. GetCoverDebugDrawType (pure) DrawDebugType (EDrawDebugTrace) Debug draw mode for every cover trace: ForOneFrame when bEnableDebug is on (wall, cover target, top height, aim line of fire, aim target, wall end and step traces are drawn), else None. CanEnterSoftCover Location (Vector), Normal (Vector) bAllowed (Boolean) Pure: true when automatic cover can be taken at Location: the character is crouching or the wall reaches HighCoverHeight, and auto cover is allowed in this camera. EvaluateCover MoveInput (Vector), DeltaSeconds (Float) bForceCrouch (Boolean), CoverInputs (S_MoverCustomInputs_Cover) Per-frame cover evaluation on the owner: updates the cover button, crouch edge and aim lock, then corner turn and cover run, and enters, keeps or leaves cover. Returns force-crouch and the cover state for the movement code. FinishCover bKeep (Boolean), Point (Vector), Normal (Vector), MoveInput (Vector) bForceCrouch (Boolean), CoverInputs (S_MoverCustomInputs_Cover) Builds the cover state output for the frame. Keeping cover: probes the wall at the character and both sides to set the high-cover and edge flags. Otherwise returns the out-of-cover state. Also returns force-crouch for low cover. GetHighCoverProbeOffset (pure) Offset (Float) Height to add to the actor location for the high-cover probe: HighCoverHeight above the feet (capsule bottom), whatever the crouch state, so a wall between the crouched and standing probe heights no longer flips between low and high cover. ResolveCoverSurface Location (Vector), MoveInput (Vector) bHit (Boolean), Point (Vector), Normal (Vector) Re-traces the wall while in cover (center, leading side and camera-forward probes) and picks the cover point and normal to follow. Bends up to MaxCoverTurnAngle are followed. TraceWall Start (Vector), Direction (Vector), Distance (Float) bHit (Boolean), Point (Vector), Normal (Vector) Pure: sphere trace (CoverTraceRadius) from Start along Direction for Distance. Returns whether a wall was hit, the impact point and the flattened wall normal.Cover probes: ignore hits where the probe starts inside geometry (common near corners). UpdateCrouchEdge Tracks crouch changes: sets bWasCrouching and bJustCrouched (true for the frame crouching started). IsAutoCoverAllowed (pure) bAllowed (Boolean) False in first person when FirstPersonAutoCover is Disabled (no soft cover from walking into walls). IsFirstPersonCamera (pure) bFirstPerson (Boolean) True when the owner AC_CameraSystem is in FirstPerson (false without a camera system). IsStickyCoverAllowed (pure) bAllowed (Boolean) False in first person when FirstPersonStickyCover is Disabled, or when it is SwitchToThirdPerson but ThirdPerson is not an available perspective on the camera system (a first-person-only pawn). The cover button then does nothing. UpdateFirstPersonCoverCamera Sticky cover in first person: switch the camera to third person (FirstPersonStickyCover = SwitchToThirdPerson), and back to first person when sticky cover ends if we switched it. Owner only, called from EvaluateCover. UsesCoverFacing (pure) bCoverFacing (Boolean) False in first-person auto cover (MovementOnly): the body follows the camera instead of the cover facing. Sticky cover in first person switches to third person, so it keeps the cover facing. GetCoverMarker Marker (WidgetComponent ref) Returns the world-space cover marker (a Widget Component showing W_CoverMarker). Creates it on the pawn the first time it is needed: hidden, absolute transform, no collision, no shadow. IsCoverTargeted (pure) bTargeted (Boolean) True while the cover button would take the character to the cover under the crosshair (in reach, or a cover run target). Updated every frame by UpdateCoverFeedback for the local player. UpdateCoverFeedback Per-frame cover feedback for the locally controlled player: UpdateCoverTarget, then UpdateCoverMarker. Called from the cover component's own update (Mover tick, CMC UpdateCoverCMC); other pawns skip it. UpdateCoverMarker Shows the cover marker (CoverMarkerWidgetClass, created on first use) on the targeted wall, CoverMarkerWallOffset in front of it, while bCoverTargeted and bShowCoverMarker. UpdateCoverTarget Each frame out of a cover run: finds the cover under the crosshair (FindCoverTarget) and sets bCoverTargeted, which shows the cover marker when that cover can be taken (sticky within StickyCoverReach, or a cover run when enabled). GetCoverTopHeight Height (Float) Height (cm above the pawn floor) of the top of the cover wall in CoverState: one line trace down from 300 cm, 10 cm inside the wall. 300 when nothing is hit (the wall is at least that tall, or thinner than 10 cm). IsSettledInCover (pure) CoverPoint (Vector), CoverNormal (Vector), bCrouched (Boolean), bSticky (Boolean) bSettled (Boolean) True when the owner is within CoverLower_SettleTolerance of its cover distance from the wall (along the cover normal). False before the component knows its pawn. GetCoverLowerAmount returns 0 until then. GetCameraStateProvider (pure) ReturnValue (ActorComponent ref) The cached BPI_CameraSystem component of the owner, or None. GetTraversalStateProvider (pure) ReturnValue (ActorComponent ref) The cached BPI_TraversalSystem component of the owner, or None. InitializeSystem ParentPawn (Pawn ref) Stores the owning pawn. Called once by the pawn; the Mover and CMC components extend it. GetCoverCameraState (pure) bLowCoverCamera (Boolean), EdgeSide (Float), ShoulderSide (Float) Cover camera state for the camera director (local player). bLowCoverCamera: in low cover. EdgeSide: -1 / +1 when a cover edge is within reach on the left / right of the screen (both edges: the side last moved to), 0 otherwise. bLowCoverCamera and EdgeSide pick the offset rigs and are off when bEnableCoverCameraOffsets is off; ShoulderSide is the same side for the shoulder swap and is 0 when bEnableCoverShoulderSwitch is off. GetCoverFacingDirection (pure) Direction (Vector) Pawn hook: the direction the character visibly faces (Mover: actor forward; CMC: the mesh, which the CMC cover rotates). Used to wait for the turn to the wall before a vault. GetCoverLowerAmount bCrouched (Boolean) Lower (Float) How far (cm) CR_Humanoid_CoverLower lowers the pelvis in cover: enough to bring the top of the capsule CoverLower_HeadClearance under the cover top (GetCoverTopHeight), capped by CoverLower_MaxStand / CoverLower_MaxCrouch. 0 out of cover and when standing behind low cover (aiming over it). Called by the character ABPs (Update_CoverLower) on every machine.No lowering until settled at the wall (the sticky pull slides the pawn there first). GetCoverOrientationIntent CurrentIntent (Vector) bInCover (Boolean), Intent (Vector) Facing hook for the movement code: in cover returns the facing from the Facing settings (toward the wall, along it or back to it), the aim direction when aiming, or the wall while a vault turn is pending. Out of cover it returns CurrentIntent.First-person auto cover: UsesCoverFacing is false, so there is no cover facing (the body follows the camera) and Intent falls back to CurrentIntent.Aim from cover: face the aim direction. GetCoverWallDistance (pure) bCrouched (Boolean), bSticky (Boolean) Distance (Float) Distance (cm) from the cover wall plane to the pawn center that the wall spring holds: the WallDistance_{Stand,Crouch}{Auto,Sticky} gap picked by crouch and sticky state, plus the pawn capsule radius. Read by the Mover cover mode (AdjustDesiredMove) and the CMC adapter (ShapeCoverMoveInput). IsCoverAiming (pure) ReturnValue (Boolean) True while aiming from cover (CoverAimPose is not None). Local owner only; not replicated. IsCoverCrouchBlocked (pure) ReturnValue (Boolean) Crouch is blocked: during a cover run (and its grace time), or while standing up to aim over low cover. Pawns use it for their crouch input. IsCoverCrouching (pure) bCrouching (Boolean) Pawn hook: true while the owning pawn is crouched. Override in the pawn-specific cover component (Mover / CMC). IsCoverMovementAllowed (pure) bAllowed (Boolean) Pawn hook: true while the pawn moves in a mode where cover is allowed (on the ground or already in cover). Override in the pawn-specific cover component (Mover / CMC). IsTraversalActive (pure) DoingTraversalAction (Boolean) True while a traversal action plays (BPI_TraversalSystem; false without a traversal system). DoCoverTapAction Location (Vector), bRelease (Boolean) The tap action, sticky first: soft cover becomes sticky; sticky cover exits (on release only); out of cover takes sticky cover nearby, else (on release) runs to the far target. EnterStickyCover Point (Vector), Normal (Vector) Starts sticky cover on the wall at Point and Normal: ends any cover run, sets bStickyCover, resets the exit timer and writes the cover state. ExitCover Leaves sticky cover: clears bStickyCover and the cover state and starts the re-entry cooldown (StickyReentryCooldown). HandleStickyToggle Location (Vector), DeltaSeconds (Float) Per frame on the owner: counts the cover button hold time and applies toggle requests (enter, upgrade to sticky), then searches for a cover target while held and starts a cover run or snaps to cover under the crosshair. IsCoverHoldDue (pure) bDue (Boolean) True when the cover run button or the sticky cover button has been held past StickyTapTime (the hold actions of UpdateCoverHold). ReleaseStickyCover Cover button released: clears bCoverButtonHeld (a running cover run continues) and flags the release for HandleStickyToggle. RequestStickyCover Cover button pressed: requests a sticky cover toggle when sticky cover is enabled and allowed in this camera, and marks the button as held. TakeStickyCover Location (Vector) bTaken (Boolean) Out of cover: takes sticky cover on the wall in front (camera forward, within StickyCoverReach), else on the targeted cover when it is within StickyCoverReach. Returns whether cover was taken. UpdateCoverHold Location (Vector) Cover button held past StickyTapTime: runs to the far target first; without one, takes sticky cover when out of cover (retried every frame while held). UpdateCoverPress Location (Vector) Cover button press: cancels a running cover run; with a far run target the press waits for hold or tap (bCoverPressPending); otherwise the tap action runs at once. UpdateCoverRelease Location (Vector) Cover button release: a quick release of a waiting press does the tap action (sticky first); otherwise a quick unused tap in sticky cover exits it. RequestCoverVault bDeferred (Boolean) Jump pressed in cover: when the character does not face the wall closely enough (VaultFacingDot) it starts turning to the wall first and returns true. Returns false when the vault can start directly. UpdateCoverVault DeltaSeconds (Float) Per frame while a vault turn is pending: counts the turn time and calls OnCoverVaultReady once the character faces the wall or VaultFacingTimeout passes. Cancels when cover is lost. GetCoverCameraContext bLowCoverCamera (Boolean), EdgeSide (Float), ShoulderSide (Float) Cover camera state for the camera director (GetCoverCameraState). (BPI_CoverSystem)

docs.title: Functions
docs.text: Function Inputs Outputs Description ApplyRemoteCoverState CMC: non-owners. Copies the replicated cover state, facing intent and cover run flags into the runtime variables used by animation, gait and facing. SendCoverState DeltaSeconds (Float) CMC: owner only. Sends the cover state, facing intent and cover run flags to the server every 0.05 s through ServerUpdateCover (unreliable). ShapeCoverMoveInput MoveInput (Vector) ShapedInput (Vector) CMC: owner-side wall hug. Projects the move input along the wall, stops at edges (sticky cover or StopAtEdges) and adds the spring pull toward GetCoverWallDistance, like BP_MovementMode_Cover does for the Mover. docs.text: Function Inputs Outputs Description CreateItemFirstPersonCopies Item (Actor ref) Copies (Array of PrimitiveComponent ref) Creates first-person copies of every static and skeletal mesh of Item (once; a second call returns the same copies) on the item actor itself (no collision, owner only, FirstPerson primitive type) and swaps them with the camera. Returns the copies, empty when first person is off or not allowed. (BPI_FirstPersonSystem) GetFirstPersonCameraBoneName BoneName (Name) The bone the camera follows in first person. (BPI_CameraSystemListener) RemoveItemFirstPersonCopies Item (Actor ref) bHandled (Boolean) Destroys the first-person copies of Item and forgets them. Call it before destroying the item. Returns the item's copies; empty when first person is off or not allowed. Returns None for other primitive types. The lead runs the first-person pipeline, followers copy its pose. DestroyFirstPersonMeshes Destroys the generated first-person meshes of the active body and forgets them, the third- and first-person mesh and the cached setup. FindThirdPersonMesh Mesh (SkeletalMeshComponent ref) The active body's mesh: BPI_VisualOverride's GetVisualBodyMesh for a visual override, else the component named ThirdPersonMeshName, else the first skeletal mesh that is not a generated first-person mesh. GetVisualMeshes ThirdPerson (SkeletalMeshComponent ref), FirstPerson (SkeletalMeshComponent ref) Returns the third-person and the lead first-person mesh. InitializePrimitives Sorts the active body's primitives into the first- and third-person lists: its third-person mesh and the meshes attached under it are third person; generated first-person meshes go to the first-person list. The held item's meshes and copies (CreateItemCopies) are added, after dropping entries of destroyed items.Sorts the owner's primitives into the first- and third-person lists. On a character (the pawn, or a visual override child actor) the third-person mesh and the meshes attached under it are third person. Other owners (equipment) get a first-person copy of each of their meshes once. Generated first-person meshes and copies go to the first-person list. IsGeneratedFirstPersonMesh (pure) Component (PrimitiveComponent ref) bIsGenerated (Boolean) True when Component is one of the first-person meshes this component generated (GeneratedFirstPersonMeshes). InitializePrimitives uses it so generated meshes are never copied again for first person. IsThirdPersonPrimitive Component (PrimitiveComponent ref), ThirdPersonMesh (SkeletalMeshComponent ref) bThirdPerson (Boolean) True when Component is part of the third-person character: the third-person mesh itself, or a mesh component attached under it. Generated first-person meshes, first-person copies and the connected logic mesh are never third person. No component tags needed. ReleaseGeneratedComponent Component (PrimitiveComponent ref) Destroys a component this system generated (a first-person mesh or an item copy). Unreal lets only the owning actor or the component itself destroy a component, so the generated classes (AC_FirstPersonSkeletalMesh, AC_FirstPersonStaticMesh) destroy themselves through ReleaseFirstPersonMesh. Any other component falls back to Destroy Component. SetActiveBody Body (Actor ref), LogicMesh (SkeletalMeshComponent ref) Makes Body (the pawn or its visual override) the first-person body. When the body changes, or its meshes are gone, destroys the previous body's generated meshes and builds Body's from its setup, on Body's actor. Always connects LogicMesh (the pawn's SkeletalMesh_FP). Called by the pawn's UpdateFirstPersonVisuals. SetupFirstPersonCopy Source (PrimitiveComponent ref), Copy (PrimitiveComponent ref) Turn Copy into the first-person copy of Source: attached to Source, same materials, visible to the owner only (hidden until first person) and a FirstPerson primitive. GetCameraStateProvider (pure) ReturnValue (ActorComponent ref) The owning pawn's component implementing BPI_CameraSystem, or None. GetActiveSetup (pure) Setup (PDA_FirstPersonSetup ref) Setup of the active body, cached in CachedSetup. Never None: a body without a setup gets a default PDA_FirstPersonSetup (empty mesh lists, so its body mesh is reused with the head hidden). GetEyeOffsetFor (pure) Actor (Actor ref) EyeOffset (Vector) Eye offset of an actor's own setup (zero without one), for the first-person Anim Blueprint of that actor's mesh. GetRetargeterFor (pure) Actor (Actor ref) Retargeter (IKRetargeter ref) Retargeter of an actor's own setup. The first-person Anim Blueprint asks it for its mesh's owner, so the pawn's logic mesh keeps the UEFN values while an override's lead gets the override's. GetSetupFor Actor (Actor ref) Setup (PDA_FirstPersonSetup ref) First-person setup of a body: DefaultSetup for the pawn, else the actor's BPI_FirstPersonCharacter setup (None when it has none). RegisterWithCamera bRegistered (Boolean) Registers this component as a camera listener (BPI_CameraSystem.RegisterCameraListener). ValidateSetup Prints orange on-screen warnings for the local pawn when the active body's setup is incomplete: no setup, no body or first-person mesh, no camera or head bone, a missing retargeter (TrueFirstPerson is used then), or Split without arms and body meshes. WarnSetup bShow (Boolean), Message (String) Orange on-screen and log warning for 10 s, prefixed with the body's name, when bShow. GetBodyActor (pure) BodyActor (Actor ref) The actor whose body is shown in first person: the active visual override set by SetActiveBody, else this component's owner (the pawn). GetFirstPersonCameraBone (pure) BoneName (Name) The active setup's CameraBone, or VB Camera when it is empty. GetFirstPersonHeadBone (pure) BoneName (Name) The active setup's HeadBone, or head when it is empty. GetRetargetSetup Retargeter (IKRetargeter ref), LogicMesh (SkeletalMeshComponent ref) Returns the active setup's Retargeter and the logic mesh (FirstPersonLogicMesh). IsCameraInFirstPerson (pure) bFirstPerson (Boolean) True when the camera reports the FirstPerson view (false without a camera system). IsFirstPersonAvailable (pure) bAvailable (Boolean) True when bEnableFirstPerson is on and the pawn's camera system allows FirstPerson (AllowedPerspectives); true when there is no camera system. BuildFirstPersonMeshes, item copies and BeginPlay do nothing when it is false. IsOnPawn (pure) bOnPawn (Boolean) True when this component's owner is the pawn. Only the pawn's component does anything: a copy left on a character or an item stays inert (the pawn's builds their meshes and copies). UsesFirstPersonScale bUsesScale (Boolean) True only in FirstPersonOverlaySplit, the one mode that stacks the first-person scale camera rig. UsesSplitMeshes (pure) bSplit (Boolean) Effective FirstPersonOverlaySplit: Split mode, not TrueFirstPerson, and the setup has ArmsMeshes. UsesTrueFirstPerson (pure) bTrueFirstPerson (Boolean) Effective TrueFirstPerson: FirstPersonMode is TrueFirstPerson, or the body is not on the logic mesh's skeleton and its setup has no Retargeter (the overlay poses could not be retargeted to it).

docs.text: Function Inputs Outputs Description Get_FirstPersonBob (pure) Profile (PDA_FirstPersonMotion ref) Position (Vector), Rotation (Vector) Bob target from the bob shape curves at the current phase, scaled by the speed curve; zero in the air. Get_FirstPersonBreathing (pure) Profile (PDA_FirstPersonMotion ref) Position (Vector), Rotation (Vector) Breathing target: slow vertical motion and pitch. Get_FirstPersonLookSway (pure) Profile (PDA_FirstPersonMotion ref) Position (Vector), Rotation (Vector) Look sway target: lag opposite to the view turn rate (through the look response curve), roll from yaw, clamped. Get_FirstPersonMoveSway (pure) Profile (PDA_FirstPersonMotion ref) Position (Vector), Rotation (Vector) Move sway target: roll and side shift into strafes, pull back when moving forward, clamped. Update_FirstPersonMotion Computes the motion rig inputs: sums look sway, move sway, bob and breathing from the active profile, applies the ADS, crouch, intensity and disable_fp_motion scales, and sets the spring settings and pivot. Update_FirstPersonMotionInputs Reads what the motion needs this frame: profile, look rates and velocity, in air / crouched, breathing time, aim alpha, bob and kicks, and the disable_fp_motion curve. Update_FirstPersonMotionKicks Bob phase (advanced by ground distance) and the one-frame jump and landing kicks from the active profile. Update_FirstPersonMotionLook Look rates (degrees per second) from the aim rotation change, and the pawn velocity in the view yaw frame. Update_FirstPersonMotionProfile Active motion profile: the equipped item's FirstPersonMotionProfile, else the pawn's (AC_FirstPersonSystem), and the motion intensity. GetEquipmentStateProvider ReturnValue (ActorComponent ref) The cached BPI_EquipmentSystem component of the owning pawn (looked up once), or None. GetFirstPersonOwner (pure) Owner (Actor ref) Where the first-person component is looked up: ParentPawn when it is set, else the owning actor (editor previews have no pawn). Update_ADSSettings Per-weapon ADS settings from the equipped item (PDA_Equipment ADSEnterSpeed, ADSExitSpeed, ADSHandOffset) for CR_FirstPerson_ADS; keeps the last values when nothing is equipped. Update_EquipmentHandTargets Game-thread copy of the held item's hand IK / ADS targets, handedness and overlay flag into the variables the anim graph reads. Update_FirstPersonMode Game thread: copies the pawn's AC_FirstPersonSystem settings (one mode for every body) and this mesh's eye offset, sets bTrueFirstPerson and bFirstPersonRunADS and computes the ADS and hand IK weights. Update_PropertiesFromCharacter Game thread: reads the pawn animation properties and the retarget setup (retargeter, logic mesh, bRetargetOverlay, bLogicOnly). Update_Values Thread-safe: sets bDisableOverlay, the enable_cr_fp_* and hand IK curve values, ControllerPitch and the aim offset and head pitch inputs.

docs.title: Pawns and Anim Blueprints reference
docs.text:
The two sample pawns, their character Anim Blueprints, the visual override manager, the debug tools component of the Mover pawn and the smart object (bench) interaction component.

How to read these tables

Settings are the values you tune: select the component in your pawn Blueprint (or open the asset) and look in the Details panel under the category shown. Runtime state is written by the system while it runs; read it, do not set it. Functions marked pure have no execution pins. The descriptions are the same as the Details panel tooltips. Default is the class default; where a sample pawn sets a different value on its component, the description says so ().

This function updates the warp targets in the component using the ledge locations. docs.title: Systems
docs.text:
Each system lives in its own folder under /GASPALS/Systems and is a component on the pawn. They are independent: a pawn uses the ones it needs. Every page follows the same order: what the system does, how it works, configuration, Blueprint API, networking and limitations. The full settings of each are in the reference.

  • Camera

    Gameplay Cameras with a camera director: four perspectives, styles, crouch and cover offsets, crosshair.

  • Cover

    Soft and sticky cover, cover run, corner turns, vault, aim from cover, pose lowering.

  • Equipment

    Data-driven items with overlay poses, attach sockets and hand IK.

  • First person

    Full-body first person built at runtime, three modes, aim down sights.

  • Overlay

    ALS-style overlay poses and body styles blended by curves.

  • Ragdoll and interactions

    Ragdoll on both pawns, physical animation, get-ups, takedowns and shoves.

  • Debug tools

    Demo shot into ragdoll, spawn or rotate characters, teleport and fly on the Mover pawn.

  • Traversal

    Vault, hurdle and mantle with ledge detection and motion warping.

  • Movement

    Gaits, rotation modes, speeds, Mover modes and transitions, slide.

docs.title: Camera system
docs.text:
The camera is built on Unreal's Gameplay Cameras. A Blueprint camera director picks camera rigs every frame from the character's state, and the component AC_CameraSystem handles the perspective, attaches the camera to the right mesh, and draws the crosshair.

Folder /GASPALS/Systems/CameraSystem Component AC_CameraSystem (on both pawns) Camera asset CameraAsset_SandboxCharacter (the pawns' Gameplay Camera component uses it) Director CameraDirector_SandboxCharacter (Blueprint camera director) Rigs Rigs/ (chooser tables CHT_CameraRig* and camera rigs, one subfolder per perspective) Data Data/ (enums E_CameraPerspective, E_CameraStyle, E_CameraMode, E_CameraSide, E_FixedCameraMouseAimType; struct S_CameraOffsetRigs) Widget W_Crosshair Camera shake CameraShake_Basic (played by the takedown montages' camera shake notify) Input IA_Camera_Perspective 1 / gamepad View, IA_Camera_Style 2, IA_Camera_SwitchShoulder Alt / R3 Settings Camera reference

docs.title: Perspectives
docs.text:
Perspective Camera Attached to ThirdPerson (default) Over-the-shoulder camera with collision push and damping. The visible mesh's Third Person Camera Bone (root) TopDown Fixed-angle camera above the character; the character aims at the mouse cursor or with the right stick. The visible mesh's Third Person Camera Bone (root) SideScroller Fixed side view; aims like top-down. The visible mesh's Third Person Camera Bone (root) FirstPerson Eye camera on the first-person mesh. See First person. The first-person lead mesh's camera bone (Camera Bone in each body's first-person setup, default the VB Camera virtual bone)

1 cycles through Allowed Perspectives in their order. By default: third person, top-down, side-scroller, first person, back to third person. Each switch prints the new perspective on screen. The visible mesh is the retargeted character's when one is active, so the camera follows it.

docs.title: Choosing the perspectives
docs.text:
Allowed Perspectives lists the views players can use. Set it on the AC_CameraSystem component of each pawn you use. Common setups:

Game Allowed Perspectives Result First person only FirstPerson Starts in first person; 1 does nothing. Third person only ThirdPerson No first-person meshes are built; 1 does nothing. You can also delete AC_FirstPersonSystem from the pawn. Third and first person ThirdPerson, FirstPerson 1 toggles between them.

If Camera Perspective (the start view) is not in the list, the camera starts in the first allowed one and shows an on-screen warning. FirstPerson only counts as available when the pawn has an enabled AC_FirstPersonSystem; when it is listed without one, a warning says so and first person is skipped. With only first person allowed, cover's First Person Sticky Cover setting SwitchToThirdPerson acts like Disabled (Cover).

The ragdoll view (Camera Perspective During Ragdoll, default ThirdPerson) is only used when it is allowed; otherwise the ragdoll keeps the current view. With a first-person-only list that happens silently while the ragdoll view is still at its ThirdPerson default, so restricting the list needs no other change. If you picked another ragdoll view that is not in the list, a warning says so.

docs.title: Styles
docs.text:
The style picks a variant per perspective. 2 cycles it (Style_2, Style_3, Style_4, Style_1, then back) and prints the new style on screen; the console variable DDCvar.CameraStyle (0 to 3) sets it too.

Style Third person Top-down / side-scroller First person Style_1 Close CameraRig_TD_1 / CameraRig_SS_1 Same rig in every style Style_2 (default) Medium _2 Style_3 Far _3 Style_4 Debug view (CameraRig_DebugView, no offset rigs) _4

docs.title: How the rig is chosen
docs.text:
Every frame the director:

  1. Reads the pawn's Get_PropertiesForCamera: perspective, style, mode (Free, Strafe or Aim, from the pawn's rotation mode and aim input; a target lock gives Strafe or Aim), shoulder side, stance and movement mode.
  2. Evaluates the chooser table CHT_CameraRig, which branches by perspective into CHT_CameraRigs_ThirdPerson, _FirstPerson, _TopDown or _SideScroller. Third person picks by style and mode: nine rigs CameraRig_TP_<Close|Medium|Far>_<Freecam|Strafe|Aim>; the Aim rigs blend in smoothly. The third-person fallback is CameraRig_TP_Medium_Freecam. First person always uses CameraRig_FP_Base.
  3. Activates the result, plus the First Person Scale Rig in first person when the pawn's first-person system uses the FirstPersonOverlaySplit mode.
  4. In third person (except the debug style Style_4), stacks the offset rigs from Camera Offset Rigs on AC_CameraSystem:
Entry Default rig When Offset Crouch Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_Crouch Crouched 50 cm down Right Shoulder Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_Right Camera on the right shoulder (the player's choice, or the cover shoulder switch at a wall end) 100 cm to the side Cover Low Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_CoverLow Behind low cover 80 cm up Cover Edge Right Rig / Cover Edge Left Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_CoverEdgeRight / Left At a cover wall end 60 cm to the open side First Person Scale Rig CameraRig_FP_Scale First person, FirstPersonOverlaySplit mode First-person scale 0.25 (keeps arms and weapon out of walls) In Air Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_InAir Jumping or falling 30 cm back, 20 cm up Sliding Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_Sliding Sliding (Mover pawn only) 30 cm down Traversing Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_Traversing Vaulting or climbing 40 cm back Ragdoll Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_Ragdoll Ragdolling in third person 60 cm back, 40 cm up

The four movement-mode rigs (in air, sliding, traversing, ragdoll) need Pass Movement Mode to Camera on. The cover rigs follow the cover system's Enable Cover Camera Offsets and Enable Cover Shoulder Switch settings (Cover).

Each pawn sets its own rigs on its camera component, so two characters can use different offsets. Point an entry at your own rig to change an offset, or clear it to turn that offset off. The director's own Camera Offset Rigs is only used for a pawn without AC_CameraSystem.

The chooser table itself is fixed in the director (the engine's Evaluate Chooser node takes the table as a node setting, not an input). To change which main rig is used when, edit CHT_CameraRig and its nested tables, or duplicate them and the director.

First person needs no crouch offset: the first-person camera follows the head, so it lowers with the head when the character crouches (about 26 cm with the UEFN mannequin).

The persistent layers CameraRig_Layer_Global and CameraRig_Layer_Base are activated when the director starts.

The base rigs hold the shared parameters, and the variants override them:

Base rig Parameters ThirdPerson/CameraRig_TP_Base Boom arm offset, camera offset, field of view, forward / lateral / vertical damping, collision push TopDown/CameraRig_TopDown_Base, SideScroller/CameraRig_SideScroller_Base Camera translation and rotation, field of view, damping FirstPerson/CameraRig_FP_Base Field of view, offset, a First Person node (keeps first-person meshes out of the third-person shadow; do not remove it)

To change the look, open the rigs in the Camera Rig Asset editor. To change which rig is used when, edit the chooser tables. See Customize the camera.

docs.title: Crosshair and aim
docs.text:
For the locally controlled player, AC_CameraSystem creates the Crosshair Widget Class (default W_Crosshair) and keeps it centered on the aim point:

  • Third and first person: a line trace (Aim Trace Channel, default Visibility; Aim Trace Distance, default 100 m) from the camera along its forward vector; the dot sits where it hits, or at the end of the ray.
  • Top-down and side-scroller: the same trace from the mouse cursor into the world, so the dot sits on the point under the cursor; with a gamepad, a point 3 m out along the right stick direction.

In the fixed cameras the character also turns toward the aim. Fixed Camera Mouse Aim Type picks how the mouse gives that direction: MouseTraceWithPositionFallback (default) faces the world point under the cursor, or uses the cursor's screen position when nothing is under it; MouseScreenPosition always uses the cursor's position relative to the screen center.

GetCrosshairAim returns the aim origin, direction, point, whether it hit, and a flattened direction. The pawns pass it on through the pawn interface function Get_AimRay (with the trace channel and distance), which is what cover targeting and aim from cover read; aim from cover traces with the same channel and length, so the crosshair and the cover line of fire never disagree.

The camera component only creates and places the crosshair, at the point the aim ray hits. The widget decides how it looks: W_Crosshair is a dot in its Default Color (white). Cover targets are shown by the cover marker, not the crosshair; a custom crosshair can still ask the cover system (IsCoverTargeted).

Turn Show Crosshair off to hide the dot (it is collapsed, not destroyed). The aim ray, cover targeting and the cover marker keep working.

docs.title: Ragdoll camera
docs.text:
With Change Perspective During Ragdoll on (default), the camera switches to Camera Perspective During Ragdoll (default ThirdPerson) while the character ragdolls, and back to the previous view afterwards. With the defaults, a player in first person, top-down or side-scroller sees the ragdoll in third person; a player already in third person keeps the view, and the Ragdoll Rig offset pulls the camera back. Both pawns trigger it: the CMC pawn through AC_RagdollSystem, the Mover pawn from its Ragdoll movement mode.

The switch only happens when the ragdoll view is in Allowed Perspectives (see Choosing the perspectives). Only the player's own copy switches; the other machines get the perspective through replication.

Allow Camera Switch (default off) decides whether the perspective and shoulder inputs work during the ragdoll; looking around is never blocked. If the player changes the perspective during the ragdoll, that view is kept afterwards. Both ragdoll settings only apply while Change Perspective During Ragdoll is on.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
On AC_CameraSystem (Details panel, Camera category). Both sample pawns use these defaults.

Setting Category Default Use Enable Camera System General true Off: a fixed third-person view with the default style and shoulder; the perspective, style and shoulder inputs do nothing, there is no crosshair, and the ragdoll keeps the view. Read when play starts. Third Person Camera Bone General root Bone or socket of the visible mesh the camera attaches to in every perspective but first person. Camera Style General Style_2 (medium) Start style. Is Camera Right Shoulder General false Start shoulder. Camera Perspective Perspective ThirdPerson Start perspective. Must be in Allowed Perspectives. Allowed Perspectives Perspective ThirdPerson, TopDown, SideScroller, FirstPerson Views the player can use; 1 cycles them in this order. Show Crosshair Crosshair true Show the crosshair dot for the local player. Crosshair Widget Class Crosshair W_Crosshair Any User Widget; it is added to the viewport and centered on the aim point. Aim Trace Channel Crosshair Visibility Channel of the aim ray (crosshair, cover targeting, aim from cover). Aim Trace Distance Crosshair 10000 Length of the aim ray in cm. Camera Offset Rigs Rigs the ten rigs above Offset rigs the director stacks on the main rig. Clear an entry to turn that offset off. Pass Movement Mode to Camera Rigs true The pawn tells the camera whether it is on the ground, in the air, sliding, traversing or ragdolling, for the movement-mode rigs (and for your own chooser rows). Off = always on the ground. The CMC pawn has no slide. Change Perspective During Ragdoll Ragdoll true See Ragdoll camera. Camera Perspective During Ragdoll Ragdoll ThirdPerson See Ragdoll camera. Allow Camera Switch Ragdoll false See Ragdoll camera. Fixed Camera Mouse Aim Type FixedCamera MouseTraceWithPositionFallback Fixed cameras: how the mouse turns the character (see Crosshair and aim).

Set new values on each pawn

Change these settings on the AC_CameraSystem component of each pawn Blueprint (select the component in the Components panel). A changed class default does not reach a pawn whose component already overrides that value.

The Gameplay Cameras setup needs the data-driven console variable DDCVar.NewGameplayCameraSystem.Enable (default true, see Console variables). When it is false or missing, the pawns fall back to a plain spring arm camera and none of this runs.

docs.title: Using the camera from Blueprints
docs.text:
Call Use SetCameraPerspective Change the perspective to the one passed in (re-attaches the camera, tells the server, fires OnCameraPerspectiveChanged). It does not check Allowed Perspectives: call IsPerspectiveAvailable first. OnCameraPerspectiveChanged Event dispatcher with the new perspective. RegisterCameraListener(Listener) (BPI_CameraSystem) Adds a component implementing BPI_CameraSystemListener; after every perspective change the camera calls its OnCameraViewChanged(bFirstPerson). AC_FirstPersonSystem registers itself this way. RequestFirstPersonView(bFirstPerson) (BPI_CameraSystem) Switch to first person (true) or third person (false); returns false when the camera system is disabled. IsFirstPersonView, IsFixedCameraView, IsCameraRightShoulder (BPI_CameraSystem) Current view and shoulder, for other systems. IsPerspectiveAvailable(Perspective) True when the perspective is allowed (and, for first person, the pawn has an enabled AC_FirstPersonSystem). With Enable Camera System off, only ThirdPerson. GetNextAvailablePerspective, GetFirstAvailablePerspective What 1 would switch to; the fallback start view. GetCrosshairAim The aim ray and point. Only valid for player-controlled pawns. Get_AimRay (pawn interface) The same ray plus the trace channel and distance; zeros when the pawn has no camera system or no player controller. CameraPerspective, CameraStyle, bIsCameraRightShoulder Current state.

Other systems reach the camera through BPI_CameraSystem (find the pawn's component that implements it), so they keep working when a pawn has no camera system.

docs.title: Networking
docs.text: The perspective is set on the owning client and sent to the server (Server_SetCameraPerspective); it replicates to the other machines. Style, shoulder and crosshair are local to the player. The component needs Component Replicates on; both sample pawns set it on their AC_CameraSystem.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• A new style or mode needs matching chooser rows and rigs.
  • The offset rigs (crouch, shoulder, cover, movement modes) apply in third person only.
  • The main rig chooser table can't be swapped per pawn (see How the rig is chosen).
  • Rig graph edits need the Camera Rig Asset editor; save each rig asset after editing.
