docs.title: Cover system
docs.text:
The cover system lets a character take cover against walls and low obstacles, move along them, run from cover to cover, turn around corners, vault over cover and aim from it. It works on both sample pawns and in multiplayer.

Folder /GASPALS/Systems/CoverSystem Components AC_CoverSystem_Base (core), AC_CoverSystem_Mover or AC_CoverSystem_CMC (adapter). Both sample pawns name it AC_CoverSystem. Mover assets BP_MovementMode_Cover, BP_MovementTransition_Cover, input struct S_MoverCustomInputs_Cover Animation CR_Humanoid_CoverLower at the end of both character Anim Blueprints Widgets W_CoverMarker (cover marker) Input IA_CoverSticky and IA_CoverRun (both on Q and gamepad X in IMC_Sandbox), plus the regular move, crouch, aim and jump inputs Level needs Walls the traces can hit; a NavMeshBoundsVolume for cover runs around obstacles Settings Cover reference

docs.title: Kinds of cover
docs.text:
Soft (auto) coverSticky coverLow cover

Walk into a wall and the character takes cover. It is kept while the character stays close to the wall and is left by moving away from it (Cover Exit Input Dot, Cover Exit Delay). Corners and wall ends release soft cover, unless the camera still looks at a wall.

Soft cover is what most "walk up to a wall and hug it" games do. Turn it off with Enable Auto Cover.

Press the cover button (IA_CoverSticky) and the character snaps to the wall in front of the camera or under the crosshair. Sticky cover pulls the character to the wall, always stops at wall ends, allows corner turns, and is only left deliberately: a quick tap of the cover button, a firm push away from the wall (Sticky Exit Input Dot, Sticky Exit Delay), a cover run, a vault or aiming out of it.

Pressing the button in soft cover upgrades it to sticky cover. Turn the button off with Enable Sticky Cover.

A wall that does not reach High Cover Height (148 cm above the character's feet) is low cover. The character crouches behind it (Auto Crouch Low Cover), the camera rises over it, and aiming can stand up over it. The height test is a sphere trace (Cover Trace Radius, 12 cm), so a wall up to about 12 cm lower still counts as high.

A standing character takes low cover only through sticky cover or by crouching in front of it, and standing up leaves soft low cover. The pelvis lowers behind low cover only once the character has reached the wall (Cover Lower Settle Tolerance, 10 cm), not while sticky cover is still pulling it there.

docs.title: What the player can do
docs.text:
Action Input (demo) Result Take soft cover Move into a wall The character turns to its cover facing and moves along the wall. Take sticky cover Tap Q or gamepad X (IA_CoverSticky) Snaps to the wall in front of the camera or under the crosshair, within Sticky Cover Reach (250 cm). In soft cover, a tap upgrades it to sticky. A tap prefers sticky cover even when farther cover is targeted. Leave sticky cover Tap Q again, or push away from the wall A tap must be shorter than Sticky Tap Time (0.25 s). The push must point almost straight out (Sticky Exit Input Dot, 0.9) for Sticky Exit Delay (0.35 s). Cover run Hold Q (IA_CoverRun) with the crosshair on farther cover Held past Sticky Tap Time, sprints to the cover under the crosshair, up to Cover Run Range (15 m), and takes sticky cover there, also from sticky cover and right in front of other cover. The run finishes after the button is released; press Q again, aim or sprint to cancel it. Off with Enable Cover Run. Move along cover Move left or right Stops at wall ends (sticky always, soft with Stop at Edges). Turn a corner Hold toward the wall end in sticky cover After Corner Turn Hold Time (0.3 s) the character moves around the corner if a side wall is there. Chained corners keep following the wall. Crouch C Crouches. Behind low cover the character crouches by itself. Sprint Shift Leaves cover. No cover is taken while sprinting. Vault Space Turns to the wall if needed, then vaults over it with the traversal system. Aim from cover Hold Right Button Picks the least exposed pose that can hit the target (see below). With Enable Cover Aim off, aiming leaves cover.

Sticky cover and the cover run are two input actions on the same key. Map IA_CoverRun to its own key to split them (see Add or rebind inputs): the sticky key then only takes and leaves sticky cover (holding it never runs), and holding the run key runs to the targeted cover (a hold past Sticky Tap Time is still needed).

The cover marker (a widget on the targeted wall) shows where the cover button will take the character.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The core component evaluates cover every frame on the owning machine, then hands the result to the movement back end.

flowchart LR
    Input[Move input<br>camera, cover button] --> Eval[EvaluateCover<br>AC_CoverSystem_Base]
    Eval -->|Mover| MoverIn[S_MoverCustomInputs_Cover<br>in the Mover input]
    MoverIn --> Mode[BP_MovementMode_Cover<br>along-wall movement, wall spring]
    Eval -->|CMC| Shape[ShapeCoverMoveInput<br>shaped acceleration]
    Shape --> CMC[Character Movement Component]
    Eval --> Facing[GetCoverOrientationIntent<br>facing]
    Eval --> Cam[GetCoverCameraContext<br>camera director offsets]
    Eval --> Pose[GetCoverLowerAmount<br>CR_Humanoid_CoverLower]
  1. Sensing. Sphere traces (Cover Trace Radius) in the move direction find a wall within Cover Enter Distance. A second trace at High Cover Height above the feet decides high or low cover (the same standing or crouched, so walls near that height don't flip between the two). Probes at Edge Probe Offset to each side find the wall ends and corners.
  2. Deciding. The move input must point into the wall (Cover Enter Input Dot). Cover is kept while the wall is within Cover Hold Distance, and left after the input points away from it (Cover Exit Input Dot) for Cover Exit Delay. Cover is also released by sprinting, a traversal, a movement mode where cover is not allowed (in the air, sliding, ragdoll), aiming with Enable Cover Aim off, and standing up with Engage Rule WhileCrouched.
  3. Moving. In cover, the move input is turned into movement along the wall, and a spring holds the capsule at the Wall Distance gap for the current case (stand or crouch, soft or sticky).
    • Mover: the cover data travels in the Mover input (S_MoverCustomInputs_Cover). BP_MovementTransition_Cover switches between Walking and the Cover mode; BP_MovementMode_Cover moves along the wall (walk 150 cm/s, run and sprint 250 cm/s) and runs the wall spring.
    • CMC: AC_CoverSystem_CMC shapes the acceleration before the Character Movement Component runs, and turns the mesh to the cover facing.
  4. Facing. Four settings pick the facing per case: FaceWall, ShoulderToWall (along the wall, in the move direction) or BackToWall.
  5. Camera. The camera director asks the cover component through BPI_CoverSystem.GetCoverCameraContext. In third person it raises the camera behind low cover (CameraRig_TP_Offset_CoverLow), offsets it at wall ends (CameraRig_TP_Offset_CoverEdgeLeft/Right) and swaps the shoulder toward the open side. Turning off Enable Cover Camera Offsets removes the raise and the wall-end offset; turning off Enable Cover Shoulder Switch keeps the camera on the player's shoulder in cover.
  6. Pose. CR_Humanoid_CoverLower lowers the pelvis so the head stays under the cover top, and plants the legs on the animated feet.

docs.title: Cover run
docs.text:
Hold the cover button while the crosshair is on cover beyond Sticky Cover Reach. The character sprints along a navigation path to a stand point Cover Run Stand Offset (60 cm) in front of the wall, slows down for the arrival (Cover Run Arrive Speed, Cover Run Brake Decel) and snaps into sticky cover at Cover Run Arrive Distance.

A new press of the cover button, aiming, sprinting, a traversal, leaving the ground, or the time limit (path length at Cover Run Expected Speed, 5 m/s, plus Cover Run Max Time) cancel the run; releasing the button does not. Crouching is ignored during the run and for Cover Run Crouch Block Time (0.4 s) after it, so the sprint never turns into a slide.

When farther cover is targeted and the cover run button is held too (IA_CoverRun shares Q with IA_CoverSticky by default, so one press holds both), the press waits to see whether it is a tap or a hold:

  • released within Sticky Tap Time, it does the sticky action: soft cover becomes sticky, sticky cover is left, or a wall within Sticky Cover Reach in front is taken (with none, it runs);
  • held longer, it runs.

Without farther cover the tap acts at once.

Turn it off with Enable Cover Run. The cover button then only takes cover within Sticky Cover Reach, and the marker only shows for cover the button can take from where the character stands.

The path comes from the navigation mesh (FindPathToLocationSynchronously). Without a navmesh, or when no path is found, the character runs in a straight line and can get blocked. Clients build their own path, which needs bAllowClientSideNavigation=True (see Project settings).

docs.title: Corner turn
docs.text: In sticky cover, hold the move input toward a wall end. If the wall continues around the corner (an outside corner up to Corner Turn Angle, 100 degrees between the two wall normals, with at least Corner Turn Min Width of wall), the character walks around it and stays in cover. The held input keeps working after the turn, so a round pillar or a run of corners is followed in one go, until the input is released or changed for Corner Remap Release Time (0.15 s). Soft cover does not turn corners.

docs.title: Vault from cover
docs.text: Jump in cover asks for a vault (RequestCoverVault). If the character does not face the wall within Vault Facing Dot, it turns first (up to Vault Facing Timeout). The component then fires the OnCoverVaultReady dispatcher; the pawn handles it and starts the traversal. If the traversal finds nothing to vault (the cover does not block the Traversable channel, or is too high), the Mover pawn jumps instead; the CMC pawn does nothing.

docs.title: Aim from cover
docs.text:
With Enable Cover Aim on (default), aiming in cover does not leave cover. The character takes the least exposed pose that can hit what the camera aims at, faces the aim direction, and walks back to its cover spot when aim is released.

Pose Meaning Exposure InPlace Stay at the cover spot (crouched behind low cover). Lowest EdgeLeft, EdgeRight Step out past the end of the wall. Medium Over Stand up behind low cover. Highest

The order is: in place, then the edge the aim points toward, then the other edge, then over. A pose "can hit" when a line from its muzzle position (Cover Aim Muzzle Height Stand/Crouch) reaches the target. The target is found along the camera direction from standing eye height above the cover spot, so the choice does not chase the camera as it moves with the pose. Aiming at your own cover counts as aiming past it.

Switching is damped so the pose does not flicker: a more exposed pose is taken only after the current one has been blocked for Cover Aim Blocked Delay, and a safer pose is taken back only after it has been clearly valid for Cover Aim Return Delay. With Cover Aim Keep Standing (default), a character standing over low cover only crouches back down, never side-steps to an edge.

While aiming, pushing away from the wall leaves cover and keeps aiming. Lateral input is ignored. The camera drops its low-cover offset and takes the shoulder of the side the character stepped out to. Turn on Cover Aim Debug to print every pose change and draw the target.

docs.title: Pose lowering
docs.text:
CR_Humanoid_CoverLower runs at the end of SandboxCharacter_Mover_ABP and SandboxCharacter_CMC_ABP. It measures the cover top with a trace down into the wall and lowers the pelvis until the capsule top is Cover Lower Head Clearance (5 cm) under it, clamped to Cover Lower Max Stand (10 cm) or Cover Lower Max Crouch (15 cm). Behind cover taller than the character it lowers nothing, and it does not lower while standing over low cover to aim. The amount is computed on every machine from the replicated cover state, so remote players look the same.

The rig uses the UEFN mannequin bone names (pelvis, thigh_l, calf_l, foot_l...). Retargeted characters copy the mannequin's pose (see Characters), so they are lowered too, without extra setup.

docs.title: First person in cover
docs.text: Setting Options First Person Sticky Cover SwitchToThirdPerson (default): sticky cover switches the camera to third person and back when it ends. Disabled: the cover button does nothing in first person. SwitchToThirdPerson acts as Disabled when the camera's Allowed Perspectives has no third person. First Person Auto Cover MovementOnly (default): walking into a wall gives cover movement (wall hug, edges), but the body follows the camera instead of the cover facing. Disabled: no auto cover in first person.

docs.title: Cover marker
docs.text:
With Show Cover Marker on, the local player sees the Cover Marker Widget Class (default W_CoverMarker, Cover Marker Draw Size 100 x 12, Cover Marker Wall Offset 3 cm off the wall) on the cover under the crosshair. Other widgets can ask the cover system the same thing (IsCoverTargeted); the cover system never calls them. In cover, only farther cover (a cover run target) is marked; with Enable Cover Run off, only cover within Sticky Cover Reach is marked, and nothing while in cover. The marker is a widget component the system creates on demand; restyle it by editing W_CoverMarker or set your own widget class. Targeting and the marker run only for the locally controlled player.

The target is found along the aim ray of the pawn interface function Get_AimRay (BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn; the sample pawns forward the camera system's crosshair aim). A pawn that returns no ray falls back to the player camera's view, so a pawn without AC_CameraSystem still finds cover targets.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
All settings are on the cover component of the pawn. Select AC_CoverSystem in the pawn's Components panel and look under Cover in the Details panel (a few internal settings, such as Cover Probe Padding, are under the category's advanced arrow). The categories are:

Category Controls General Master switches: Enable Cover, Enable Auto Cover, Enable Sticky Cover, Enable Cover Run, Engage Rule (Automatic or WhileCrouched), Move Into Cover, Auto Crouch Low Cover. Detection Trace distances, radius, High Cover Height, edge probes, how sharp a bend cover follows; Cover Top Probe Height (300 cm, walls taller than this count as this high) and the advanced Cover Probe Padding (20 cm). Movement Wall gaps per case, the wall spring, pull and push speeds, stopping at edges in soft cover; Cover Side Input Threshold (0.2, sideways stick needed to move along the wall, stop at an edge or turn a corner). Facing Facing style per case, shoulder yaw offsets (and on the CMC adapter, Character Rotation Interp Speed, the mesh turn speed). Exit How firmly and how long to push away to leave soft and sticky cover. Sticky Cover button reach and tap time, and Sticky Reentry Cooldown (0.5 s before cover can grab the character again after leaving it). CoverRun Range, time limit, path following and arrival; Cover Run Expected Speed (500, plans the time limit), Cover Run Stand Offset (60 cm from the wall), Cover Run Crouch Block Time (0.4 s) and Cover Run Reentry Delay (0.2 s) after a run. CornerTurn Hold time, corner angle and width, and Corner Remap Release Time (how long the held input keeps turning corners). Traversal Facing needed before a vault, and its timeout. Aim Aim from cover: switch, muzzle heights, hit tolerance, cover depth, damping, edge clearance, step-out steering. Debug Enable Debug (draws every cover trace for one frame) and Cover Aim Debug (prints aim pose changes and draws the aim target). Pose Pelvis lowering limits and head clearance. FirstPerson Behavior when the camera is in first person. Camera Enable Cover Camera Offsets (low-cover raise, wall-end offset) and Enable Cover Shoulder Switch (camera moves to the open side at a wall end). Marker Cover marker on or off, its widget class, draw size and wall offset. Collision Cover Trace Channel (default Cover): the channel of every cover probe. Mover AC_CoverSystem_Mover only: Cover Mode Name and Ground Mode Name (Cover, Walking). CMC AC_CoverSystem_CMC only: Forced Crouch Delay (0.1 s of low cover before the forced crouch).

Every setting with its default is in the Cover reference. Recipes for common setups (no auto cover, Gears-style sticky only, crouch-only cover, wider wall gaps) are in Configure cover behavior.

Check settings on the pawn's component

Enable Cover and Auto Crouch Low Cover are on by default, so adding a cover component to your own pawn enables cover without further setup; the sample pawns also set them on their components. Check settings on the pawn's component rather than on the class: a value changed in AC_CoverSystem_Base does not reach pawns that already set their own.

docs.title: What counts as cover
docs.text:
Cover probes trace the Cover channel. Every collision profile answers it like Visibility, so anything that blocks visibility is cover, and characters, triggers and invisible walls are not. To change that per object, set its collision to Custom and change the Cover response:

  • Ignore: the object is never cover (foliage, a fence you see through, a prop too small to hide behind).
  • Block: the object is cover even if it ignores Visibility.

Level requirements and examples are in Set up cover in a level, and the channel itself in Project settings.

To trace another channel (for example Visibility in a project without the Cover channel), set Cover Trace Channel on the pawn's cover component. Aiming from cover traces the camera's Aim Trace Channel instead (see Camera), so a wall that isn't cover still blocks shots.

docs.title: Networking
docs.text:
• Mover pawn. The cover state is part of the Mover input, so the server and the other clients run the same cover movement as the owner. Simulated proxies get it through the synced inputs. No extra replication is needed.
  • CMC pawn. The owner shapes its own acceleration (replicated by the CMC). The cover state is sent to the server about 20 times a second (ServerUpdateCover) and replicated to other machines, which apply it in ApplyRemoteCoverState. Small corrections (2 to 4 cm) can happen at sticky edge stops and corners.
  • Aim from cover runs on the owner only. Other machines see its result: position, crouch and facing.
  • Cover run paths are built on the owning client, so bAllowClientSideNavigation must be on.

docs.title: Using cover from Blueprints
docs.text:
Call On Use RequestStickyCover / ReleaseStickyCover Base Sticky cover button pressed / released (IA_CoverSticky: tap for sticky cover). RequestCoverRun / ReleaseCoverRun Base Cover run button pressed / released (IA_CoverRun: hold to run to the targeted cover). InitializeSystem Base Call once when the pawn starts: stores the pawn (the adapters extend it). EvaluateCover Base Runs the cover logic for this frame. Mover pawns call it in ProduceInput; the CMC adapter calls it from UpdateCoverCMC. RemapCoverMoveInput Base Mover pawns: turns the move input into corner-turn, cover-run and aim steering, before EvaluateCover. IsCoverCrouchBlocked Base True during a cover run (and shortly after it) and while standing to aim over low cover: ignore crouch requests then. GetCoverLowerAmount Base Pelvis lowering in cm for CR_Humanoid_CoverLower; the Anim Blueprints call it. RequestCoverVault Base Ask for a vault from cover; listen to OnCoverVaultReady to start the traversal. IsCoverAiming Base True while aiming from cover. GetCoverCameraState Base Low cover, edge side and shoulder side (each already filtered by the camera settings), for your own camera logic. GetCoverOrientationIntent Base The facing the pawn should turn to. IsCoverTargeted Base True while the cover button would take the local player to cover (what the cover marker shows). UpdateCoverCMC CMC adapter Call every frame before the Character Movement Component ticks (the sample pawn calls it from its pre-movement event, which AC_PreCMCTick fires). UpdateMoverCoverState Mover adapter Keeps the in-cover flag in step with the Cover mode. The component calls it on its own tick, with UpdateCoverVault and the cover marker update.

On any machine, the component's bIsCharacterInCover and CoverState (wall normal and point, low cover, edges, sticky) give the current cover state: the CMC adapter replicates it, and the Mover adapter reads it from the synced Mover input. To put cover on your own pawn, follow Add the systems to your own pawn.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Cover needs walls the traces can hit (the Cover channel by default). Very thin walls (under 10 cm) count as tall for the pose lowering.
  • Peek (leaning out without aiming) is not implemented.
  • The cover run runs straight when no navmesh path exists, and can then be blocked.
  • The pose-lowering rig expects the UEFN mannequin bone names.
  • In first person, only the two behaviors of the First Person settings are available.
  • The CMC pawn shows small corrections at sticky edge stops and corners in network play.

docs.title: Debug tools
docs.text: /GASPALS/Systems/DebugTools/AC_DebugTools is a component on SandboxCharacter_Mover that groups the sandbox's demo and debug tools: shooting characters into ragdoll, spawning or rotating characters, teleporting and flying. It works in any game mode; RagdollLevel, with its placed target characters and physics obstacles, is the place to try it. Enable Debug Tools turns it off, and it can be removed from the pawn (Turning systems on and off).

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
Input Condition Action Left Button (gamepad RT) aim held (Right Button or LT) Shoot: the character hit goes ragdoll, with an impulse at the bone that was hit. Without aim, the same key is a takedown. E (gamepad Y) aim held Spawn or rotate: rotate the character you aim at by 90 degrees, or spawn a new character on the floor where you aim. Without aim, E is a shove or a bench interaction. J Teleport to the point under the view. Z keyboard only Fly: toggle the Mover Flying mode.

The component has no input events of its own. The Mover pawn's input events call it: the takedown and interact inputs call Shoot and Spawn Or Rotate while aim is held, and a raw Z key event calls Toggle Debug Fly. J (IA_TeleportToTarget) belongs to the player controller (PC_Sandbox), which calls the component's Teleport To Target when the possessed pawn has one. N (next pawn) and M (next character) belong to the player controller too. See Controls.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Aim. Every tool reads the view from the pawn's camera (its Gameplay Camera component), or from the pawn's eyes when it has no camera component.
  • Shoot. The server traces along the view for physics bodies; the character hit is asked to ragdoll and to push the bone that was hit (BPI_RagdollSystem, through Get Ragdoll System). A Mover character applies the impulse once its body is simulating. A standing CMC character's mesh has no collision, so the shot passes through it.
  • Spawn or rotate. The server traces along the view. A character hit (Mover or CMC) is turned 90 degrees; anything else spawns a new character of your pawn's class at the hit point (or at the end of the trace), facing you. Only the last Max Spawned Characters spawned characters are kept: the oldest is destroyed. Spawned Mover characters have no player, so they get up by themselves after a ragdoll (Ragdoll).
  • Teleport. A sphere trace runs from the eyes along the view; the pawn moves just off the surface hit, or to the end of the trace, keeping its rotation. Pawns without the component (the CMC pawn) use the controller's own teleport instead, with the controller's Teleport Max Distance (also 10000 cm). With Enable Debug Tools off, J does nothing on a pawn that has the component.
  • Fly. Switches the Mover pawn between the Flying mode and falling, with an on-screen message.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Settings on the AC_DebugTools component of the Mover pawn:

Setting Category Default Use Enable Debug Tools Debug Tools > General true Master switch for the shot, spawn / rotate, teleport and fly tools of this component. Shot Trace Distance Debug Tools > Demo 100000 Length of the shot trace in cm. Shot Impulse Debug Tools > Demo 2500 Impulse applied to the bone hit by a shot. Spawn Trace Distance Debug Tools > Demo 1000 Reach of the spawn / rotate trace in cm; with no hit the character spawns at the end of the trace. Max Spawned Characters Debug Tools > Demo 3 Spawned characters kept alive; the oldest is destroyed beyond this. Teleport Max Distance Debug Tools > Teleport 10000 Reach of the teleport trace in cm.

Shipping a game

Turn Enable Debug Tools off on your pawn, or remove the component, so players can't spawn characters or teleport. The component is optional: nothing else in GASPALS depends on it. The pawn calls it through wrapper functions (DebugTools_Shoot, DebugTools_SpawnOrRotate, DebugTools_ToggleFly) that find it by class, so the pawn still compiles without it.

The full variable and function list is in the Pawns and Anim Blueprints reference.

docs.title: Adding the debug tools to another pawn
docs.text:
What each tool needs:

Tool Your pawn needs The target needs Shoot An input that calls Shoot A ragdoll system (BPI_RagdollSystem, on the actor or one of its components) and a mesh that a PhysicsBody trace hits Rotate An input that calls Spawn Or Rotate TeleportCharacter from BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn Spawn An input that calls Spawn Or Rotate Teleport TeleportCharacter from BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn; possessed by PC_Sandbox (or your controller calls Teleport To Target) Fly A CharacterMoverComponent and an input that calls Toggle Debug Fly
  1. Open your pawn Blueprint. In the Components panel, click Add and pick AC_DebugTools. Component Replicates is already on in its class defaults; leave it on.
  2. Copy the three wrapper functions (DebugTools_Shoot, DebugTools_SpawnOrRotate, DebugTools_ToggleFly) from SandboxCharacter_Mover, or call the component's functions directly.
  3. In your input events, call Shoot and Spawn Or Rotate where you want them, for example from the IA_Takedown and IA_Interact events while aim is held, as the Mover pawn does. For flying, add a keyboard Z event (or your own input action) that calls Toggle Debug Fly.
  4. Compile and save. Play with your pawn in a level that has another character with a ragdoll system (a placed SandboxCharacter_Mover, for example). Hold aim on that character and shoot: it falls into ragdoll. Aim at the floor and spawn: a character of your pawn's class appears. Press J: your pawn moves to the point you look at.

docs.title: Networking
docs.text:
Tool How it replicates Shoot The owner sends its view to the server (reliable server RPC); the server traces and starts the ragdoll, and the impulse is multicast to every machine. Spawn or rotate The owner sends its view to the server (reliable server RPC). Spawned characters replicate as actors. Rotating another player's pawn is done by that player's machine (a replicated counter tells it to turn), so its own prediction doesn't undo it. Teleport, fly Run locally on the owner, so they work in standalone and for the listen server host. A client's teleport or fly is overridden by the server: both are single-player debug helpers.

Over a listen server, expect one movement correction on the client when the host shoots or rotates the client's pawn.

docs.title: Other debug aids
docs.text:
These are not part of the component:

  • The movement debug shapes (DDCvar.DrawCharacterDebugShapes) are drawn by the Mover pawn and the Anim Blueprints.
  • DDCVar.CharacterPhysics.DrawDebug 1 draws the Mover ragdoll's obstacle sweep and impact traces.
  • DDCVar.CharacterPhysics.DefaultProfile 1 turns on physical animation outside ragdoll (Ragdoll).

All debug console variables: Console variables.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Shoot needs the characters hit to have a ragdoll system (BPI_RagdollSystem) and a mesh that blocks the shot's PhysicsBody trace; rotate and teleport need TeleportCharacter (BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn); fly needs a CharacterMoverComponent on the owner.
  • The demo shot is a debug tool, not a weapon system: no damage, ammunition or effects.
  • Teleport and fly don't work for network clients (see Networking).

docs.text:

  • Mover and CMC pawns
  • Add the systems to your own pawn

docs.title: Equipment system
docs.text:
The equipment system puts an item in the character's hands. Selecting an item spawns its actor, attaches it to a hand socket, links the item's overlay poses (third and first person) and updates the hand IK targets. Items are described by data assets, so adding one needs no code.

Folder /GASPALS/Systems/EquipmentSystem Component AC_EquipmentSystem (on both pawns) Interface BPI_EquipmentSystem (what other systems ask about the held item) Data Data/PDA_Equipment (class), Data/DA_Equipment_<Item> (one per item), Data/CHT_Equipment (chooser), Data/Enum_Equipment (slots) Actors Actors/BP_Equipment_<Item> Meshes Assets/Meshes (M4A1, M9, Bow skeletal meshes with their skeletons; Torch, Binoculars, Box, Barrel static meshes) Menu UI/W_Switcher_Equipment, UI/W_Button_Equipment Input IA_Equipment: T or gamepad RB (hold for the menu); IA_Select_Next / IA_Select_Previous: mouse wheel or D-pad up / down to choose Settings Equipment reference

docs.title: Included items
docs.text:
Slot Actor (mesh) Third-person overlay First-person overlay Attach socket Unequip none The selected overlay stance (ABP_Overlay_Default unless changed) none none Rifle BP_Equipment_Rifle (M4A1) ABP_Overlay_Rifle ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Rifle overlay_rifle Pistol BP_Equipment_Pistol (M9) ABP_Overlay_Pistol2H ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Pistol2H overlay_pistol Revolver (hidden from the menu by default) BP_Equipment_Revolver (M9) ABP_Overlay_Pistol1H ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Pistol1H overlay_pistol Bow BP_Equipment_Bow (Bow) ABP_Overlay_Bow ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Bow overlay_bow Torch BP_Equipment_Torch (Torch) ABP_Overlay_Torch none overlay_torch Binoculars BP_Equipment_Binoculars (Binoculars) ABP_Overlay_Binoculars none overlay_binoculars Box BP_Equipment_Box (Box) ABP_Overlay_Box none overlay_box Barrel BP_Equipment_Barrel (Barrel) ABP_Overlay_Barrel none overlay_barrel

The rifle, pistol, revolver and bow are skeletal meshes whose skeletons carry HandIK and ADS sockets (the pistol and the revolver share the M9 mesh with two different poses: two-handed and one-handed). The bow animates its string while you aim (Bow_AnimBP, driven by the actor's Draw value). The others are static meshes; only the binoculars have a HandIK socket.

The revolver is not polished yet, so it is listed in Hidden Equipment and does not appear in the menu. It still works when selected from Blueprints. To bring it back, remove it from Hidden Equipment (see Settings).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    Sel[SelectedEquipment<br>Enum_Equipment] --> Ch[CHT_Equipment<br>chooser]
    Ch --> DA[DA_Equipment_Item<br>PDA_Equipment]
    DA -->|Overlay Pose TP| L1[LinkAnimClassLayers<br>third-person mesh]
    DA -->|Overlay Pose FP| L2[LinkAnimClassLayers<br>first-person meshes]
    DA -->|Spawned Actor| Sp[Spawn actor<br>attach to socket]
    Sp --> IK[UpdateHandIK<br>IK_* transforms]
    IK --> ABP[Character Anim Blueprints<br>CR_Humanoid_HandIK]

At start, the pawn hands the component its meshes (InitializeSystem, called from the pawn's Equipment_Initialize; see Add the systems to your own pawn) and the starting item is equipped.

When Selected Equipment changes (UpdateEquipment):

  1. The previous item's actor is destroyed.
  2. CHT_Equipment turns the slot into its data asset. A slot without a chooser row falls back to DA_Equipment_Unequip (empty hands).
  3. When the data asset has a Spawned Actor, its Overlay Pose TP is linked on the pawn's third-person mesh. When it has none (Unequip), the overlay system applies the selected stance instead (see Overlay system). The Overlay Pose FP is linked on the first-person meshes; an empty one resets the first-person layers to their defaults.
  4. If the data asset has an actor class, the actor is spawned (owned by the pawn) and attached to the visible third-person mesh at Attach Socket TP, with Attach Offset TP.
  5. The item's mesh components are attached to the visible third-person mesh (meshes tagged DoNotAttach are left where they are). If the pawn has a first-person system and the data asset's Create First Person Copy is on, the equipment system asks it for first-person copies of the item's meshes (CreateItemFirstPersonCopies on BPI_FirstPersonSystem) and attaches them to the first-person mesh at Attach Socket FP with Attach Offset FP. Before an item is destroyed, its copies are removed (RemoveItemFirstPersonCopies). Without a first-person system, the item still attaches in third person.
  6. UpdateHandIK computes the hand targets. It runs for every slot, so after Unequip (no actor) the hand IK transforms are reset instead of keeping the previous item's values.

The "visible" mesh is the one the player sees: the pawn's own mesh, or the retargeted character's mesh when one is shown (M), so items attach to that character's skeleton sockets.

docs.title: Hand IK
docs.text:
Two sockets on the item mesh place the hands (names set per item in the data asset):

Socket (default name) Use HandIK (Hand IKSocket) Where the support hand grips the item. ADS (ADSSocket) The sight point, lined up with the eye when aiming down sights in first person.

UpdateHandIK stores six transforms (IK_HandLeft, IK_HandRight, IK_ADS and their _FP versions), each expressed relative to the hand that holds the item (Left Hand Bone / Right Hand Bone on AC_EquipmentSystem, default hand_l / hand_r), so they follow it. IK_HandLeft is the HandIK socket in the right hand's space (for items held in the right hand), IK_HandRight the same socket in the left hand's space (for items held in the left hand), and IK_ADS the ADS socket in the space of the hand that holds the item (the left hand when Is Left Handed is on).

The character Anim Blueprints (and the retarget and first-person Anim Blueprints) read them and run CR_Humanoid_HandIK. The hand IK weight comes from the overlay pose's enable_handik_l / enable_handik_r curves, so each pose decides when, and with which hand, the support hand grips. Items without a HandIK socket (torch, box, barrel) rely on their overlay pose alone.

The bow moves its sockets as it draws, so it updates the hand IK every frame.

docs.title: Sockets on the character
docs.text: The items attach to overlay_* sockets on the character's Skeleton (not on the skeletal meshes): overlay_rifle, overlay_pistol, overlay_bow, overlay_torch, overlay_binoculars, overlay_box, overlay_barrel. On the UEFN mannequin (SK_UEFN_Mannequin) they hang from weapon_r / weapon_l; on the UE5 mannequin (SK_Mannequin) and the MetaHuman skeleton (metahuman_base_skel) from hand_r / hand_l. Retargeted characters need them on their own skeleton (see Add a retargeted character). A missing socket attaches the item at the mesh origin, at the character's feet.

docs.title: The menu
docs.text:
Hold T (gamepad RB): the world slows to Menu Time Dilation (0.35) and the Equipment Menu Widget Class (default W_Switcher_Equipment) opens with one button per Enum_Equipment value not listed in Hidden Equipment, labeled with the enumerator's display name. The highlight starts on the current item. Scroll up (mouse wheel up, D-pad up) to move the highlight up the list and down to move it down (it wraps at the ends and skips hidden slots); release the key to equip it. A new enum value appears in the menu automatically, unless it is added to Hidden Equipment.

The buttons follow the enum order: Unequip, Rifle, Pistol, Bow, Torch, Binoculars, Box, Barrel (Revolver, between Pistol and Bow, is hidden by default). To reorder the menu, drag the enumerators in Enum_Equipment (pins, data assets and chooser rows refer to them by name).

Hidden Equipment only hides slots from the menu: SelectNewEquipment and Selected Equipment still equip them. Use it for unfinished items, or for items a pawn should not offer.

The component owns the menu: it keeps the highlighted item (HighlightedEquipment), moves it on scroll and equips it on release. The widget only shows it, reading the component every frame, so a custom menu widget needs no calls from the component; read HighlightedEquipment (and SelectedEquipment) from the owning pawn's AC_EquipmentSystem.

If the pawn is destroyed while the menu is open, the component's EndPlay calls CloseEquipmentMenu: it removes the menu widget and sets the world speed back to normal.

docs.title: Cleanup
docs.text: When the pawn is destroyed, DestroySpawnedActors (bound to the pawn's On Destroyed) destroys the item actor.

docs.title: Data asset fields
docs.text:
PDA_Equipment, in the Details panel of each DA_Equipment_<Item>:

Field Category Use Spawned Actor Equipment > Attach Actor class to spawn. Empty for Unequip: nothing is held and the overlay system's stance shows. Attach Socket TP / Attach Socket FP Equipment > Attach Socket on the visible third-person / first-person mesh. Attach Offset TP / Attach Offset FP Equipment > Attach Transform relative to the socket. Is Left Handed Equipment > Attach The item is held in the left hand (the bow): the ADS target follows the left hand. Overlay Pose TP Equipment > Overlay Overlay Anim Blueprint linked on the third-person mesh (a child of ABP_OverlayPose_Base). Linked when Spawned Actor is set; without an actor, the overlay system's stance shows. Overlay Pose FP Equipment > Overlay First-person overlay Anim Blueprint (a child of ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Base). Optional: without one, first person shows the third-person overlay. Hand IKSocket / ADSSocket Equipment > HandIK Socket names on the item mesh (default HandIK, ADS). ADSEnter Speed / ADSExit Speed Equipment > ADS First-person aim down sights blend speeds for this item (15 / 5). ADSHand Offset Equipment > ADS First person: moves the hands (and the item) toward or away from the eyes while aiming, in the head's space at the reference pose (0, 0, 0). Create First Person Copy Equipment > First Person On (default): the pawn's first-person system makes a first-person copy of the item's meshes for the first-person hands. Off: the item is only seen in third person. First Person Motion Profile Equipment > First Person First-person hand and item motion while this item is equipped (a PDA_FirstPersonMotion: DA_FPMotion_Rifle, DA_FPMotion_Pistol, DA_FPMotion_Bow, DA_FPMotion_Heavy). Empty: the pawn's default profile on AC_FirstPersonSystem. See Tune first-person motion.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
On AC_EquipmentSystem (select the component in the pawn Blueprint). Both sample pawns use the defaults.

Setting Category Default Use Enable Equipment Equipment > General true Read at start. Off: the pawn starts and stays empty-handed (Unequip) and the equipment menu does nothing. Selected Equipment Equipment > Selection Unequip The item the pawn starts with. Left Hand Bone / Right Hand Bone Equipment > HandIK hand_l / hand_r Hand bones the hand IK targets are expressed in. Change them for skeletons with other hand bone names. Equipment Menu Widget Class Equipment > UI W_Switcher_Equipment The menu opened while T is held. Any User Widget (a custom widget should also skip Hidden Equipment). Menu Time Dilation Equipment > UI 0.35 World speed while the menu is open. 1 turns the slow motion off. Hidden Equipment Equipment > UI Revolver Slots left out of the menu (also skipped when scrolling). They can still be selected from Blueprints. Set it on the component of each pawn that should differ from the class default.

The rest of the component's variables are runtime state. With no first-person meshes (first person not in the camera's Allowed Perspectives, or no AC_FirstPersonSystem on the pawn), the first-person links and copies are skipped and the item is attached in third person only.

docs.title: Using equipment from Blueprints
docs.text:
On the pawn's AC_EquipmentSystem:

Call Use SelectNewEquipment(SelectedEquipment) Event: equip a slot. Call it on the machine that controls the pawn (see Networking). SelectedEquipment The current slot. SpawnedActor The current item actor (none when empty-handed). EquipmentData The current data asset. GetHandIK(SocketName, TargetBoneName, bIsFirstPerson) A socket of the item in a hand bone's space (identity without an item).

Other systems ask through BPI_EquipmentSystem, so they work (with "nothing held" answers) when the component is removed:

Interface function Returns GetHeldItemHands Which hands hold the item (used by the CMC ragdoll to pick a get-up animation). GetFirstPersonItemSettings The item's ADS speeds, ADS hand offset and first-person motion profile. GetFirstPersonHandTargets The first-person hand IK and ADS targets, the handedness and whether the item has a first-person overlay.

GetHeldItemHands lists the slots by hand

GetHeldItemHands answers with a Switch on Enum_Equipment, one return per slot. A slot that is not wired there (for example a new item) answers "no hands", so the CMC ragdoll plays the default get-up. Wire new slots in it (see Add an equipment item).

docs.title: Networking
docs.text:
Selected Equipment is replicated with a RepNotify, skipping the owner. The owning client sets it locally (and equips at once), then sends it to the server with one reliable Server RPC (UpdateSelectedEquipment); the server and the other clients spawn and attach their own copy of the item in the RepNotify.

Call SelectNewEquipment where the pawn is controlled: on the owning client, or on the server for the listen server host's pawn and AI. Because the replication skips the owner, a server-side call on a pawn that a remote client controls updates the server and the other clients, but not that client.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The menu slows the whole world (also on a listen server host) while it is open.
  • The torch, binoculars, box and barrel have no first-person overlay pose.
  • The revolver is hidden from the menu by default (see Included items).
  • Changes to a data asset made while playing apply the next time the item is selected.

docs.title: First person system
docs.text:
GASPALS first person shows the character's own body from its eyes, not floating arms. One component on the pawn generates the first-person meshes at runtime for whatever body the player sees: the pawn's own mannequin, the active retargeted character and the held item. What to draw for each body comes from a small data asset, so you never add or tag first-person components by hand. On top of the third-person pose, a first-person Anim Blueprint adds a stable camera, first-person arm poses, aim down sights (ADS) and an arm aim offset.

Folder /GASPALS/Systems/FirstPersonSystem Component AC_FirstPersonSystem (on the pawn only) Modes E_FirstPersonMode: TrueFirstPerson, FirstPersonOverlay, FirstPersonOverlaySplit Generated meshes AC_FirstPersonSkeletalMesh, AC_FirstPersonStaticMesh (created at runtime, never added by hand) Body setup PDA_FirstPersonSetup (class); Setups/DA_FirstPersonSetup_UEFN (the pawns), _Manny, _Quinn, _Kellan Interfaces BPI_FirstPersonSystem (asked by other systems), BPI_FirstPersonCharacter (a character's setup) Anim Blueprint ABP_FirstPerson_UEFN (and the template ABP_FirstPerson_Host for meshes on other skeletons) Control Rigs CR_FirstPerson_BodyCamera, CR_FirstPerson_Camera, CR_FirstPerson_ADS, CR_FirstPerson_AimOffset, Motion/CR_FirstPerson_Motion Motion profiles Motion/PDA_FirstPersonMotion (class); Motion/DA_FPMotion_Unarmed, _Pistol, _Rifle, _Bow, _Heavy Overlays ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Base and its children (Rifle, Pistol2H, Pistol1H, Bow) Camera rigs CameraRig_FP_Base, CameraRig_FP_Scale (Split mode) Tools Tools/EUB_SplitFirstPersonMesh (cut a mesh into arms and body) Settings First person reference

Press 1 (next perspective) until the view is in first person; by default it comes after third person, top-down and side-scroller (see Controls). First person must be in the camera's Allowed Perspectives and Enable First Person must be on; otherwise the component builds nothing (Choosing the perspectives).

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
Set First Person Mode on the pawn's AC_FirstPersonSystem. It applies to every body the pawn shows, including the retargeted characters.

FirstPersonOverlay (default)FirstPersonOverlaySplitTrueFirstPerson

First-person arm poses on the full body: the classic shooter look while keeping legs and shadow. Looking down, the arms follow the view pitch up to First Person Arm Pitch Down Limit (45 degrees) and the spine leans for the rest; the camera follows the lean by First Person Camera Follow Lean (0.75).

One full-body mesh (plus clothing). Bodies on another skeleton than the UEFN mannequin need a Retargeter in their first-person setup.

The same image, but arms and body are separate meshes sharing one pose. The camera director adds CameraRig_FP_Scale, which draws the arms and the weapon at 0.25 scale toward the camera, so they do not clip into walls. The image looks the same; only depth changes.

Needs Arms Meshes and Body Meshes in the body's first-person setup. A body whose setup has no Arms Meshes uses FirstPersonOverlay instead, and an on-screen warning says so. All shipped setups have both.

The third-person animation seen from the eyes, unchanged, plus ADS while aiming. The head is pitched by the view. No first-person overlay poses.

Needs no retargeter and no UE-standard spine names (see Skeleton requirements). A body on another skeleton whose setup has no Retargeter uses this mode automatically, whatever the pawn's mode, and an on-screen warning says so. Weapons can clip into walls.

docs.title: Body setup
docs.text:
What to draw for a body is a PDA_FirstPersonSetup data asset (in Systems/FirstPersonSystem/Setups):

Field Use Full Meshes Meshes for FirstPersonOverlay and TrueFirstPerson. The first entry is the lead, the others (clothing, hair) follow it. Empty = the third-person body is reused with the head hidden. Arms Meshes / Body Meshes Meshes for FirstPersonOverlaySplit. Retargeter IK Retargeter from the UEFN mannequin to this body's skeleton. Empty for the UEFN mannequin. Eye Offset Camera point relative to the head bone. Camera Bone / Head Bone VB Camera / head by default.

Each body names its setup:

  • The pawn: Default Setup on AC_FirstPersonSystem (DA_FirstPersonSetup_UEFN on both sample pawns). Its body mesh is the component named by Third Person Mesh Name.
  • A retargeted character: its First Person Setup variable (DA_FirstPersonSetup_Manny, _Quinn, _Kellan), returned by GetFirstPersonSetup (BPI_FirstPersonCharacter). Its body mesh comes from GetVisualBodyMesh (BPI_VisualOverride), which returns the SkeletalMesh component on BP_RetargetedCharacter_Base.

A character without a setup still works: its body mesh is reused as the first-person mesh with the head hidden, and a warning is shown.

docs.title: Mesh generation
docs.text:
When the pawn initializes its systems, it tells AC_FirstPersonSystem which body is active: the retargeted character when one is shown, else the pawn itself. The component then builds the first-person meshes of that body from its setup:

  • Overlay and true modes: the first entry of Full Meshes becomes the lead mesh: it runs the first-person Anim Blueprint. The other entries follow it.
  • Split mode: the first Arms Meshes entry is the lead; the other arms meshes and all Body Meshes follow.
  • Empty lists: the third-person mesh is reused as the lead, with the head bone hidden.

The meshes are created on the body's actor, so a retargeted character's first-person meshes go away with it. When the character changes (M), the previous body's first-person meshes are removed and the new body's are built.

Generated meshes use two small component classes, AC_FirstPersonSkeletalMesh and AC_FirstPersonStaticMesh (item copies of static meshes). They are plain mesh components that can remove themselves: Unreal only lets a component be destroyed by its own actor or by itself, and the first-person system is a different component. If you create first-person meshes of your own, remove them from the actor that owns them.

Every generated mesh is attached to the third-person mesh, visible to the owning player only, casts no shadow and only animates when rendered. Material overrides are copied from the matching third-person component (same mesh, or a mesh named <Name>_FP...). Followers that have their own skeleton and post-process Anim Blueprint (the MetaHuman hoodie and shoes) keep that Anim Blueprint, which copies the lead's pose and drives their corrective bones; other followers use leader pose.

When the camera switches perspective, the component swaps visibility: in first person the first-person meshes show for the owner and the third-person meshes become world-space representations (other players and shadows still see them).

docs.title: The first-person pose
docs.text:
ABP_FirstPerson_UEFN runs on the lead mesh:

flowchart TD
    A[Copy pose from the third-person mesh] --> B[CR_FirstPerson_BodyCamera<br>VB Camera follows the body head]
    B --> C{Overlay?}
    C -->|TrueFirstPerson, montage, no overlay| E
    C -->|overlay modes| D[First-person overlay from spine_03 up<br>retargeted from the UEFN logic mesh if needed]
    D --> E[CR_FirstPerson_Camera<br>stable head, camera at the eyes]
    E --> F[CR_FirstPerson_ADS<br>hands to the sight line when aiming]
    F --> G[CR_FirstPerson_AimOffset<br>arms follow the view, spine leans]
    G --> M[CR_FirstPerson_Motion<br>hand and item sway]
    M --> H[Hand IK]
  1. Copy the third-person pose (all locomotion, montages and overlays come along).
  2. Body camera: VB Camera follows the body's head, smoothed vertically, so the view follows crouches, traversal and landings. That is why first person needs no crouch camera offset.
  3. Overlay: the first-person arm pose (ALI_OverlayFirstPerson) replaces the upper body from spine_03. On other skeletons it is retargeted from the pawn's hidden UEFN first-person logic mesh with the setup's Retargeter.
  4. Camera rig: keeps the head stable, puts the head at its reference rotation (plus the view pitch) and places VB Camera at the eyes (the setup's Eye Offset).
  5. ADS: while aiming, the hands move so the item's ADS socket sits on the sight line in front of the eye. The blend speeds and a hand offset come from the equipped item (ADSEnter Speed, ADSExit Speed and ADSHand Offset on its PDA_Equipment data asset, category Equipment > ADS).
  6. Aim offset: the arms rotate with the view pitch up to the limits; the spine takes the rest.
  7. Motion: CR_FirstPerson_Motion sways the hands and the item (see Hand and item motion).
  8. Hand IK keeps the hands on the item's grips.

In first person, AC_CameraSystem attaches the camera to the lead mesh's Camera Bone (VB Camera by default).

docs.title: Equipment in first person
docs.text:
Equipment actors (BP_Equipment_*) only carry their third-person meshes, with no first-person component. When an item is equipped, the equipment system asks the pawn's first-person system for first-person copies (CreateItemFirstPersonCopies on BPI_FirstPersonSystem). Each copy uses the same mesh and anim class, belongs to the item actor, is attached to its source, is visible to the owner only and has no collision. The equipment system attaches the copies to the first-person hand socket. In third person the copy is hidden; in first person it shows and the original becomes a world-space representation. Before the item is destroyed, the equipment system removes its copies (RemoveItemFirstPersonCopies).

Turn Create First Person Copy off on an item's PDA_Equipment data asset to give it no first-person copy. A pawn without AC_FirstPersonSystem still holds items in third person.

On a body (the pawn or a retargeted character), the third-person mesh and every mesh attached under it count as the third-person body, so no component tags are needed anywhere.

docs.title: Overlays
docs.text: First-person overlay Blueprints (ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_<Item>) are linked by the equipment system from the item's data asset (Overlay Pose FP). They hold first-person arm poses and curves for the first-person rigs (enable_cr_fp_stable_arms, enable_cr_fp_stable_head, enable_cr_fp_ads, enable_cr_fp_aimoffset, hand IK). Rifle, Pistol2H, Pistol1H (revolver) and Bow have one; items without one show the third-person overlay in first person.

docs.title: Hand and item motion
docs.text:
On top of the first-person pose, the hands and the held item move with the player: they lag behind view turns, lean into strafes, bob with the steps, breathe at rest and take a jolt on jumps and landings. While aiming down sights the motion fades so the sight stays steady. The camera never moves.

  • The rig CR_FirstPerson_Motion (in ABP_FirstPerson_UEFN, after the aim offset and before the hand IK) moves both arms and the item together around a point in front of the eyes, with springs. The left hand stays on two-handed items.
  • The values come from motion profiles (PDA_FirstPersonMotion data assets in /GASPALS/Systems/FirstPersonSystem/Motion): the equipped item's First Person Motion Profile, else the pawn's. Four ship with the template: Unarmed, Pistol, Rifle and Heavy.
  • On the pawn's AC_FirstPersonSystem (First Person > Motion): First Person Motion Profile (the default, DA_FPMotion_Unarmed) and First Person Motion Intensity (1; 0 turns the motion off); Debug First Person Motion is under First Person > Debug.
  • A curve disable_fp_motion (0 to 1) in an animation the character plays (a montage, for example) pauses the motion while it is above 0.
  • It works in all three modes and on retargeted characters. It is local only: other players don't see first-person meshes, and shots and the crosshair use the camera, so the motion never changes where shots go.

Recipes and the full setting list: Tune first-person motion.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
How first person behaves is set once, on the pawn's AC_FirstPersonSystem (under FirstPerson in the Details panel), and applies to every body:

Setting Category Use First Person Mode First Person > General See Modes. Enable First Person First Person > General Off: FirstPerson is removed from the available perspectives and no first-person meshes are built. Read at start. Default Setup First Person > Setup The pawn's own PDA_FirstPersonSetup (DA_FirstPersonSetup_UEFN for the UEFN mannequin). Third Person Mesh Name First Person > Setup The pawn's body Skeletal Mesh Component to copy from (SkeletalMesh on the Mover pawn, CharacterMesh0 on the CMC pawn; empty in the class default). Empty or not found: the first Skeletal Mesh Component that is not a generated first-person mesh. First Person Arm Pitch Down Limit / Up Limit First Person > Arms Degrees the arms follow the view before the spine leans (45 / 90). First Person Camera Follow Lean First Person > Camera How much the camera follows the spine lean looking down (0 stays, 1 follows; 0.75). First Person Full Body View First Person > Camera How much of the view pitch the arms follow before the spine takes the rest (1). First Person Camera Vertical Smoothing First Person > Camera How quickly the camera height follows the body (12; lower = softer crouches and landings). First Person Max Root Yaw Lag First Person > Camera Degrees the body may lag behind the view before it turns (60). First Person Motion Profile / Intensity First Person > Motion See Hand and item motion. Debug First Person Motion First Person > Debug Draws the motion pivot and targets and prints the motion inputs on screen (false).

The settings are read from the pawn's component, so set them on the AC_FirstPersonSystem component of both sample pawns (SandboxCharacter_Mover and SandboxCharacter_CMC), or on each pawn you use. All settings are listed in the First person reference.

What to draw is set per body, in its PDA_FirstPersonSetup asset:

Field Category Use Full Meshes First Person > Setup > Meshes Meshes for the overlay and true modes. First = lead. Use headless meshes when you have them. Arms Meshes / Body Meshes First Person > Setup > Meshes Meshes for the Split mode. Retargeter First Person > Setup > Retarget IK Retargeter from the UEFN mannequin to this skeleton. Needed by the overlay modes on non-UEFN skeletons; without it the body uses TrueFirstPerson. Eye Offset First Person > Setup > Camera Camera point relative to the head bone, in mesh space at the reference pose (X right, Y forward, Z up, cm). UEFN (0,0,0); Manny, Quinn, Kellan (0,12,0). Camera Bone First Person > Setup > Camera Bone the first-person camera attaches to (VB Camera). Head Bone First Person > Setup > Camera Head bone, hidden when the third-person mesh is reused as the lead, and the reference for the eye offset and ADS (head). Pipeline Anim Class (advanced) First Person > Setup > Advanced Anim Blueprint of the lead mesh (ABP_FirstPerson_UEFN). Replace it with a child to extend the first-person pipeline. Empty = default. Retarget Host Anim Class (advanced) First Person > Setup > Advanced Anim Blueprint used when the pipeline class cannot run on the lead's skeleton (ABP_FirstPerson_Host). Empty = default. Mesh Suffix (advanced) First Person > Setup > Advanced Suffix that pairs a first-person mesh with its third-person component for material copies (_FP). Empty = _FP.

For retargeted characters, duplicate DA_FirstPersonSetup_Manny and set it as the character's First Person Setup (see Add a retargeted character). Recipes are in Configure first person.

docs.title: Skeleton requirements
docs.text:
• A VB Camera virtual bone from root to head (add it in the Skeleton editor: right-click root > Add Virtual Bone > head, then rename it VB Camera). The retargeter does not animate virtual bones, so GASPALS writes it from the body's head in CR_FirstPerson_BodyCamera. Camera Bone in the setup can name another bone, but the first-person Control Rigs place the bone named VB Camera at the eyes, so keep that name when you can.
  • A head bone. Head Bone in the setup changes which bone is hidden and checked, but the first-person Control Rigs still use head.
  • For the overlay modes: UE-standard spine, clavicle and neck names (spine_01..spine_05, clavicle_l/r, neck_01).
  • The UE5 mannequin and MetaHuman skeletons shipped with GASPALS have all of these.

Missing pieces are reported on screen for the local player, in orange, starting with GASPALS First Person (<body name>). See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Cover, traversal and ragdoll in first person
docs.text:
• Cover: sticky cover switches to third person by default; auto cover gives wall-hug movement while the body follows the camera. See Cover system.
  • Traversal: during a traversal move in first person, the view turns toward the obstacle when it is more than 15 degrees off (First Person Traversal Turn Speed and First Person Traversal Turn Threshold on AC_TraversalLogic; see Traversal system).
  • Ragdoll: the camera switches to Camera Perspective During Ragdoll (ThirdPerson by default) while the character ragdolls and back afterwards, when that view is allowed (see Ragdoll camera).

docs.title: Using first person from Blueprints
docs.text:
Other systems talk to the pawn's AC_FirstPersonSystem through BPI_FirstPersonSystem (call the interface function on the component; no cast needed):

Function Use IsFirstPersonEnabled True when Enable First Person is on. GetFirstPersonCameraBoneName The bone the camera follows in first person. IsUsingFirstPersonScale True in FirstPersonOverlaySplit (the arms scale rig applies). CreateItemFirstPersonCopies / RemoveItemFirstPersonCopies First-person copies of a held actor's meshes; remove them before destroying the actor. The equipment system already does this for its items.

To know whether the camera is in first person, ask the camera system (see Using the camera from Blueprints). A visual override that is not a child of BP_RetargetedCharacter_Base gives its first-person setup by implementing BPI_FirstPersonCharacter (GetFirstPersonSetup) and its body mesh by implementing BPI_VisualOverride (GetVisualBodyMesh).

docs.title: Networking
docs.text: First-person meshes exist only for the owning player's view; other players see the third-person character. The camera perspective is sent to the server, so the server knows which representation the owner uses. Nothing else in the first-person pipeline replicates.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• TrueFirstPerson: weapons can clip into walls (no first-person scale), and the weapon follows the third-person aim with a frame of delay.
  • FirstPersonOverlaySplit: the body is not scaled, so it receives the hidden third-person body's shadow.
  • EUB_SplitFirstPersonMesh gives a usable first cut; hand-authored arm and body meshes look cleaner, especially with dense clothing.
  • Only the rifle, pistol, revolver and bow have first-person overlay poses.
  • Cost: the first-person Anim Blueprint copies and re-poses a full body. One extra IK retarget runs for the overlay on retargeted characters.

docs.title: Movement
docs.text: This page covers how the pawns move: gaits and rotation modes (both pawns), the Mover movement modes and transitions, and the slide. The animation side is in Animation pipeline.

docs.title: Input state
docs.text:
Both pawns keep an input state (S_PlayerInputState): WantsToSprint (hold Shift), WantsToWalk (toggle Ctrl), WantsToStrafe (toggle middle mouse), WantsToAim (hold Right Button), WantsToCrouch (toggle C). Movement, animation and camera are derived from it. Each of these five can be switched between hold and toggle per pawn (Toggle Crouch, Toggle Walk, Toggle Sprint, Toggle Aim, Toggle Strafe, in GASPALS > Input > Hold Toggle). Gamepad buttons are in Controls.

On the Mover pawn, crouch only toggles on the ground or while sliding. Pressing sprint while crouched stands up.

docs.title: Gait
docs.text:
Gait When (Mover pawn) Sprint Sprint on, not aiming, and (while strafing) the input is within Sprint Max Angle from Facing of the facing direction. Walk Walk on, or a small stick deflection (with the default DDCvar.AnalogInputStyle 1: below 0.7). Run Otherwise.

In cover the gait is Walk (unless crouched), and during a cover run it is Sprint.

The CMC pawn decides in GetDesiredGait: Sprint when sprint is on, the stick counts as full input and (unless the character orients to movement) the input is within Sprint Max Angle from Facing of the facing; otherwise Walk when walk is on or the stick is not at full input; otherwise Run. Movement Stick Mode (Input) decides what full input is: the default Fixed Speed - Single Gait treats any deflection as full, the two Walk / Run modes compare it with Analog Walk/ Run Threshold (0.7).

Sprint Max Angle from Facing (on the pawn, GASPALS > Movement > Sprint): the Mover pawn has one angle per DDCvar.StrafeStyle (60 / 95.7 / 95.7 degrees), the CMC pawn one value (50). Raise it to let the character sprint sideways while strafing.

docs.title: Rotation mode
docs.text:
Mode When The character faces OrientToMovement Default in third person Where it moves Strafe Strafe toggled on, in first person, while auto-strafing, or near a targeted actor The camera direction (the target when locked on) Aim Aim held The aim direction

The camera uses the same mode to pick its Free, Strafe or Aim rig.

Auto-strafe (GASPALS > Strafe on both pawns, off by default): with Auto Strafe Enabled, the character strafes while the player looks around and orients to movement again Auto Strafe Delay (1 s) after the look input stops. It works in third person on both pawns, and also in the top-down and side-scroller views on the Mover pawn. It only matters while strafe is toggled off; the CMC pawn starts strafing. On the CMC pawn the state is sent to the server with the rest of the input state, so other players see the same facing.

Target lock: actors that call AddTarget / RemoveTarget on the pawn (the /GASPALS/Levels/LevelPrototyping/TargetDummy does on overlap) can be locked on; the nearest one is marked with a red cone and the character keeps facing it, out of cover. Both pawns support it; the CMC pawn turns toward the target at Target Lock Interp Speed (GASPALS > Targeting, 10).

docs.title: Speeds
docs.text:
Mover pawnCMC pawn

Set on the Walking mode instance of the pawn's CharacterMover component: select the component in the pawn Blueprint, find Movement Modes in the Details panel and expand the Walking entry (category Blueprint Overrides (Change These)). The class defaults are on BP_MovementMode_Walking; a value changed on the pawn's instance wins over them.

Setting Default Walk Speed / Walk Acceleration 165 / 500 Run Speed / Run Acceleration 375 / 800 Sprint Speed / Sprint Acceleration 585 / 300 Crouch Speed 165 Walk/ Run Turn Strength / Sprint Turn Strength 8 / 4 Gait Change Deceleration / Stopping Deceleration 300 / 1000 Walk/ Run Facing Time / Sprint Facing Time / Idle Facing Time 0.4 / 0.8 / 0.2 (the Mover pawn's instance uses 0.1 for walk/run and idle)

The Cover mode (a child of Walking) moves at 150 (walk) and 250 (run and sprint), with Gait Change Deceleration 1500.

Right after landing the Walking mode brakes with Just Landed Deceleration (20000) for Just Landed Duration (0.2 s), so the character doesn't slide (GASPALS > Movement > Landing). The Cover mode uses the same values. The Falling mode turns at most Falling Rotation Rate (300 degrees per second, GASPALS > Movement > Falling). It only matters while the pawn faces the camera (strafing, aiming or first person): without strafing, the Mover pawn keeps its take-off facing in the air by design, whatever the rate.

Set on the pawn (class defaults, category Movement). Each is a vector: forward, strafe, backward speed, blended by direction with Curve_StrafeSpeedMap while strafing. Walk Speeds Demo, Run Speeds Demo and Sprint Speeds Demo in the same category are not used.

Setting Forward, strafe, backward Walk Speeds 200, 180, 150 Run Speeds 500, 350, 300 Sprint Speeds 700, 700, 700 Crouch Speeds 225, 200, 180

UpdateMovement_PreCMC writes the resulting max speed, acceleration, braking and friction into the Character Movement Component every frame, before it moves, so change them on the pawn (GASPALS > Movement > CMC), not on the component:

Setting Default Gait Max Acceleration 800, 800, 300 (walk, run, sprint at top speed) Sprint Acceleration Speed Range 300 to 700 (sprint acceleration eases from the run value to the sprint value over this speed range) Gait Ground Friction 5, 5, 3 Sprint Ground Friction Speed Range 0 to 500 Braking Deceleration 500 with movement input, 2000 when stopping (also in cover) Stopping Braking Friction 3 Falling Rotation Rate 200 degrees per second (the CMC pawn turns toward its input in the air, also without strafing)

docs.title: Mover movement modes
docs.text:
Registered on CharacterMover > Movement Modes of the Mover pawn:

Name Class Use Walking BP_MovementMode_Walking (Smooth Walking) Ground movement with gait speeds, turning and facing. Falling BP_MovementMode_Falling Air: air control 0.5. Flying B_MovementMode_Flying Traversal moves, debug flying (max speed 1000). Sliding BP_MovementMode_Slide Slide. Cover BP_MovementMode_Cover Along cover (see Cover). Traversing Flying (native) Registered but not used. Ragdoll BP_MovementMode_Ragdoll Physics ragdoll (X); see Ragdoll and interactions.

The mode and transition classes are in /GASPALS/Blueprints/MovementModes. The pawn holds its own instance of every mode, so a value changed on that instance only affects that pawn, and a later change to the class default does not reach a value the instance overrides.

Shared settings: legacy movement settings (max step height 30, perch radius 20) and stance settings (crouched half height 60). Sync Inputs For Sim Proxy is on, so remote characters receive the inputs for animation.

The pawn's Movement Mode Map translates mode names into the animation's movement modes (E_MovementMode): Cover counts as on ground, Sliding as sliding, and so on.

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text:
Transition Where Condition BP_MovementTransition_SuggestedMode Global Applies a mode requested in the input (ragdoll enter and exit). BP_MovementTransition_Cover Global Walking to Cover and back, from the cover input. BP_MovementTransition_ToSlide Walking and Cover modes Speed over Slide Enter Speed (380), crouching, not in cover, cooldown over. BP_MovementTransition_FromSlide Sliding mode Not crouching, or speed at or below Slide Exit Speed (200). Returns to Walking.

Transitions are instanced per mode: each mode carries its own copy.

docs.title: Slide
docs.text:
Sprint, then crouch: the Mover pawn slides. BP_MovementMode_Slide is a smooth walking mode whose speed and deceleration depend on the slope. Its settings are on the Sliding entry of the pawn's CharacterMover > Movement Modes (class defaults on BP_MovementMode_Slide; categories Blueprint Overrides (Change These) and GASPALS > Movement > Slide):

Setting Default Initial Boost Time / Initial Boost Speed / Initial Boost Acceleration 0.2 s / 800 / 2000 After Boost Acceleration 300 Steep Slope Angle / Shallow Slope Angle 40 / 10 degrees Steep Slope Speed / Shallow Slope Speed / Flat Ground Speed 800 / 500 / 100 Steep Slope Deceleration / Flat Ground Deceleration 2000 / 500 Slide Cooldown 0.75 s Slide Enter Speed / Slide Exit Speed 380 / 200

The slide starts when the speed is over Slide Enter Speed (380; running forward is about 375, so it needs a sprint), the character crouches, is not in cover, and the cooldown is over. It ends when the character stands up (crouch again, sprint or jump) or slows to Slide Exit Speed (200). The transitions read both speeds from the Slide mode.

Slide Cooldown stops crouch-tapping from restarting the slide with a fresh boost: a new slide can start only 0.75 s after the last one started or ended (0 turns the cooldown off). It is measured in Mover simulation time, so the server and the predicting client agree.

The CMC pawn has no slide.

docs.title: Debug
docs.text:
• p.VisualizeMovement 1 shows the movement state.
  • On the Mover pawn, Z (keyboard only) toggles a debug flying mode (debug tools).

docs.title: Overlay system
docs.text:
An overlay is a pose layered on top of locomotion. The legs keep walking, running and turning with motion matching; the overlay decides how the upper body is held: a rifle at the ready, a torch held up, a box carried in both arms, hands tied, an injured stance. This is the layering approach of the Advanced Locomotion System (ALS), on the Game Animation Sample.

There are two independent overlays:

  • Overlay pose: what the character holds or how it holds itself. Item poses come from the equipment system; stance poses (Default, Injured, HandsTied) from the overlay menu.
  • Overlay body: a body style applied to the whole figure: Default, Masculine, Feminine.
Folder /GASPALS/Systems/OverlaySystem Component AC_OverlaySystem (on both pawns) Interface BPI_OverlaySystem (RefreshOverlayPose, used by the equipment system) Layer interfaces OverlayPose/ALI_OverlayPose, OverlayBody/ALI_OverlayBody, FirstPerson/ALI_OverlayFirstPerson Pose Anim Blueprints OverlayPose/ABP_OverlayPose_Base and children OverlayPose/<Name>/ABP_Overlay_<Name> Body Anim Blueprints OverlayBody/ABP_OverlayBody_Base and children OverlayBody/<Style>/ABP_OverlayBody_<Style> (Default, Masculine, Feminine) First-person poses FirstPerson/ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Base and children (Rifle, Pistol2H, Pistol1H, Bow) Data Data/Struct_OverlayCurves (pose + curve map), OverlayPose/Enum_OverlayPose, OverlayBody/Enum_OverlayBody Blending ABP_LayerBlending (linked into both character Anim Blueprints) Menus UI/OverlayPose/W_Switcher_Pose, UI/OverlayBody/W_Switcher_Body Input V or gamepad Menu (hold, pose menu), B (hold, body menu, keyboard only), mouse wheel / D-pad up / down to move the highlight.
