docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The character Anim Blueprints call two linked anim layers, OverlayPose and OverlayBody. Which Anim Blueprint implements them is decided at runtime with Link Anim Class Layers on the character mesh:

  • AC_OverlaySystem links the class its Overlay Pose Layers map gives for the selected stance (ABP_Overlay_Default, _Injured, _HandsTied), and the class from Overlay Body Layers for the body (ABP_OverlayBody_<Style>). A value with no row keeps the current layer and prints an orange warning.
  • AC_EquipmentSystem links the item's pose (ABP_Overlay_Rifle...) from its data asset.

The last link wins: equipping an item replaces a stance pose, and choosing a stance in the menu replaces the item pose. With nothing in hand (Unequip), the equipment system applies the selected stance instead of a pose of its own, so an Overlay Pose set on the pawn's component shows at spawn and comes back when the item is put away.

Overlay changes are instant (no transition animation plays). Each linked Anim Blueprint outputs a pose; ABP_LayerBlending blends it onto locomotion per body part using curves. See Animation pipeline for where this sits in the full graph.

The pawn sets the component up at start (Overlay_Initialize > InitializeSystem with the third-person mesh). The component can be turned off with Enable Overlay or deleted from the pawn; see System switches.

docs.title: Pose Anim Blueprints
docs.text:
ABP_OverlayPose_Base holds the logic; its children only hold data. A state machine (SM_OverlayPose) chooses between three states:

State Meaning Enters when Relaxed Item lowered Start state. From Ready: when sprinting, after Ready Hold Time Moving (2 s) in Ready while moving, or after Ready Hold Time Idle (3 s) in Ready. Ready Item raised, not aiming From Relaxed: aim pressed (and not sprinting). From Aiming: aim released or sprint, after at least Aim Min Time (0.75 s) of aiming. Aiming Aiming From Ready: aim held, once Ready is a quarter blended in.

With Can Aim off (box, barrel, default and the stance poses), the machine stays in Relaxed. Within each state, the pose is picked by stance (stand, crouch) and speed:

Variable (class defaults of the child) Used for Stand_Relax_Idle, _Walk, _Run, Stand_Relax_Sprint Standing, relaxed Stand_Ready_Idle, _Walk, _Run Standing, ready Stand_Aim_Idle, _Walk, _Run Standing, aiming Crouch_Relax_Idle, _Move; Crouch_Ready_Idle, _Move; Crouch_Aim_Idle, _Move Crouched Stand_Aim_Sweep, Crouch_Aim_Sweep Additive aim sweep: arms up and down with the aim pitch

Each pose variable is a Struct_OverlayCurves with two fields: Overlay Pose (an animation) and Curve Map (curve name to value). The Anim Blueprint plays the animation's first frame as a still pose, so a single-frame animation is enough. It writes the curve map onto the pose, and ABP_LayerBlending reads those curves.

docs.title: Curves
docs.text:
The curve map decides how much of the body each pose takes over. Names are lowercase:

Curve 0 1 layering_legs, layering_pelvis Locomotion legs and pelvis Overlay legs and pelvis (carry stances) layering_spine Locomotion spine Overlay spine layering_spine_add No additive Locomotion spine motion added on top layering_head, layering_head_add Locomotion head Overlay head / additive layering_arm_l, layering_arm_r Locomotion arm Overlay arm layering_arm_l_add, layering_arm_r_add No additive Arm swing added on top of the overlay arm layering_arm_l_ls, layering_arm_r_ls Arm in mesh space (keeps its aim while the spine moves) Arm in local space (follows the spine) layering_hand_l, layering_hand_r Locomotion fingers Overlay fingers enable_handik_l, enable_handik_r Hand IK off Hand IK to the item's HandIK socket enable_cr_aimoffset Aim offset rig off Aim offset rig on disable_cr_aimoffset_pitch, _yaw Axis on Axis off

A curve that neither the map nor the animation sets is 0. Two shipped examples:

  • Rifle, ready (Stand_Ready_Idle): layering_pelvis, layering_spine, layering_spine_add, layering_head_add, both arms, both hands and layering_legs at 1; layering_arm_r_ls 0.5; enable_handik_l 1 (support hand on the handguard). The head, the arm additives and layering_arm_l_ls stay at 0.
  • Box (every pose), Injured and HandsTied: layering_pelvis, layering_spine, layering_spine_add, layering_head, both arms, both arms' _ls, both hands and layering_legs at 1; layering_head_add 0.5; no arm additives and no hand IK.

docs.title: Aim sweep
docs.text:
While aiming, the arms follow the camera pitch through the aim sweep additive, blended by AimSweepValue (the pitch from +90 to -90 degrees mapped to 0..1). Aim Sweep Interp Speed Local (0) and Remote (10) set how fast it follows on the owning machine and on others. 0 means no interpolation: the owning player's arms follow the camera pitch exactly (interpolating there makes the weapon lag behind the view and step while turning). See Animation pipeline.

An aim sweep animation (for example OverlayPose/Rifle/AO_Rifle_Stand_Sweep) is 1 second long: aiming straight up at the start, level in the middle, straight down at the end. AimSweepValue is the time it is sampled at. Its additive settings are Additive Anim Type Mesh Space and Base Pose Type Selected animation frame (the middle, level frame).

docs.title: Body Anim Blueprints
docs.text: ABP_OverlayBody_Base picks one of four poses by stance and movement: Pose Stand Idle, Pose Stand Move, Pose Crouch Idle, Pose Crouch Move. The children set those four animations: ABP_OverlayBody_Default uses BasePoses/Pose_Base_Stand and Pose_Base_Crouch; Masculine and Feminine use their own Pose_<Style>_Stand and Pose_<Style>_Crouch (one pose for idle and moving).

docs.title: First-person poses
docs.text: ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Base has the same pose variables (without the aim sweeps) for the first-person arms, with curves for the first-person rigs. The equipment data's Overlay Pose FP links it. See First person.

docs.title: The menus
docs.text:
Hold V (pose) or B (body): the world slows to Menu Time Dilation (0.35), the Overlay Pose Menu Widget Class / Overlay Body Menu Widget Class opens with one entry per enum value, mouse wheel up or D-pad up moves the highlight up the list and down moves it down (wrapping at the ends), and releasing the key selects it. As with the equipment menu, the component keeps the highlight (HighlightedOverlayPose / HighlightedOverlayBody) and the widgets only read it, so a replacement widget only has to display it. The entries come from Enum_OverlayPose (Default, Injured, HandsTied) and Enum_OverlayBody (Default, Masculine, Feminine); a new enum entry appears automatically.

If the pawn is destroyed while a menu is open, the component's EndPlay calls CloseOverlayMenus: it closes both menus, removes their widgets and sets the world speed back to normal.

docs.title: Shipped overlays
docs.text:
Overlay pose Can aim First-person version ABP_Overlay_Default no ABP_Overlay_Injured no ABP_Overlay_HandsTied no ABP_Overlay_Rifle yes ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Rifle ABP_Overlay_Pistol1H yes ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Pistol1H ABP_Overlay_Pistol2H yes ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Pistol2H ABP_Overlay_Bow yes ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Bow ABP_Overlay_Torch yes ABP_Overlay_Binoculars yes ABP_Overlay_Box no ABP_Overlay_Barrel no

ABP_Overlay_Default sets no pose and no curves, so it adds nothing: plain locomotion. Injured holds one hand to the side and HandsTied keeps the hands behind the back. Their relaxed standing poses use Pose_Injured_Stand / Pose_HandsTied_Stand and their relaxed crouch poses Pose_Injured_Crouch / Pose_HandsTied_Crouch, with the same layering curve values as the box. They are complete examples of a stance overlay: see Add an overlay state. Pistol1H is the one-handed pose set of the Revolver item.

docs.title: Animation modifiers
docs.text: AnimModifiers/ holds four animation modifiers for authoring: Create_LayeringCurves keys every layering curve (value 1) on an animation, Copy_Curves and Copy_Curves_Pose copy curves from another animation, and Create_Curves creates curves from parameters. Apply them from the animation's Animation Modifiers window. The shipped overlays use curve maps instead, so the modifiers are optional: use them if you prefer layering curves authored in the animations.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Where Setting Default AC_OverlaySystem Enable Overlay true. Off: the pawn keeps the default pose and body and the overlay menus do nothing. Read at start. AC_OverlaySystem Overlay Pose Default (the starting stance) AC_OverlaySystem Overlay Body Default (the starting body style) AC_OverlaySystem Overlay Pose Layers Default, Injured, HandsTied > their ABP_Overlay_* AC_OverlaySystem Overlay Body Layers Default, Masculine, Feminine > their ABP_OverlayBody_* AC_OverlaySystem Overlay Pose Menu Widget Class / Overlay Body Menu Widget Class W_Switcher_Pose / W_Switcher_Body AC_OverlaySystem Menu Time Dilation 0.35 (world speed while a menu is open; 1 = no slow motion) ABP_OverlayPose_Base and its children Can Aim per overlay (see Shipped overlays) ABP_OverlayPose_Base and its children Ready Hold Time Idle / Moving, Aim Min Time 3 / 2 / 0.75 s. A very large hold time keeps the item raised. ABP_OverlayPose_Base and its children Aim Sweep Interp Speed Local / Remote 0 / 10 Pose children pose variables and aim sweeps per overlay Body children the four body poses per style

The component settings are under Overlay in the Details panel of the component (select AC_OverlaySystem in the pawn Blueprint); the Anim Blueprint settings are in each child's Class Defaults.

docs.title: Networking
docs.text: Overlay Pose and Overlay Body are replicated with RepNotify. The owner changes them locally and sends a reliable Server RPC; every machine links the Anim Blueprints in the RepNotify. Test with a listen server and a client (see Networking).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The menus slow the whole world while open. Time dilation is global: on a listen server, the host's menu slows every player.
  • An item's pose replaces the stance while the item is held (see How it works).
  • The stance poses (Default, Injured, HandsTied) and the item poses share the pose layer, so a stance and an item cannot be combined.
  • Adding a value to Enum_OverlayPose needs a row in Overlay Pose Layers (otherwise the warning OverlayPoseLayers has no anim layer class for the selected OverlayPose shows and the layer is unchanged).
  • Variables added to ABP_OverlayPose_Base do not reach existing children's class defaults: set them on each child.
  • All overlay animations are authored on the UEFN mannequin skeleton; other characters copy or retarget the final pose (see Characters and visual overrides).

docs.title: Ragdoll and interactions
docs.text:
GASPALS has two ragdoll implementations, one per pawn type, with the same input on both:

CMC pawn Mover pawn Pawn SandboxCharacter_CMC SandboxCharacter_Mover Implementation AC_RagdollSystem component A Mover movement mode (BP_MovementMode_Ragdoll) plus a Physics Control component Input X ragdolls; on a floor, X or Space gets up X ragdolls; on a floor, X or Space gets up Entry Keeps the movement momentum (Inherited Velocity Scale); the legs collide with each other The Ragdoll physics profile; the legs collide with each other Get-up Get-up animation chosen from the pose (front, back) and the held item Get-up animation chosen from the pose (front, back, rolling) Physical animation No Off by default (kinematic); DDCVar.CharacterPhysics.DefaultProfile 1 turns it on Characters without a player Get up by themselves once the body has rested for Auto Get Up Delay (3 seconds) (below) Get up by themselves once the body has rested for about 3 seconds Interactions No Takedowns and shoves between characters; demo shooting and spawning (debug tools) Level Any (DefaultLevel starts on the CMC pawn) Any (N switches to the Mover pawn in DefaultLevel); RagdollLevel has targets and obstacles

On both pawns the gamepad uses D-pad right to ragdoll and D-pad right or A to get up (Controls). While a character ragdolls, the camera system switches to its ragdoll view (see Camera).

docs.title: CMC ragdoll (AC_RagdollSystem)
docs.text:
/GASPALS/Systems/RagdollSystem/AC_RagdollSystem. Press X (IA_Ragdoll) to ragdoll. While ragdolling, X again or Space (the pawn's jump input) gets up, through RequestGetUp (see Get-up input): only once the body rests on a floor.

Start: the owner calls StartRagdoll, which asks the server (Server_StartRagdoll) to multicast it to everyone. Each machine stops montages, turns the capsule's collision off, switches the mesh to physics (Ragdoll profile, simulating the bodies below the pelvis), applies the entry physics (ApplyEntryPhysics, below), and sets the movement mode to none. OnRagdollStarted fires.

Entry physics: right after the bodies start simulating, and before the movement mode is cleared, the bodies get the pawn's velocity times Inherited Velocity Scale, so a running character keeps its momentum instead of dropping in place, and collision is turned on between the left and right leg bodies so the legs don't pass through each other (the Mover ragdoll profile does the same for the legs). Settings on AC_RagdollSystem (Ragdoll > Entry), set per pawn because the bone names depend on the skeleton:

Setting Default Use Inherited Velocity Scale 1.0 Share of the movement velocity the ragdoll starts with. 1 keeps the momentum, 0 drops in place. Left Leg Bones thigh_l, calf_l, foot_l Bodies of the left leg. Right Leg Bones thigh_r, calf_r, foot_r Bodies of the right leg; each collides with each left leg body.

Stop: StopRagdoll reverses it the same way and fires OnRagdollEnded. Each machine turns physics off and puts the mesh back where it sat on the capsule when the ragdoll started (CacheMeshTransform / RestoreMeshTransform: the simulated pelvis drags the mesh away during the ragdoll). The capsule and mesh get back the collision settings they had when the ragdoll started (cached by CacheCollisionState), so a pawn with its own collision setup keeps it. On the ground the pawn walks again and plays a get-up montage picked from the pose (lying on the back or the front) and the held item (Ragdoll > Get Up settings: Default, right hand, left hand, two hands). The get-up keys only work on a floor; when your own Blueprint calls StopRagdoll directly in the air, the pawn falls with the body's last velocity.

While ragdolling the CMC accepts the client's position, so the capsule follows the body without corrections. The component tells the pawn's other components through BPI_RagdollSystemListener; the camera system uses it to switch to the ragdoll view. Enable Ragdoll (Ragdoll > General) turns the system off, and the component can be removed from the pawn (Turning systems on and off).

docs.title: Automatic get-up
docs.text:
A CMC character that no player controls (a placed character, an AI) gets up by itself. On the server, while it ragdolls, the component adds up the time the pelvis moves slower than Auto Get Up Max Speed and, after Auto Get Up Delay, calls RequestGetUp. If the body is not on a floor yet, it tries again after another delay. Player characters wait for the get-up input. Settings on AC_RagdollSystem (Ragdoll > Get Up):

Setting Default Use Auto Get Up true Off: characters without a player stay down until something calls RequestGetUp (below). Auto Get Up Delay 3 Seconds the body must rest before getting up. Auto Get Up Max Speed 10 Pelvis speed (cm/s) under which the body counts as resting.

Settings and functions: Ragdoll reference.

docs.title: Mover ragdoll
docs.text:
SandboxCharacter_Mover is the player pawn of RagdollLevel (game mode GM_Sandbox_Ragdoll), and it is the Mover pawn of every other level too: the ragdoll, takedowns and debug tools work wherever it plays. It has:

  • a Physics Control component (PhysicsControl, with the Physics Control asset PCA_SandboxCharacter in /GASPALS/Characters/UEFN_Mannequin/Rigs): when not ragdolling, DDCVar.CharacterPhysics.DefaultProfile picks kinematic (0, default: the body plays the animation exactly) or physical animation (1: every limb is a simulated body pulled toward the animation, so it reacts to contacts, but hands and arms can catch on walls, for example in cover). The value is read again whenever it changes, so you can try it from the console during play. An AC_PostABPTick helper updates the ragdoll strengths from animation curves right after the Anim Blueprint runs.
  • the Ragdoll movement mode and the BP_MovementTransition_SuggestedMode transition;
  • interactions with other characters (takedowns, shoves);
  • the debug tools component (AC_DebugTools): demo shot, spawn or rotate characters, teleport, fly.

Its settings and functions are in the Pawns reference (Ragdoll categories).

docs.title: Entering and leaving ragdoll
docs.text:
1. X (IA_Ragdoll), when not ragdolling, calls TriggerRagdoll. On the owner it writes a ragdoll request into the Mover input, and the suggested-mode transition switches to the Ragdoll mode inside the simulation, so the owner and the server agree. (A server ragdolling a character it doesn't control, such as another player or a character without a player, queues the mode directly.)
  2. Every machine applies the ragdoll look when the mode changes: physics on, the Ragdoll physics profile.
  3. While ragdolling, the owner can roll the body with the move input; the roll travels in the input too. On slopes steeper than about 20 degrees the body also rolls downhill by itself. Remote ragdolls are pulled toward the replicated capsule so they stay in sync.
  4. X again or Space leaves the ragdoll once the body rests on a floor (RequestGetUp: the Ragdoll mode and HasFloor, then ExitRagdoll); a press in mid-air does nothing. Entering and leaving ragdoll put the capsule back on the collision profile the pawn was built with (GetDefaultCapsuleProfile, CharacterCapsule in the sample), which also clears a takedown's collision override. The owner picks a get-up montage from the body's pose (lying on the back or the front, rolling) and sends it in the input; the server and the owner play it.

A Mover character that no player controls (a placed target, a spawned character) gets up by itself: once its body is nearly still, it waits 3 seconds and, if the body is still resting, calls ExitRagdoll.

When the ragdoll starts and ends, the pawn tells its components through BPI_RagdollSystemListener, as AC_RagdollSystem does on the CMC pawn; the camera system uses it for the ragdoll view.

docs.title: Physics Control asset
docs.text: The PhysicsControl component names its Physics Control Asset through a soft reference only, so in a packaged game the asset can be garbage-collected and the physics profiles (kinematic, physical animation, Ragdoll) stop applying. At BeginPlay the pawn loads whatever asset the component names and keeps it in the runtime variable Loaded Physics Control Asset (LoadedPhysicsControlAsset). If you copy the Physics Control setup into your own pawn, keep a hard reference to the loaded asset the same way.

docs.title: Settling
docs.text:
The ragdoll's arms are pulled toward the animated pose, which keeps moving while the body lies still, so the hands would keep shaking. Once the body has stayed slower than Ragdoll Settle Speed for Ragdoll Settle Delay, the physics control strengths fade to zero over Ragdoll Settle Blend Time; when the body moves again (pushed, shot, rolled) they come back four times faster.

Settings on SandboxCharacter_Mover (GASPALS > Ragdoll > Settle):

Setting Default Use Ragdoll Settle Speed 15 Body speed (cm/s) below which the ragdoll counts as still. Ragdoll Settle Delay 0.3 Seconds below that speed before the strengths start fading. Ragdoll Settle Blend Time 0.5 Seconds to fade the strengths to zero (coming back takes a quarter of it).

docs.title: Takedowns and shoves
docs.text:
Near another Mover character, without aiming:

Input Action Left Button (IA_Takedown, gamepad RT) Takedown: a paired takedown animation on both characters. E (IA_Interact, gamepad Y) Shove.

A character can be the target when it is a Mover character within 2 m, in front of you (within 60 degrees), with nothing in between, and walking on the ground. You must be on the ground with no montage playing. The victim's animation puts it into ragdoll partway through, and it gets up as usual. With aim held (Right Button or LT), the same keys are the debug tools' shot and spawn.

The interaction is matched with multi-character motion matching: the best paired animation for both characters' poses and positions is chosen, and both are warped into place. On a client, the initiator plays its part at once and asks the server (Server_TryCharacterInteraction), which checks the victim (walking, not already in a root-motion animation, within 3.5 m) and multicasts the interaction. Each machine sets up the participants (ignored collisions, tick order, the animation contexts the Anim Blueprint uses for constraints).

docs.title: Demo tools
docs.text:
The AC_DebugTools component on the Mover pawn. Hold aim (Right Button), then:

Input Action Left Button Shoot: the character hit goes ragdoll with an impulse. E Spawn a character where you aim, or rotate the one you aim at.

Clients send these to the server with the view; the server traces, applies the ragdoll and multicasts the impulse. Settings (trace distances, impulse, spawn limit, an on/off switch) and the teleport and fly keys are on the Debug tools page.

docs.title: Get-up input
docs.text:
Both pawns get up through BPI_RagdollSystem > RequestGetUp (returns bHandled). It ends the ragdoll and plays the get-up only while the character is ragdolling on a floor, and returns false otherwise, so a press in mid-air does nothing; press again after landing.

CMC pawn Mover pawn Implemented by AC_RagdollSystem (body on the ground) The pawn itself (Ragdoll mode and HasFloor, then ExitRagdoll) X (IA_Ragdoll) The component's input event: ragdolling, RequestGetUp; else start the ragdoll Ragdolling, RequestGetUp; else TriggerRagdoll Space (IA_Jump) The pawn's jump input calls Ragdoll_RequestGetUp, a wrapper that finds the component by class, so the pawn still compiles if the component is deleted In the Ragdoll mode, the jump input calls RequestGetUp

If you implement BPI_RagdollSystem on your own pawn or component, implement RequestGetUp too to support the get-up keys: unimplemented, it returns false and the keys do nothing.

docs.title: Using the ragdoll from Blueprints
docs.text:
Both pawns answer the same interface, BPI_RagdollSystem. Get the object that implements it with Get Ragdoll System (BPFL_GASPALS): on the CMC pawn it returns the AC_RagdollSystem component, on the Mover pawn the pawn itself, and None on an actor without a ragdoll (the interface calls then do nothing).

Call Use RequestRagdoll(bStopActiveMontages, MontageBlendOut, InjuryState) Ragdoll the character. Returns false when the ragdoll system is turned off. InjuryState is an E_RagdollInjuryState value as a byte (None, Head_Face, Head_Back, Stunned, Body_Front, Limp, Groin); the Mover pawn replicates it to its Anim Blueprint, the CMC component ignores it and the blend-out. ApplyRagdollImpulse(BoneName, Impulse) Push one body of the ragdoll. Called on the server, every machine pushes its own copy. The Mover pawn waits up to 1 second for the ragdoll to start, so you can call it right after RequestRagdoll. IsRagdollActive True while the character ragdolls. RequestGetUp Get up, only while ragdolling on a floor (see Get-up input).

Call RequestRagdoll on the server (or on the owning client) in multiplayer: the CMC component starts the ragdoll through a server RPC, which a client can only send for its own pawn.

docs.title: Ragdoll from an animation
docs.text:
The anim notify BP_AnimNotify_TriggerRagdoll (/GASPALS/Blueprints/AnimNotifies) calls RequestRagdoll on the character playing the animation. The takedown and shove victim animations use it. To use it in your own montage:

  1. Open the montage, right-click the Notifies track at the frame where the character should fall, and choose Add Notify > BP_AnimNotify_TriggerRagdoll.
  2. Select the notify. In the Details panel set Stop Active Montages, Montage Blend Out and Ragdoll Injury State (the RequestRagdoll inputs above).
  3. Save the montage, play it on either pawn (for example with Play Montage from your Blueprint), and check that the character falls into ragdoll at that frame and gets up with X or Space once it rests.

docs.title: Physics obstacles
docs.text:
RagdollLevel has moving obstacles (bumpers, hammers, turnstiles, moving platforms, in /GASPALS/Levels/LevelPrototyping/Obstacles) on the Obstacle collision channel, which the Ragdoll profile blocks. Walk into them with physical animation on, or ragdoll into them.

The locally controlled Mover pawn sweeps a sphere from the neck to between the feet every frame; an obstacle hit knocks it into ragdoll. Settings on SandboxCharacter_Mover (GASPALS > Ragdoll > Obstacles):

Setting Default Use Ragdoll on Obstacle Hit true Off: obstacles only push the capsule. Ragdoll Obstacle Object Types Obstacle Object types that knock the pawn over. Ragdoll Obstacle Trace Radius 15 Radius of the sweep in cm.

DDCVar.CharacterPhysics.DrawDebug 1 draws the obstacle sweep and the ragdoll's impact traces (Console variables).

docs.title: Networking summary
docs.text:
Event CMC pawn Mover pawn Start / stop Server RPC, then reliable multicast Mover input request and transition; cosmetics on mode change Roll n/a Mover input Get-up Played on every machine by the stop multicast Montage chosen by the owner, sent in the input, played on server and owner Interactions n/a Client predicts, server validates, reliable multicast Impulse (ApplyRagdollImpulse) Server: reliable multicast, every machine pushes its own copy. Client: local copy only Reliable multicast

Over a listen server, expect one movement correction on the client for each of: a takedown or shove from the host on a client, a shot from the host at a client, the host rotating a client. Ragdoll bodies agree within a few centimeters across machines.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The two implementations are separate: the CMC pawn has no physical animation, settling, roll or interactions. Both get characters without a player back up, each in its own way.
  • Takedowns and shoves are on the Mover pawn only, between Mover characters.
  • The CMC ragdoll simulates the bodies below the pelvis.
  • The Mover ragdoll's bone names are those of the UEFN mannequin; the ragdoll always simulates the pawn's UEFN mesh, also when a retargeted character is shown (Characters).

docs.title: Traversal system
docs.text:
Traversal moves the character over obstacles: vault (over and land on the other side), hurdle (over and keep running), mantle (climb up onto). It is the Game Animation Sample traversal, shared by both pawns and triggered by jump and by vaulting from cover.

Folder /GASPALS/Systems/TraversalSystem Components AC_TraversalLogic (orchestration), AC_TraversalTracer (ledge measurement) Preview actor BP_TraversalTester Choosers /GASPALS/Characters/UEFN_Mannequin/Animations/Traversal/CHT_TraversalMontages_Mover, _CMC Montages Traversal/Vault, Hurdle, Mantle, Climb, Catch folders Collision The Traversable trace channel Input Space / gamepad A (IA_Jump) Settings Traversal reference

docs.title: How a traversal happens
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    J[Jump pressed] --> CV{In cover?}
    CV -->|facing away| Turn[Turn to the wall] --> T
    CV -->|no| T[TryTraversalAction]
    T --> Tr[Capsule trace<br>Traversable channel]
    Tr --> L[Measure ledges<br>AC_TraversalTracer]
    L --> R[Room checks]
    R --> C[Chooser picks montage]
    C --> P[Play montage<br>with motion warping]
    T -->|nothing found| Jmp[Normal jump]
  1. Trigger. Jump calls TryTraversalAction with inputs from the pawn's GetTraversalCheckInputs: a trace forward whose length grows with speed (on the ground) or a short trace (in the air), sized by the Check settings below. In cover, the cover system first turns the character to the wall (RequestCoverVault). Held jump keeps retrying every frame.
  2. Find the obstacle. A capsule trace on the Traversable Trace Channel (the Traversable channel). No hit: the pawn jumps instead (crouched on the Mover pawn: it stands up).
  3. Measure it. AC_TraversalTracer finds the front ledge, checks the width (Min Ledge Width, 70 cm), and finds the back ledge and the floor behind.
  4. Room checks. Capsule traces on the Room Check Trace Channel (Visibility) check the character fits on top of the front ledge and between the ledges. They give the obstacle height and depth, and whether there is a back ledge and a back floor.
  5. Pick the montage. The chooser (CHT_TraversalMontages_Mover or _CMC) gets the action type, ledge data, height, depth, distance, movement mode, gait, speed and the pose history, and returns a montage with a start time and play rate. No match: the pawn jumps.
  6. Play it. The montage plays with motion warping targets FrontLedge, BackLedge and BackFloor, so the animation lands exactly on the measured ledges. During the montage the character ignores the obstacle's collision and moves in flying mode; afterwards it returns to falling (vault) or walking.

docs.title: Mover and CMC
docs.text:
Mover pawn CMC pawn Montage playback Mover's montage support (root motion through the movement modes) Anim instance montage with root motion Movement mode during the move Flying (queued) MOVE_Flying Replication behavior Prediction handles it Client-authoritative position during the move Can traverse when On the ground or in the air, no montage playing, not already traversing Not already traversing Jump while another montage plays Nothing happens (no jump either) Traversal or jump as usual

Set Is Mover Character (Traversal > Setup) on the pawn's AC_TraversalLogic component to match the pawn (on for Mover pawns, off for CMC pawns): it selects the chooser, the montage playback and the movement mode path.

docs.title: Networking
docs.text: The owner predicts: it runs the checks and plays the montage at once, then sends the result to the server (PerformTraversalAction_Server, reliable). The server plays it too, except for a pawn it controls locally (a listen-server host, a standalone player or a server AI), which already started the move itself, so every traversal starts once. Other machines see the montage through the movement component's montage replication. AC_TraversalLogic has Component Replicates on in both sample pawns.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text: Tool Shows DDCvar.Traversal.DrawDebugLevel 1 Ledge points ... 2 Plus the initial trace ... 3 Plus the room checks and printed ledge data DDCvar.Traversal.DrawDebugDuration How long the shapes stay BP_TraversalTester Place it in a level, its forward (X) arrow toward an obstacle: it draws the ledges the tracer finds, in the editor without playing. Initial Trace Distance (600) sets how far it looks. It finds the obstacle with the Pawn collision profile, not the Traversable channel, so it does not tell you whether the obstacle is traversable. Show Trace / Persistent Show Trace on AC_TraversalTracer Tracer debug lines show collision Whether the obstacle's collision matches what you see

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
AC_TraversalTracer (Traversal > Tracer and Traversal > Debug):

Setting Default Use Min Ledge Width 70 Narrowest traversable ledge. Min Front Ledge Depth 37.52 Depth of the width check into the obstacle. Trace Complex true Trace complex collision for the ledges. Show Trace / Persistent Show Trace false Debug drawing.

AC_TraversalLogic (Traversal > General): Enable Traversal (true, read when play starts). Off: Space just jumps, and in cover it does nothing (the cover vault is a traversal).

AC_TraversalLogic (Traversal > Collision, set on each pawn's component):

Setting Default Use Traversable Trace Channel Traversable Channel of the obstacle search. Only geometry that blocks it can be traversed. Room Check Trace Channel Visibility Channel of the three room checks; anything that blocks it stops the move.

AC_TraversalLogic (Traversal > Check): the obstacle search the pawns' GetTraversalCheckInputs builds. The Mover and CMC pawns set their own speed and reach ranges, so change both when tuning.

Setting Default Use Traversal Check Radius 30 Radius of the capsule traced forward. Traversal Check Half Height 60 on the ground, 86 in the air Half height of that capsule. Traversal Check Speed Range / Traversal Check Distance Range Mover 0 to 375 / 75 to 300; CMC 0 to 500 / 75 to 350 On the ground the reach grows with speed: the speed range maps onto the distance range. Traversal Check Air Distance / Traversal Check Air End Offset 75 / (0, 0, 50) Reach and end offset in the air.

AC_TraversalLogic (Traversal > First Person): in first person the view turns toward the obstacle during a traversal, at First Person Traversal Turn Speed (2; 0 leaves the view alone), when it is more than First Person Traversal Turn Threshold (15 degrees) off.

AC_TraversalLogic (Traversal > Setup): Is Mover Character (see Mover and CMC).

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• The project defines the Traversable trace channel (and the TraversalObjectPreset profile): see Project settings. If your project numbers its custom channels differently, pick the channel again by name in Traversable Trace Channel (AC_TraversalLogic).
  • Obstacles must block the Traversable channel. See Make objects traversable.
  • The pawn has an AC_TraversalLogic, an AC_TraversalTracer and a Motion Warping component, with Is Mover Character set to match the pawn.
  • The pawn implements Get_PropertiesForTraversal (BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn: capsule, mesh, motion warping component, movement mode, gait, speed) and has a GetTraversalCheckInputs function that the jump input passes to TryTraversalAction.
  • The montages' motion warping windows must be named FrontLedge, BackLedge and BackFloor.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only geometry on the Traversable channel is considered; everything else is jumped.
  • Very thin or narrow obstacles (under Min Ledge Width) are not traversed.
  • What can be traversed (heights, depths, speeds) is decided by the chooser tables: an obstacle with no matching row is jumped.
  • On the Mover pawn, Jump does nothing while another montage plays on the default slot or a traversal is running.

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text: Each tutorial goes step by step from start to a working result, and ends with how to check it in Play.

docs.title: Characters and animation
docs.text: Tutorial You will Add a retargeted character Bring your own skeletal mesh in, with first person and equipment. Add an equipment item Add a weapon or carried item with its poses, sockets and data. Add an overlay state Create stance poses and body styles, starting from the Injured overlay. Configure first person Pick a mode, set meshes, place the camera at the eyes, add first-person poses. Tune first-person motion Make the hands and items sway, bob and react with motion profiles, per item or per pawn.

docs.title: Levels and gameplay
docs.text: Tutorial You will Set up cover in a level Build cover that works with every cover feature. Configure cover behavior Sticky-only, crouch-only, wall gaps, facing, exits, aim from cover. Make objects traversable Let characters vault, hurdle and mantle your geometry. Customize the camera Change rigs, offsets, styles and the perspective cycle. Add or rebind inputs Rebind keys, add gamepad bindings, add inputs to systems.

docs.title: Your project
docs.text: Tutorial You will Use GASPALS in your own project Set up your game mode, pawn and levels, remove demo features, package. Add the systems to your own pawn Wire every system on a pawn of your own.

docs.title: Customize the camera
docs.text:
The camera is data: Gameplay Cameras rigs chosen by chooser tables, plus settings on the pawn's camera component. Most changes need no Blueprint work. Background: Camera system.

Where things are:

  • Rigs and chooser tables: /GASPALS/Systems/CameraSystem/Rigs (third-person rigs in ThirdPerson/, first-person rigs in FirstPerson/, and so on). Double-click a rig to open it in the Camera Rig Asset editor, select a node in its graph to edit it in the Details panel, then save the rig asset.
  • Component settings: open the pawn Blueprint (/GASPALS/Blueprints/SandboxCharacter_Mover or SandboxCharacter_CMC), select AC_CameraSystem in the Components panel, and use the Details panel under Camera. The full list is in the Camera reference.

Change both pawns

Each sample pawn has its own AC_CameraSystem component. When you change a component setting on one, change it on the other too, or the Mover and CMC pawns will behave differently. Rig and chooser table edits apply to both.

Check what is active

While playing, type GameplayCameras.Debug.Enable 1 in the console (`) to show the active rigs and their parameters, and GameplayCameras.Debug.Enable 0 to hide them.

docs.title: Change distance, field of view or damping for everything
docs.text:
Open ThirdPerson/CameraRig_TP_Base. Its parameters (boom arm offset, camera offset, field of view, forward / lateral / vertical damping) are the shared defaults. The variants (CameraRig_TP_Close_Freecam...) override some of them: check a variant before assuming the base value applies.

The fixed cameras work the same way: TopDown/CameraRig_TopDown_Base and SideScroller/CameraRig_SideScroller_Base, with one variant per style (CameraRig_TD_1 to _4, CameraRig_SS_1 to _4).

Check: play, and compare the view in third person with the change and without it.

docs.title: Change one situation
docs.text:
Each third-person situation has its own rig: CameraRig_TP_<Close|Medium|Far>_<Freecam|Strafe|Aim>. The distance is the style (Close = Style_1, Medium = Style_2, the default, Far = Style_3). The mode is Freecam while the character turns toward its movement, Strafe while it strafes, and Aim while the player aims. For example, to bring the camera closer while aiming at the medium distance, edit CameraRig_TP_Medium_Aim.

Check: play in the default style, hold aim, and compare.

docs.title: Change the crouch, shoulder, cover and movement offsets
docs.text:
The offsets come from Camera Offset Rigs on each pawn's AC_CameraSystem component (category Camera > Rigs). They apply in third person only:

Entry Default rig Default offset Crouch Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_Crouch 50 cm down Right Shoulder Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_Right 100 cm to the side (right shoulder) Cover Low Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_CoverLow 80 cm up behind low cover Cover Edge Left Rig / Right CameraRig_TP_Offset_CoverEdgeLeft / Right 60 cm toward the open side at a wall end In Air Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_InAir 30 cm back, 20 cm up while jumping or falling Sliding Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_Sliding 30 cm down while sliding (Mover pawn) Traversing Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_Traversing 40 cm back while vaulting or climbing Ragdoll Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_Ragdoll 60 cm back, 40 cm up while ragdolling

The offset rigs are in Rigs/ThirdPerson.

  • To tweak an offset for everyone, open the rig and edit the translation of its offset node.
  • To give one character different offsets, duplicate the rig, edit the copy and point that pawn's entry at it.
  • To turn an offset off (for example no crouch drop), clear the entry.
  • The four movement offsets (in air, sliding, traversing, ragdoll) need Pass Movement Mode to Camera on (default). Turn it off to drop all four at once.
  • To turn the cover offsets off without touching the rigs, use Enable Cover Camera Offsets and Enable Cover Shoulder Switch on the cover component (Cover).

Check: play in third person and crouch (or jump, take low cover, and so on): the camera moves by the new offset.

docs.title: Change the first-person field of view
docs.text:
Open FirstPerson/CameraRig_FP_Base and change its field of view. Keep its First Person node: it keeps the first-person meshes out of the third-person body's shadow. For the arm scale of the FirstPersonOverlaySplit mode, edit CameraRig_FP_Scale (or point Camera Offset Rigs > First Person Scale Rig at your own rig).

Check: play, press 1 until the camera is in first person, and compare.

docs.title: Add a camera style
docs.text:
1. Make the rigs for the new style: in Rigs/ThirdPerson, duplicate CameraRig_TP_Medium_Freecam, _Strafe and _Aim, and edit the copies.
  2. Open /GASPALS/Systems/CameraSystem/Data/E_CameraStyle and add an enumerator at the end of the list. Save.
  3. Open Rigs/CHT_CameraRigs_ThirdPerson and add three rows for the new style, one per mode (Free, Strafe, Aim), each with the ThirdPerson perspective like the existing rows, pointing at your three rigs. Save.
  4. If the style should change the fixed cameras too, add a row to Rigs/CHT_CameraRigs_TopDown and Rigs/CHT_CameraRigs_SideScroller (duplicate a CameraRig_TD_* / CameraRig_SS_* rig for it). Without these rows, the top-down and side-scroller views have no rig for the new style; the third-person table falls back to CameraRig_TP_Medium_Freecam and first person ignores the style.

The style input (2) cycles through every entry of E_CameraStyle, so it reaches the new style after Style_1. You can also start in it (Camera Style on the pawn's AC_CameraSystem) or select it with DDCvar.CameraStyle 4 (the fifth entry; the console variable counts from 0).

Check: play, press 2 until the on-screen message shows the new style, and compare the view in free movement, strafe and aim. GameplayCameras.Debug.Enable 1 shows which rig is active.

docs.title: Change the start perspective or style
docs.text:
On each pawn's AC_CameraSystem component: Camera Perspective (category Camera > Perspective) and Camera Style (Camera > General). The style also follows the console variable DDCvar.CameraStyle, whose default (1, Style_2) is set in Project Settings > Engine > Data Driven CVars.

Check: play: the game starts in the chosen view.

docs.title: Limit the perspectives
docs.text:
On each pawn's AC_CameraSystem component, set Allowed Perspectives (category Camera > Perspective) to the views you want, in the order 1 should cycle them (for example ThirdPerson, FirstPerson). One entry turns the perspective input off. Make sure Camera Perspective (the start view) is in the list; otherwise the camera starts in the first entry and shows a warning.

The ragdoll view (Camera Perspective During Ragdoll, ThirdPerson by default) can stay as it is: when it is not in the list (first person only, for example), the ragdoll keeps the current view, and no warning is shown while it is at its default.

For a third-person-only game you can also delete AC_FirstPersonSystem from the pawn. See Choosing the perspectives.

Check: play and press 1: only the listed views come up, in the listed order, and no warning appears.

docs.title: Change the ragdoll camera
docs.text:
On each pawn's AC_CameraSystem component, category Camera > Ragdoll:

Goal Setting Keep the current view during the ragdoll Change Perspective During Ragdoll off Watch the ragdoll from another view (for example top-down) Camera Perspective During Ragdoll; the view must be in Allowed Perspectives Let the player switch perspective or shoulder during the ragdoll Allow Camera Switch on (needs Change Perspective During Ragdoll on)

Check: play in first person and press X to ragdoll: the camera switches to the ragdoll view, and back after you get up (X or Space). See Ragdoll and interactions for the ragdoll controls.

docs.title: Restyle the crosshair
docs.text:
Edit W_Crosshair, or make your own User Widget and set it as Crosshair Widget Class on each pawn's AC_CameraSystem (category Camera > Crosshair). The camera component only adds the widget to the screen and centers it on the aim point; nothing calls into it. W_Crosshair is a plain dot (its Default Color); cover targets are shown by the cover marker. To react to cover in your own crosshair, read the owning pawn's cover system each frame (IsCoverTargeted on AC_CoverSystem). To hide the crosshair, turn Show Crosshair off.

Check: play: your widget follows the aim point in every perspective.

docs.title: Set up cover in a level
Set up cover in a level
docs.text: The cover system needs no special actors: it finds cover with traces against the level geometry. This page lists what the geometry needs so every cover feature works, and how to test a level.

docs.title: Requirements at a glance
docs.text: Feature The level needs A playable level The level's GameMode Override set to GM_Sandbox (World Settings) and a Player Start. Taking cover Walls whose collision blocks the Cover channel (every profile that blocks Visibility does, so the default for static meshes). Low vs. high cover Walls that do not reach High Cover Height (148 cm above the feet) are low cover. The check is a sphere trace (Cover Trace Radius, 12 cm), so a wall down to about 136 cm still counts as high. Cover run A NavMeshBoundsVolume covering the play area, with the navmesh built, and floor the character can stand on in front of the target cover. Vault from cover The cover must block the Traversable channel (see Make objects traversable) and be low enough to vault. Corner turn An outside corner of at most Corner Turn Angle (100 degrees between the normals of the two faces), with at least Corner Turn Min Width (50 cm) of wall around it. Aim around an edge Free space past the wall end: a capsule width plus Cover Aim Edge Clearance (20 cm). Pose lowering Walls at least 10 cm thick, so the down trace from the top finds them.

docs.title: 1. Block out the cover
docs.text:
To start from an empty level, use File > New Level > Basic, open Window > World Settings and set GameMode Override to GM_Sandbox. The Basic level already has a Player Start and a floor. (Or work in a copy of DefaultLevel, which already has all of this.)

Any static mesh works as cover. The demo levels use LevelBlock and LevelBlock_Traversable from /GASPALS/Levels/LevelPrototyping, which you can place and scale directly.

Good cover heights for the sample characters (about 180 cm tall):

Height Plays as 90 to 110 cm Low cover: the character crouches behind it, can aim over it, can vault it. 110 to 130 cm Low cover, but the character barely clears it when standing to aim. 150 cm and more High cover: the character stands; aiming steps out at the wall ends.

Avoid walls between about 130 and 150 cm: they sit at the boundary between low and high cover, so a small height change along the wall changes how the character plays it.

Leave at least a capsule width (about 80 cm) of floor along the cover so the character can move along it.

docs.title: 2. Check the collision
docs.text:
Select a wall and look at Collision Presets in its Details panel. BlockAll, BlockAllDynamic and TraversalObjectPreset all block Cover. InvisibleWall and triggers ignore it, and so do characters. Avoid simple collision that does not match the visible shape: the character hugs the collision, not the mesh.

Exclude or include objects. Set the object's Collision Presets to Custom and change its Cover response:

  • Ignore keeps it from being cover: foliage, see-through fences, props too small to hide behind. The character walks past it, and the cover marker does not show on it.
  • Block makes it cover even if it ignores Visibility, for example an invisible blocking volume along a broken wall.

Shots from cover still trace Visibility (the camera's Aim Trace Channel), so excluding an object from cover does not let shots through it.

Type show collision in the console during Play to see what the traces hit.

docs.title: 3. Add navigation for cover runs
docs.text:
The cover run follows a navmesh path to the target cover.

  1. In the main toolbar, open the Add (+) menu and choose Volumes > Nav Mesh Bounds Volume. Scale it over the whole play area.
  2. Press P in the viewport to show the navmesh (green). It must reach the floor in front of the cover. If it does not appear, use Build > Build Paths.
  3. Keep Project Settings > Engine > Navigation System > Allow Client Side Navigation on for multiplayer (the template sets it; see Project settings).

Without a navmesh the character runs to the cover in a straight line, and stops at the first obstacle.

docs.title: 4. Make cover vaultable
docs.text: Pressing jump in cover vaults over it through the traversal system. Traversal only considers geometry that blocks the Traversable trace channel. Use LevelBlock_Traversable, set the wall's collision preset to TraversalObjectPreset, or set its Traversable response to Block in a custom preset. On walls that do not block it, the Mover pawn jumps instead and the CMC pawn does nothing.

docs.title: 5. Test
docs.text:
Press Play and check:

  1. Walk into a high wall: the character takes soft cover and turns along it.
  2. Put the crosshair on a wall within 2.5 m and tap Q: the cover marker shows on the wall and the character snaps to it in sticky cover.
  3. Put the crosshair on a wall 3 to 15 m away and hold Q: the marker shows, and the character runs there and takes sticky cover.
  4. In sticky cover, hold the move input toward a wall end: the character stops at the end, and after 0.3 s walks around an outside corner.
  5. Behind low cover, aim (Right Button) over the wall: the character stands up; aim along the wall: it stays down.
  6. In cover behind low cover, press Space: the character turns to the wall and vaults over it.

Press N to switch between the Mover and CMC pawns and repeat the checks on both. For multiplayer, set Number of Players to 2 and Net Mode to Play As Listen Server in the Play options (the menu next to Play), and try the cover run on the client.

For debugging, turn on Enable Debug on the pawn's cover component to draw the cover traces and Cover Aim Debug to print aim pose changes, and use show collision and the navmesh view (P).

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text:
Symptom Cause The character never takes cover The wall ignores the Cover channel, the project has no Cover channel (copy the collision settings, or set Cover Trace Channel to Visibility), or Enable Cover is off on the pawn's cover component. A trigger or volume behaves like a wall It uses Custom collision that blocks Cover (a new channel's default response). Set its Cover response like its Visibility response. Cover drops when moving along a long wall The wall is made of pieces with gaps or uneven faces. Close the gaps, or raise Max Cover Turn Angle for bends. No character spawns, or a default pawn flies around The level's GameMode Override is not GM_Sandbox. A standing character walks into low cover without taking it Expected: soft low cover needs crouching. Crouch first (C), or use sticky cover (Q). The cover marker does not show The crosshair is not on cover the button can take: farther than Cover Run Range (15 m), no floor to stand on in front of it, or (with Enable Cover Run off) farther than Sticky Cover Reach. The cover run goes straight into an obstacle No navmesh, or the navmesh does not reach the target. The cover run works on the server but not on clients Allow Client Side Navigation is off. Jump in cover jumps instead of vaulting The cover does not block Traversable, or it is too high to vault. The corner turn stops at the wall end It is an inside corner, the corner is sharper than Corner Turn Angle, or the wall around it is thinner than Corner Turn Min Width. The character sinks into low cover The cover top is lower than the head clearance assumes; lower Cover Lower Max Crouch.

More settings are in Configure cover behavior.

docs.title: Configure cover behavior
docs.text:
All cover settings are on the pawn's cover component. Open the pawn Blueprint (SandboxCharacter_Mover or SandboxCharacter_CMC in /GASPALS/Blueprints), select AC_CoverSystem in the Components panel, and use the Details panel under Cover. Compile and save the Blueprint, then press Play to try the change. The full list is in the Cover reference.

Change both pawns

The two sample pawns each have their own cover component. When you change a setting on one, change it on the other, or the Mover and CMC pawns will behave differently (press N in Play to switch pawns and compare). Child Blueprints of a pawn inherit its values except where they override them. Changing a default in AC_CoverSystem_Base does not reach components that already set their own value.

docs.title: Sticky cover only (button to take cover)
docs.text:
Walking into walls no longer takes cover; only the cover button does.

Setting Value Enable Auto Cover off Enable Sticky Cover on

docs.title: Automatic cover only (no button)
docs.text:
Setting Value Enable Auto Cover on Enable Sticky Cover off

The cover button does nothing, no cover marker shows, and there are no cover runs or corner turns.

docs.title: Sticky cover without cover runs
docs.text:
Setting Value Enable Cover Run off

The cover button only takes cover within Sticky Cover Reach, and the marker only shows on cover it can take from where the character stands.

docs.title: Cover only while crouching
docs.text:
Setting Value Engage Rule WhileCrouched

Cover is taken and kept only while the crouch input is on (C); standing up leaves it, even behind low cover.

docs.title: Keep a gap to the wall
docs.text:
The character rests touching the wall by default. To leave a gap (for bulky characters or poses that clip):

Setting Value Wall Distance Stand Auto / Stand Sticky / Crouch Auto / Crouch Sticky Gap in cm between the capsule and the wall, per case. Cover Hold Distance Keep it larger than the largest gap plus the capsule radius (about 30 cm on the Mover pawn, 40 cm on the CMC pawn), or cover drops.

docs.title: Choose how the character faces
docs.text:
Four settings, one per case, each FaceWall, ShoulderToWall or BackToWall:

Setting Class default Facing Stand Auto ShoulderToWall Facing Stand Sticky BackToWall Facing Crouch Auto FaceWall Facing Crouch Sticky ShoulderToWall

With FaceWall, Character Rotation Right Shoulder and Left Shoulder (25 and -25 degrees) turn the character toward the camera side.

docs.title: Make cover harder or easier to leave
docs.text: Setting Effect Cover Exit Input Dot How directly the input must point away from the wall (0.7 is more than 45 degrees away). Lower leaves more easily. Cover Exit Delay Seconds of pushing away before soft cover is released. Sticky Exit Input Dot / Sticky Exit Delay The same for sticky cover (0.9 and 0.35 s: deliberate). Sticky Tap Time A cover button press shorter than this (0.25 s) is a tap: it leaves sticky cover. A longer press is a hold (cover run). Sticky Reentry Cooldown Seconds after leaving cover before cover can grab the character again (0.5 s).

docs.title: Snap to cover from farther away
docs.text: Setting Effect Sticky Cover Reach How far along the camera the cover button finds a wall (250 cm). Cover Run Range Up to where the button runs to cover (1500 cm). Cover Enter Distance How far soft cover reaches when walking into a wall (80 cm). Cover Enter Input Dot How directly the move input must point into the wall to take soft cover (0.3). Higher needs a more direct push.

docs.title: Tune the cover run arrival
docs.text: The run slows down before it snaps into cover. If the character overshoots or slides along the wall, lower Cover Run Brake Decel (700) below what the pawn can brake, or raise Cover Run Arrive Distance (80 cm). Cover Run Arrive Speed (150 cm/s) is the speed at the snap. If long runs are cancelled before they arrive, raise Cover Run Max Time (2 s on top of the planned time).

docs.title: Aim from cover
docs.text: Goal Setting Aiming always leaves cover Enable Cover Aim off Step out to edges even when standing over low cover Cover Aim Keep Standing off Fewer pose switches Raise Cover Aim Min Pose Time, Cover Aim Blocked Delay and Cover Aim Return Delay Tall or short characters Cover Aim Muzzle Height Stand (145) and Crouch (95): muzzle height above the capsule bottom Thick walls Cover Aim Cover Depth: hits this deep behind the cover face count as the cover itself See what it does Cover Aim Debug prints every pose change and draws the target; Enable Debug draws the cover traces

docs.title: Pose lowering
docs.text: Setting Effect Cover Lower Max Stand / Max Crouch The most the pelvis is lowered, in cm (10 and 15). 0 turns lowering off. Cover Lower Head Clearance How far under the cover top the head should end up (5 cm). Cover Lower Settle Tolerance How close to its cover distance the character must be before the pelvis lowers (10 cm). Larger lowers earlier, while the character still slides to the wall.

docs.title: Camera in cover
docs.text:
Goal Setting No camera raise behind low cover and no push past wall ends Enable Cover Camera Offsets off Keep the camera on the player's shoulder at wall ends Enable Cover Shoulder Switch off

The offsets themselves are camera rigs; see Camera system.

docs.title: Cover marker
docs.text:
Goal Setting No marker Show Cover Marker off Your own marker Cover Marker Widget Class (any User Widget), Cover Marker Draw Size (100 x 12) and Cover Marker Wall Offset (3 cm)

Or edit W_CoverMarker (/GASPALS/Systems/CoverSystem) to restyle the default marker for every pawn.

docs.title: First person
docs.text: Setting Options First Person Sticky Cover SwitchToThirdPerson (default) or Disabled First Person Auto Cover MovementOnly (default) or Disabled

docs.title: Separate keys for sticky cover and the cover run
docs.text: Both input actions are on Q. To give the cover run its own key, change the IA_CoverRun mapping in IMC_Sandbox (see Add or rebind inputs). The sticky key then only takes and leaves sticky cover, and the run key runs to the targeted cover when held past Sticky Tap Time.

docs.title: Movement speeds in cover
docs.text: On the Mover pawn, cover speeds belong to the Cover movement mode: Walk Speed 150, Run Speed and Sprint Speed 250 cm/s in the class defaults of BP_MovementMode_Cover (/GASPALS/Blueprints/MovementModes). On the CMC pawn, cover uses the pawn's Walk Speeds (or Crouch Speeds when crouched); see Movement. The cover run sprints with the normal sprint speed on both pawns.

docs.title: Turning cover off
docs.text: Turn off Enable Cover on the component. Everything else stays in place, so you can turn it back on per pawn. See System switches for what the pawn does without cover.

docs.title: Add an equipment item
docs.text:
This tutorial adds a shotgun. The same steps work for any held item: a weapon, a tool, a carried object. You need:

  • the item's mesh (skeletal or static);
  • ideally, a few poses of the character holding it, as animations on the UEFN mannequin skeleton (/GASPALS/Characters/UEFN_Mannequin/Meshes/SK_UEFN_Mannequin), the skeleton the overlay Anim Blueprints use. Single-frame animations are enough. Until you have them, the rifle's poses work as placeholders.

The result: the shotgun appears in the equipment menu, attaches to the hand, switches the character to your poses in third and first person, and places the support hand with IK.

Background: Equipment system, Overlay system.

All equipment assets are in /GASPALS/Systems/EquipmentSystem; the paths below are relative to it unless they start with /GASPALS.

docs.title: 1. Add the slot
docs.text:
Open Data/Enum_Equipment, click Add Enumerator and set the new enumerator's Display Name to Shotgun. Save.

The equipment menu builds its buttons from this enum (labeled with the display name), so the new slot shows up in the menu by itself, at the end of the list. To place it elsewhere, drag its row by the handle on its left; the menu follows the enum order. Slots listed in the component's Hidden Equipment are left out (the revolver is, by default).

docs.title: 2. Prepare the mesh sockets
docs.text:
Add these sockets to the item mesh: for a skeletal mesh, on its Skeleton (open the skeleton, right-click a bone > Add Socket); for a static mesh, in the Static Mesh Editor's Socket Manager.

Socket Where HandIK Where the support hand grips (the shotgun's pump). The support hand is placed on this socket, position and rotation. ADS The sight point: on the sight line, at the rear sight. Only for items you aim down sights with.

Use the rifle's sockets as a starting point: they are on the root bone of Assets/Meshes/M4A1_Skeleton. If your mesh already has sockets with other names, keep them and set Hand IKSocket / ADSSocket in the data asset (step 6).

docs.title: 3. Create the item actor
docs.text:
Duplicate an existing item actor in Actors/ and rename it BP_Equipment_Shotgun:

  • for a skeletal mesh, duplicate BP_Equipment_Rifle;
  • for a static mesh, duplicate BP_Equipment_Torch (or BP_Equipment_Box).

Open it, select its mesh component (SkeletalMesh or StaticMesh) and set your mesh. The item must not collide (it could push the character or block the camera): on a static mesh, keep Collision Presets on NoCollision (the torch's setting); on a skeletal mesh, use no physics asset or set the same preset.

The actor only needs its mesh component. Do not add a first-person component, a first-person duplicate mesh or rendering tags: the pawn's first-person system creates the first-person copy of the mesh at runtime. To show the item in third person only, turn Create First Person Copy off in its data asset (step 6).

Tip

Add extra parts (a flashlight, a strap) as more mesh components. Each gets its own first-person copy. Tag a component DoNotAttach if it should stay where it is instead of being attached to the hand socket.

docs.title: 4. Add the attach socket on the character skeletons
docs.text:
The item attaches to a socket on the character's Skeleton. Either reuse overlay_rifle (a long gun held in the right hand; nothing to do), or add overlay_shotgun to every skeleton your characters use:

Skeleton Bone for a right-hand item /GASPALS/Characters/UEFN_Mannequin/Meshes/SK_UEFN_Mannequin (the pawns) weapon_r /GASPALS/Characters/UE5_Mannequins/Meshes/SK_Mannequin (Manny, Quinn) hand_r /GASPALS/MetaHumans/Common/Female/Medium/NormalWeight/Body/metahuman_base_skel (Kellan) hand_r

On each skeleton, start from the overlay_rifle values (select the socket and copy its Relative Location and Relative Rotation, then add overlay_shotgun on the same bone and paste them). To adjust it, right-click the socket > Add Preview Asset, pick the shotgun mesh, and preview a holding pose (a Pose_Rifle_* animation or yours).

A skeleton without the socket attaches the item at the character's feet.

docs.title: Third person
docs.text:
1. Duplicate /GASPALS/Systems/OverlaySystem/OverlayPose/Rifle/ABP_Overlay_Rifle, rename it ABP_Overlay_Shotgun and move it to a new folder, OverlaySystem/OverlayPose/Shotgun.
  2. Open it and go to Class Defaults. Under Overlay > Poses > Stand and Overlay > Poses > Crouch, each pose (Stand_Relax_Idle, Stand_Ready_Idle, Stand_Aim_Idle, the Walk, Run and Sprint variants, and the crouch Idle and Move variants) has an Overlay Pose (the animation) and a Curve Map. Set your shotgun animations; keep the rifle's where you have none yet.
  3. Keep the rifle's curve maps: they decide which body parts the pose takes over, and enable_handik_l turns the support-hand IK on.
  4. Set Stand Aim Sweep and Crouch Aim Sweep if you have aim sweep animations (arms aiming up and down); otherwise keep the rifle's.
  5. Under Overlay > General, keep Can Aim on (an item you aim with); under Overlay > Aim, keep Aim Sweep Interp Speed Local / Remote at 0 / 10 (a local value of 0 follows the aim without interpolation, which avoids visible stepping).

See Add an overlay state for the poses and curves in detail.

docs.title: First person (optional)
docs.text: Duplicate /GASPALS/Systems/OverlaySystem/FirstPerson/Rifle/ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Rifle, rename it ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Shotgun and set its first-person poses, keeping the rifle's curve maps (see Give an item first-person poses). Without one, first person shows the third-person overlay; the first-person curves (enable_cr_fp_ads for aiming down sights, among others) come from the first-person overlay, so give an item you aim with one.

docs.title: 6. Create the data asset
docs.text:
Duplicate Data/DA_Equipment_Rifle and rename it DA_Equipment_Shotgun (or right-click in Data/ > Miscellaneous > Data Asset and pick PDA_Equipment). Fill it:

Field Value Spawned Actor BP_Equipment_Shotgun. Required: without an actor, the item's overlay poses are not used. Overlay Pose TP ABP_Overlay_Shotgun Overlay Pose FP ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Shotgun (or empty) Attach Socket TP / Attach Socket FP overlay_shotgun (or overlay_rifle) Attach Offset TP / Attach Offset FP Small corrections; the rifle uses a -5 degree yaw on TP. Is Left Handed Off (on for items held in the left hand, like the bow). Hand IKSocket / ADSSocket HandIK / ADS (the defaults), or your mesh's socket names. ADSEnter Speed / ADSExit Speed / ADSHand Offset First-person aim down sights: keep 15 / 5 / (0, 0, 0) to start. Create First Person Copy On (the default): the item shows in the first-person hands. Off: third person only. First Person Motion Profile DA_FPMotion_Rifle, DA_FPMotion_Pistol, DA_FPMotion_Bow or DA_FPMotion_Heavy (in /GASPALS/Systems/FirstPersonSystem/Motion), or empty for the pawn's default (Tune first-person motion).

docs.title: 7. Add the chooser row
docs.text:
Open Data/CHT_Equipment and add a row: in its enum column pick Shotgun, and as its result pick DA_Equipment_Shotgun. Save.

Without a row, the slot falls back to DA_Equipment_Unequip: selecting it leaves the hands empty.

docs.title: 8. Optional: ragdoll get-up
docs.text:
The CMC pawn's ragdoll picks its get-up animation from the hands that hold the item, which AC_EquipmentSystem gives per slot. A new slot answers "no hands" (the default get-up) until you add it:

  1. Open AC_EquipmentSystem and the function GetHeldItemHands.
  2. The Switch on Enum_Equipment node now has a Shotgun pin. Connect it to a new Return Node with Left Hand and Right Hand set like the most similar item (copy the Rifle's return node).
  3. Compile and save.

docs.title: 9. Test
docs.text:
1. Save all, then play. Hold T and scroll up once (from Unequip the highlight wraps to the end of the list) to highlight Shotgun, then release.
  2. Check the grip in third person: idle, walk, run, sprint, crouch, aim (Right Button). If the item is offset, fix the skeleton socket (step 4) or Attach Offset TP. If the support hand misses, move the item's HandIK socket. If nothing appears in the hands, check the chooser row (step 7) and Spawned Actor (step 6).
  3. Switch to first person (press 1 until you reach it) and aim: the sights should line up with the screen center. Fix the ADS socket if not.
  4. Press M to try the retargeted characters (each uses its own skeleton's socket), and N for the other pawn.
  5. Run a listen server with a client (Try multiplayer), equip the shotgun on the client and check it in both windows.

docs.title: Variations
docs.text:
• Pose without an item (hands tied, an injured arm): use an overlay stance instead (Add an overlay state). An equipment data asset without Spawned Actor behaves like Unequip: the overlay system's stance shows, not the data asset's poses.
  • Left-handed item: turn on Is Left Handed, attach to a socket on the left hand (weapon_l on the UEFN mannequin, hand_l on the others, like overlay_bow), and turn on enable_handik_r instead of enable_handik_l in the poses' curve maps so the right hand is the support hand.
  • Start with the item: set Selected Equipment (Equipment > Selection) on the AC_EquipmentSystem component of both pawns, SandboxCharacter_Mover and SandboxCharacter_CMC (or of your own pawn).
  • Hide an unfinished item: add its slot to Hidden Equipment (Equipment > UI on AC_EquipmentSystem): in the class defaults, and on the component of each pawn, whose value can differ. The menu leaves it out and scrolling skips it; SelectNewEquipment still equips it. Remove it from the list to show it again.

docs.title: Tune first-person motion
docs.text: In first person, the hands and the held item react to the player: they lag behind when the view turns, lean into strafes, bob with the steps, breathe at rest and take a jolt on jumps and landings. While aiming down sights the motion fades so the sight stays steady. The camera itself never moves, which keeps the view comfortable. The motion works in all three first-person modes and on the retargeted characters, and only the local player sees it. Background: First person system.

docs.title: Where the settings are
docs.text:
All the values live in motion profiles, data assets of the class PDA_FirstPersonMotion in /GASPALS/Systems/FirstPersonSystem/Motion. Four ship with the template:

Profile Feel Used by DA_FPMotion_Unarmed Loose Empty hands (the pawns' default) DA_FPMotion_Pistol Light Pistol, revolver, torch, binoculars DA_FPMotion_Rifle Medium (the class defaults) Rifle DA_FPMotion_Bow Medium, with a wider bob and a bob roll Bow DA_FPMotion_Heavy Slow and heavy Box, barrel

Which profile is active:

  1. The equipped item's First Person Motion Profile (on its DA_Equipment_* data asset in /GASPALS/Systems/EquipmentSystem/Data, category Equipment > First Person), when set.
  2. Otherwise the First Person Motion Profile on the pawn's AC_FirstPersonSystem component (First Person > Motion). It applies to every character the pawn shows. Set it on both sample pawns (SandboxCharacter_Mover and SandboxCharacter_CMC).

Open a profile (double-click it) and change its values while playing in the editor: the change shows at once. Save the profile to keep it.

docs.title: Check what is active
docs.text: Turn Debug First Person Motion (First Person > Debug) on, on the pawn's AC_FirstPersonSystem, and play in first person: the motion pivot and targets are drawn, and the active profile, the targets, the view turn rate and the aim amount are printed on screen. If the pawn has no profile at all, an orange warning says so and the hands do not move. Turn the setting off again when you are done.

docs.title: Make an item feel heavier or lighter
docs.text:
Setting Heavier Lighter Position Strength / Rotation Strength (Hz) lower (1 to 1.2) higher (1.8 to 2.5) Look Rotation Per Degree higher lower Look Max Rotation higher lower Position Damping / Rotation Damping higher (0.9 to 1: no wobble) lower (0.6 to 0.8: a little overshoot)

The strengths are how many times per second the hands could swing back; the damping decides whether they overshoot (below 1) or settle smoothly (1). For reference, DA_FPMotion_Heavy uses 1.1 / 1.4 Hz and 0.9 damping, DA_FPMotion_Pistol 1.8 / 2.2 Hz and 0.8.

docs.title: Less or no sway when turning
docs.text: Lower Look Rotation Per Degree and Look Position Per Degree, or turn Look Sway off. To keep slow aiming steady but let fast flicks swing, make the start of Look Response Curve flat.

docs.title: Less or no sway when strafing
docs.text: Lower Move Roll Per Speed and Move Side Offset Per Speed, or turn Move Sway off.

docs.title: Change the steps
docs.text: Bob Stride Length is the distance of one bob cycle (two steps). Bob Side Amplitude, Bob Up Amplitude and Bob Roll Amplitude set the size, Bob Speed Curve how it grows with speed. Bob Shape Side, Bob Shape Up and Bob Shape Roll draw the path over one cycle (X = phase 0 to 1, Y = -1 to 1): the default makes a figure eight with one dip per step. Turn Bob off for no bob.

docs.title: Steadier or looser aiming
docs.text: While aiming, every source is multiplied by its ADS scale: ADSLook Scale, ADSMove Scale, ADSBob Scale, ADSBreathing Scale and ADSImpulse Scale (0 = none while aiming). ADSMotion Settle Speed makes leftover motion die out faster when you start aiming (2 = twice as fast; higher = less motion; 1 = no change). ADSBlend Curve shapes the change as the aim comes up. For a scope with deliberate sway, raise ADSBreathing Scale on that item's profile.

docs.title: Jumps and landings
docs.text: Jump Position Impulse / Jump Rotation Impulse and Landing Position Impulse / Landing Rotation Impulse are the kicks (cm/s and degrees/s); Landing Curve scales the landing kick by fall speed, so small hops barely show. Turn Jump Impulse or Landing Impulse off to remove one.

docs.title: Players sensitive to motion
docs.text: First Person Motion Intensity (First Person > Motion) on the pawn's AC_FirstPersonSystem scales all of it: 1 = as the profiles say, 0 = off. Bind it to an options menu to let players choose: get the pawn's AC_FirstPersonSystem component and set First Person Motion Intensity on it.

docs.title: Pause the motion during an animation
docs.text: Add a curve named disable_fp_motion to the animation of a montage the character plays (in the animation editor: Curves > Add Curve; 1 = motion off, 0 = on). The motion fades with the curve, which keeps it from fighting reload or interaction hand animation.

docs.title: Give an item its own feel
docs.text:
1. Duplicate the closest profile (for example DA_FPMotion_Rifle), name it DA_FPMotion_<Item>, and tune it.
  2. Set it as First Person Motion Profile on the item's DA_Equipment_* data asset and save both.
  3. Play in first person, equip the item (hold T, scroll, release), then turn, strafe, walk, jump and aim (Right Button) to check the feel.

docs.title: Setting reference
docs.text:
Every setting has a tooltip in the editor. Each group is a category (First Person > Motion > ) of the profile; the values are the class defaults (the Rifle profile):

Group Settings Springs Position Strength (1.6 Hz), Rotation Strength (2 Hz), Position Damping / Rotation Damping (0.85), Pivot Offset ((0, 30, -10): the point the hands rotate around, from the eyes; it blends to the eyes while aiming) Look Look Sway (on), Look Rotation Per Degree (0.02), Look Roll from Yaw (0.3), Look Position Per Degree (0.005), Look Max Rate (400 degrees/s), Look Max Rotation (6), Look Max Position (2), Look Response Curve Move Move Sway (on), Move Roll Per Speed (1.5), Move Side Offset Per Speed (0.6), Move Back Offset Per Speed (0.4), Move Max Rotation (5), Move Max Position (3) Bob Bob (on), Bob Stride Length (140), Bob Side Amplitude (1), Bob Up Amplitude (0.8), Bob Roll Amplitude (1.5), Bob Speed Curve, Bob Shape Side / Up / Roll Breathing Breathing (on), Breathing Position (0.15), Breathing Rotation (0.3), Breathing Rate (0.25 breaths per second) Impulses Jump Impulse (on), Jump Position Impulse ((0, 0, -25)), Jump Rotation Impulse ((-40, 0, 0)), Landing Impulse (on), Landing Position Impulse ((0, 0, -60)), Landing Rotation Impulse ((-80, 0, 0)), Landing Curve Stance Crouch Scale (0.6: motion scale while crouched) ADS ADSLook Scale (0.1), ADSMove Scale (0.1), ADSBob Scale (0), ADSBreathing Scale (0), ADSImpulse Scale (0.3), ADSMotion Settle Speed (2), ADSBlend Curve

Rotations are pitch, yaw, roll in degrees; positions are right, forward, up in cm, as seen from the eyes. Per-speed values are per meter per second of movement; per-degree values are per degree per second of view turn.

docs.title: Configure first person
docs.text:
First person works out of the box on the sample pawns and the shipped characters. This page covers the choices you make for your own characters and items. Background: First person system.

Where to find the settings:

  • How first person behaves (mode, arm limits, camera, motion): the AC_FirstPersonSystem component of the pawn Blueprint (SandboxCharacter_Mover and SandboxCharacter_CMC), category FirstPerson in the Details panel. One value for every body the pawn shows, including the retargeted characters. Change it on both sample pawns (or on each pawn you use): each pawn's component has its own values.
  • What to draw (meshes, retargeter, eye offset, camera and head bones): a PDA_FirstPersonSetup data asset per body, in /GASPALS/Systems/FirstPersonSystem/Setups. The pawns use DA_FirstPersonSetup_UEFN (Default Setup on AC_FirstPersonSystem); each retargeted character names its own in its First Person Setup class default (for example DA_FirstPersonSetup_Manny on BP_RetargetedCharacter_Manny).

To try any change: play, press 1 until the view is in first person (third person, top-down, side-scroller, then first person by default), and press M to cycle the characters (UEFN mannequin, Kellan, Manny, Quinn).

docs.title: Choose a mode
docs.text:
You want Mode Classic shooter view with body and shadow FirstPersonOverlay (default) The same, without weapons clipping into walls FirstPersonOverlaySplit (needs arms and body meshes) Immersive view of the real third-person animation TrueFirstPerson A skeleton with non-standard spine names TrueFirstPerson

Set First Person Mode (First Person > General) on the pawn's AC_FirstPersonSystem; every character the pawn shows uses it. A character on another skeleton whose setup has no Retargeter uses TrueFirstPerson whatever the mode, with an on-screen warning. See Modes for what each one looks like.

docs.title: Set the meshes
docs.text:
Open the body's PDA_FirstPersonSetup asset (double-click it in the Content Browser):

  1. Full Meshes: add the body mesh first, then clothing and accessories. A headless body variant avoids seeing the inside of the head; without one, leave the list empty and the component reuses the third-person mesh with the head bone hidden.
  2. Materials: nothing to do. Material overrides are copied from the third-person component that uses the same mesh, or whose mesh name followed by Mesh Suffix (_FP) starts the first-person mesh name: SKM_Hero gives its materials to SKM_Hero_FP and SKM_Hero_FP_Arms. Name your first-person meshes that way.
  3. Body component: on a pawn, Third Person Mesh Name (First Person > Setup) on AC_FirstPersonSystem names the body component to copy from. A retargeted character returns its body from GetVisualBodyMesh (the SkeletalMesh component by default).
  4. Save the asset.

To create a setup for a new character, duplicate DA_FirstPersonSetup_Manny and follow Add a retargeted character.

docs.title: Split meshes
docs.text:
FirstPersonOverlaySplit needs an arms mesh (arms and hands, cut at the clavicles) and a body mesh without arms, neck and head. Author them in your DCC tool (keep a small overlap at the shoulders), or generate a first version with the editor utility EUB_SplitFirstPersonMesh:

  1. Duplicate your body mesh twice (right-click > Duplicate): SKM_Hero_FP_Arms and SKM_Hero_FP_NoArms.
  2. Open /GASPALS/Systems/FirstPersonSystem/Tools/EUB_SplitFirstPersonMesh, click Class Defaults and set Source Mesh (your body mesh), Arms Target (SKM_Hero_FP_Arms) and Body Target (SKM_Hero_FP_NoArms) under First Person > Mesh Split. Arm Root Bones (clavicle_l, clavicle_r) and Head Root Bones (neck_01) decide what counts as arm and head; change them only for other bone names. Compile and save.
  3. Right-click the utility in the Content Browser > Run Editor Utility Blueprint.
  4. Save the two target meshes. They keep LOD 0 only.
  5. Put them in the setup's Arms Meshes and Body Meshes, add your clothing meshes to Body Meshes if you have any, and set First Person Mode to FirstPersonOverlaySplit on the pawns.

Warning

The utility overwrites the target meshes. Never point it at meshes you authored by hand. Source Mesh, Arms Target and Body Target are empty by default: set all three before running it. Without a Source Mesh it stops with the message Split: could not read Source Mesh.

Check it: play in first person. Look down and at a wall with the rifle: the arms and the rifle stay in front of the wall while the body shows below. No orange warning starting with GASPALS First Person should appear.

docs.title: Place the camera at the eyes
docs.text:
