The camera sits on the head bone plus Eye Offset (First Person > Setup > Camera), set in the body's PDA_FirstPersonSetup (for example DA_FirstPersonSetup_Manny). The offset is in centimeters, in the mesh's space at the reference pose: X right, Y forward, Z up. On the UEFN mannequin the head bone is at the eyes (offset (0, 0, 0)); on UE5 mannequins and MetaHumans it is at the base of the skull, so the shipped characters use (0, 12, 0): 12 cm forward.

  1. Play, switch to the character in first person, and look straight ahead, then fully down.
  2. If you see the inside of the head or the chest, increase Y (forward). If the view is too high or too low, change Z. X moves the camera sideways. Stop, change Eye Offset in the setup, save and play again.
  3. Equip the rifle (hold T, scroll to the rifle, release) and aim (hold Right Button). The sights should line up with the screen center. The ADS hand targets use the same offset, so fixing the eye position also fixes the sights. If one item still sits too close or too far while aiming, change ADSHand Offset on its DA_Equipment_<Item> data asset.

docs.title: Tune the look-down and camera behavior
docs.text:
On the pawn's AC_FirstPersonSystem (overlay modes):

Setting Category Effect First Person Arm Pitch Down Limit (45) First Person > Arms How far the arms follow the view down before the spine leans. Lower values lean more. First Person Arm Pitch Up Limit (90) First Person > Arms The same looking up. First Person Camera Follow Lean (0.75) First Person > Camera 1: the camera moves forward with the leaning head. 0: the camera stays, the body moves back. First Person Camera Vertical Smoothing (12) First Person > Camera How quickly the camera height follows the body. Lower = softer crouches and landings. First Person Max Root Yaw Lag (60) First Person > Camera Degrees the body may lag behind the view before it turns with it.

Check it: play in first person, look fully down while standing and while walking, and crouch (C).

For the field of view, see Change the first-person field of view. For hand and item sway, see Tune first-person motion.

docs.title: Give an item first-person poses
docs.text:
Items without a first-person overlay show their third-person overlay in first person. To add one:

  1. Duplicate ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Rifle (/GASPALS/Systems/OverlaySystem/FirstPerson/Rifle), name it ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_<Item>.
  2. Open it, click Class Defaults and, under Overlay > Poses, set each pose variable (Stand Relax Idle, Stand Ready Idle, Stand Aim Idle, the walk, run and crouch variants...): its animation and its curve map, as for a third-person overlay (see Pose Anim Blueprints). Keep the first-person curves: enable_cr_fp_stable_arms, enable_cr_fp_stable_head, enable_cr_fp_ads, enable_cr_fp_aimoffset, and enable_handik_l or enable_handik_r for the support hand. Turn Can Aim (Overlay > General) off for an item that cannot aim. Compile and save.
  3. Set it as Overlay Pose FP in the item's data asset (DA_Equipment_<Item>, in /GASPALS/Systems/EquipmentSystem/Data).
  4. Make sure the item mesh has an ADS socket (the sight point) and a HandIK socket (support hand), or set ADSSocket and Hand IKSocket in the data asset to your socket names.

Check it: play in first person, equip the item, then stand, walk, crouch and aim. The arms should use your poses, the support hand should stay on the item, and aiming should bring the ADS socket to the screen center.

docs.title: Turn first person off
docs.text:
Either:

  • turn Enable First Person (First Person > General) off on each pawn's AC_FirstPersonSystem: FirstPerson is removed from the available perspectives; or
  • remove FirstPerson from Allowed Perspectives on each pawn's AC_CameraSystem (see Limit the perspectives).

The first-person meshes are then never built. To strip it completely, also delete AC_FirstPersonSystem from the pawns, and remove FirstPerson from Allowed Perspectives (otherwise the camera shows a warning); the retargeted characters and items have no first-person component.

Check it: play and press 1 repeatedly: the first-person view never comes.

docs.title: First person only
docs.text:
On each pawn's AC_CameraSystem, set Allowed Perspectives to FirstPerson only and Camera Perspective (the start view) to FirstPerson; if you leave the start view at ThirdPerson, the game still starts in first person but shows an on-screen warning. The perspective input (1) then does nothing.

  • Cover: sticky cover never switches to third person: set First Person Sticky Cover to Disabled on the pawn's cover component, or leave it, it acts the same.
  • Ragdoll: the ragdoll keeps the first-person view. Its default view (Camera Perspective During Ragdoll, ThirdPerson) is not allowed, so the switch is skipped, without a warning while that setting is at its default.

Check it: play: the game starts in first person with no orange warning, and 1 does nothing.

docs.title: Add or rebind inputs
docs.text: GASPALS uses Enhanced Input. When a player possesses a pawn, the pawn adds the mapping contexts listed in its Input Mapping Contexts setting (default: IMC_Sandbox at priority 0). The systems listen to input actions (IA_*), not keys, so rebinding is a matter of editing mappings.

docs.title: Rebind a key
docs.text: Open /GASPALS/Input/Mappings/IMC_Sandbox, find the action, and change its key. For example, move the cover run (IA_CoverRun) from Q to F to give it its own key; sticky cover (IA_CoverSticky) stays on Q. Save; the change applies at the next Play.

docs.title: Add gamepad bindings
docs.text:
A few actions have no gamepad key in IMC_Sandbox: IA_Overlay_Body, IA_Camera_Style, IA_NextPawn, IA_NextVisualOverride, IA_TeleportToTarget and IA_Move_WorldSpace. Every gamepad button already has an action (see Controls), so free one first, or map the action to a button combination with a Chorded Action trigger.

Note

The Z key is hard-wired to the Mover pawn's debug flying toggle (keyboard only; it does not use a gamepad button). Turn Enable Debug Tools off on the pawn's AC_DebugTools, or remove that node from the Mover pawn's Event Graph (an Input Key node for Z), before shipping. See Debug tools.

docs.title: Use your own mapping context
docs.text:
1. Create your context and map the GASPALS input actions (copy IMC_Sandbox to start).
  2. Open each pawn's Class Defaults and, under GASPALS > Input, replace IMC_Sandbox in Input Mapping Contexts with yours. No graph edit is needed.

Add more contexts as more entries of the map, with a higher priority for contexts that should win on shared keys (for example a gamepad-only context). An empty map leaves the player without controls and shows an on-screen warning.

docs.title: Who handles which action
docs.text:
Handled by Actions The pawn Move, look, sprint, walk, strafe, aim, crouch, jump (also gets up from a ragdoll), cover PC_Sandbox Next pawn, next character, teleport (through AC_DebugTools on the Mover pawn) AC_CameraSystem Perspective, style, shoulder AC_EquipmentSystem Equipment menu, menu next / previous AC_OverlaySystem Overlay pose and body menus, menu next / previous AC_RagdollSystem Ragdoll and get up (CMC pawn) AC_SmartObjectAnimation Interact (benches) SandboxCharacter_Mover Ragdoll and get up, takedown, interact (shove), jump (get up), debug fly (Z); with aim held, takedown and interact call AC_DebugTools (demo shot, spawn / rotate)

Components bind their own input actions, so they receive input only when their pawn is player controlled and a context maps the action. The full list is in Input actions.

docs.title: Add an input to a system
docs.text:
Example: a button that leaves cover at once.

  1. Create an input action IA_LeaveCover (value type Digital (bool)) in your own content folder, not inside the plugin.
  2. Map it in your mapping context (or in IMC_Sandbox) to a free key.
  3. In the pawn's Event Graph, add the IA_LeaveCover event and, on Started, call AC_CoverSystem > ExitCover.
  4. On the Mover pawn, remember that movement goes through the input command: changes that affect movement should be read in ProduceInput rather than applied directly.

docs.title: Unused input assets
docs.text: IMC_Sandbox is the only mapping context in /GASPALS/Input/Mappings. Traversal runs from IA_Jump; there is no separate traverse action. IA_TwinStick_AimDirection is read by the Mover pawn's twin-stick mode but not mapped.

docs.title: Add an overlay state
docs.text:
An overlay state is an Anim Blueprint that provides a pose for the overlay layer. This tutorial covers three cases:

  1. Look at the Injured stance (a complete stance overlay that ships with the plugin): the quickest way to learn the pose Anim Blueprint.
  2. Add a new stance to the overlay pose menu (for example Wounded Arm).
  3. Add a body style to the overlay body menu.

For an item pose (something held, spawned by the equipment system), see Add an equipment item; the pose Anim Blueprint part is the same as here.

Background: Overlay system.

You need: pose animations on the UEFN mannequin skeleton (SK_UEFN_Mannequin): one standing and one crouched pose for a stance, plus ready and aim poses for an item.

docs.title: The pose Anim Blueprint in short
docs.text:
Every pose overlay is a child of ABP_OverlayPose_Base with only class defaults set:

  • Pose variables (Stand_Relax_Idle, Stand_Ready_Walk, Crouch_Aim_Move...): each has an Overlay Pose (the animation) and a Curve Map.
  • Can Aim: whether the Ready and Aiming states are used.
  • Aim sweeps (Stand_Aim_Sweep, Crouch_Aim_Sweep) for items that aim.
  • Aim Sweep Interp Speed Local / Remote: 0 / 10 (0 = the owning player's arms follow the camera exactly).

The Anim Blueprint plays the first frame of each pose animation as a still pose, so single-frame animations of the character holding the pose are enough. The curve map says which body parts take the pose (see Curves).

docs.title: 1. Look at the Injured stance
docs.text:
ABP_Overlay_Injured (one hand held to the side) and ABP_Overlay_HandsTied (hands behind the back) are complete stance overlays. Open one to see how a stance is set up:

  1. Open /GASPALS/Systems/OverlaySystem/OverlayPose/Injured/ABP_Overlay_Injured and click Class Defaults in the toolbar.
  2. Under Overlay > Poses > Stand, Stand Relax Idle has its Overlay Pose set to Pose_Injured_Stand, and so do Stand Relax Walk, Stand Relax Run and Stand Relax Sprint (one pose can serve every speed).
  3. Under Overlay > Poses > Crouch, Crouch Relax Idle and Crouch Relax Move use Pose_Injured_Crouch. The Ready and Aim variables stay empty: a stance never uses them.

  4. Each Curve Map uses the same values as the poses in ABP_Overlay_Box. They take the whole body, legs included, and keep some locomotion motion on top:

    Curve Value layering_pelvis, layering_legs 1 (the pose's legs; 0 keeps the locomotion legs) layering_spine, layering_head 1 layering_spine_add 1 (locomotion spine motion added on top) layering_head_add 0.5 layering_arm_l, layering_arm_r 1 layering_arm_l_ls, layering_arm_r_ls 1 layering_hand_l, layering_hand_r 1

    The arm additives (layering_arm_l_add, layering_arm_r_add) and hand IK curves are not in the map, so they are 0: no arm swing, no hand IK. 5. Can Aim is off: the stance never goes to Ready or Aiming. 6. ABP_Overlay_HandsTied is set up the same way with Pose_HandsTied_Stand and Pose_HandsTied_Crouch. 7. Test: click Play, hold V, scroll the mouse wheel to Injured and release V. Walk, run, crouch (C). To experiment, stop Play, change the curves in the class defaults, compile, save and play again: lower layering_spine_add to make the torso stiffer, or set layering_legs and layering_pelvis to 0 to keep the locomotion legs.

Starting stance

Set Overlay Pose on the pawn's AC_OverlaySystem (Details panel, Overlay > Selection) to start in a stance. It shows while nothing is held; an equipped item's pose replaces it, and it comes back when the item is put away.

docs.title: 2. Add a new stance
docs.text:
1. Animations. Author the stance poses (standing and crouched) on the UEFN mannequin (/GASPALS/Characters/UEFN_Mannequin/Meshes/SK_UEFN_Mannequin), or author them on your own skeleton and retarget them to the UEFN mannequin with an IK Retargeter (Export Animations in the retargeter).
  2. Anim Blueprint. Duplicate ABP_Overlay_Injured (a complete example, see part 1) into a new folder, for example OverlayPose/WoundedArm/ABP_Overlay_WoundedArm. In its Class Defaults, set the Overlay Pose of Stand Relax Idle / Walk / Run / Sprint to your standing pose and of Crouch Relax Idle / Move to your crouched pose, and adjust the curve maps. Compile and save.
  3. Enum. Open /GASPALS/Systems/OverlaySystem/OverlayPose/Enum_OverlayPose, click Add Enumerator and name it WoundedArm. Save. The menu lists the new entry automatically.
  4. Link it. Open /GASPALS/Systems/OverlaySystem/AC_OverlaySystem, click Class Defaults, and under Overlay > Selection add an element to Overlay Pose Layers: key WoundedArm, value ABP_Overlay_WoundedArm. No graph edit. Compile and save. The sample pawns' components use the class default map, so the row reaches both pawns; if your own pawn's AC_OverlaySystem overrides the map (a reset arrow next to it in the Details panel), add the row there too.
  5. Test. Click Play, hold V and pick WoundedArm: the pose shows and no orange warning appears. Walk, run and crouch, then press N to switch to the other pawn and test again. For multiplayer, run a listen server with a client (see Networking) and pick the stance on the client: both windows show it.

Stances and items share the layer

A stance from the overlay menu and an item from the equipment menu both link the same overlay pose layer, and the last one wins. If a stance must combine with items (an injured character holding a pistol), make it an item pose instead: an equipment data asset with the stance poses (see Add an equipment item).

docs.title: 3. Add a body style
docs.text:
1. Animations. Author a standing and a crouched body pose on the UEFN mannequin, as for a stance.
  2. Duplicate /GASPALS/Systems/OverlaySystem/OverlayBody/Feminine/ABP_OverlayBody_Feminine into a new folder and name it, for example, ABP_OverlayBody_Heavy.
  3. In its Class Defaults, set Pose Stand Idle, Pose Stand Move, Pose Crouch Idle and Pose Crouch Move (the shipped styles use the standing pose for both standing entries and the crouched pose for both crouched ones). Compile and save.
  4. Open /GASPALS/Systems/OverlaySystem/OverlayBody/Enum_OverlayBody, click Add Enumerator and name it Heavy. Save.
  5. In the Class Defaults of AC_OverlaySystem, add an element to Overlay Body Layers: key Heavy, value ABP_OverlayBody_Heavy. Compile and save.
  6. Test. Click Play, hold B and pick Heavy. Stand and crouch, then press N and check the other pawn.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Ready and aim poses for items: hold the weapon raised (Ready) and at the eye (Aim). Set Can Aim on. The state machine uses Ready after aiming and drops to Relaxed after Ready Hold Time Idle / Moving (3 / 2 s).
  • Aim sweeps: copy the format of OverlayPose/Rifle/AO_Rifle_Stand_Sweep: a 1-second animation aiming straight up at the start, level in the middle and straight down at the end, with Additive Anim Type Mesh Space and Base Pose Type Selected animation frame (the middle frame).
  • Hand IK: set enable_handik_l (or _r) to 1 in the poses where the support hand holds the item, and add a HandIK socket on the item.
  • New settings on the base: if you add a variable to ABP_OverlayPose_Base, existing children keep their own class defaults (empty or 0). Set the value on every child.
  • Authoring curves in animations instead of curve maps: apply the Create_LayeringCurves animation modifier (OverlaySystem/AnimModifiers) to your pose animations and edit the keys.
  • Warning on screen (OverlayPoseLayers has no anim layer class...): the enum value has no row in the map; see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Add the systems to your own pawn
Add the systems to your own pawn
docs.text:
The simplest path is a child Blueprint of a sample pawn (Use GASPALS in your own project). This page is for when you need your own pawn class, for example to add GASPALS to an existing character. It lists every connection the sample pawns make. Open SandboxCharacter_CMC or SandboxCharacter_Mover next to your pawn and copy the graphs as you go.

Background: Architecture.

docs.title: 1. Base class and movement
docs.text:
Character (CMC)Pawn with Mover

Parent class Character. Copy the sample's Character Movement settings (CharMoveComp: crouched half height 60, use controller desired rotation, rotation rate yaw -1, can walk off ledges when crouching, nav agent can crouch). Speeds, acceleration, ground friction and braking are set every frame by the pawn's pre-movement update from its GASPALS > Movement settings, so copy those variables and the Calculate* functions too.

Parent class Pawn, with a CharacterMoverComponent named CharacterMover: copy its Movement Modes, Transitions (BP_MovementTransition_SuggestedMode, which the ragdoll needs, and BP_MovementTransition_Cover), Shared Settings (legacy movement and stance settings) and Sync Inputs For Sim Proxy. Copy the pawn's Movement Mode Map too (it maps the Mover mode names to the animation's movement modes, Cover to OnGround). Add a NavMoverComponent for AI. Turn off Replicate Movement on the pawn (Mover replicates itself), and implement MoverInputProducerInterface (see Cover).

Capsule: half height 86 (radius 30 on the Mover sample, 40 on the CMC sample). The capsule must ignore the Visibility, Camera and Cover channels, so camera, aim and cover traces pass through characters: use the CharacterCapsule collision profile (the Mover sample), or a custom profile with those responses (the CMC sample).

docs.title: 2. Components
docs.text: Component Notes Third-person Skeletal Mesh SKM_UEFN_Mannequin with SandboxCharacter_Mover_ABP or SandboxCharacter_CMC_ABP, location (0, 0, -88), yaw -90. Its name must match Third Person Mesh Name on AC_FirstPersonSystem. SkeletalMesh_FP (Skeletal Mesh, child of the mesh) SKM_UEFN_Mannequin_FP_Arms with ABP_FirstPerson_UEFN; Only Owner See, Owner No See, no shadow, First Person Primitive Type FirstPerson. The first-person logic mesh. VisualOverride (Child Actor, child of the mesh) Attached directly to the third-person mesh (no socket), component tag VisualOverride, Set Owner on, no child actor class (the visual override manager sets it). GameplayCamera (Gameplay Camera, child of the mesh, socket root) Camera asset CameraAsset_SandboxCharacter, Auto Activate off, absolute rotation. MotionWarping For traversal. SpringArm > Camera (optional) The legacy camera, used only when DDCVar.NewGameplayCameraSystem.Enable is off. Camera Auto Activate off. AC_CameraSystem, AC_EquipmentSystem, AC_OverlaySystem, AC_FirstPersonSystem, AC_TraversalLogic, AC_TraversalTracer, AC_VisualOverrideManager The systems. AC_FirstPersonSystem is the only first-person component: it also builds the first-person meshes of the retargeted characters and the held items. AC_CoverSystem_CMC or AC_CoverSystem_Mover Name it AC_CoverSystem. AC_RagdollSystem, AC_PreCMCTick Character only. AC_SmartObjectAnimation, AC_FoleyEvents Optional: benches, foley sounds. PhysicsControl, AC_PostABPTick Mover only, for the physics ragdoll and takedowns. Copying these means copying the ragdoll logic of SandboxCharacter_Mover too (including the hard reference to the Physics Control Asset, see Ragdoll and teleport); a child Blueprint of it is simpler. AC_DebugTools Optional: demo shot, spawn / rotate, teleport, fly. Shot, rotate and teleport need a ragdoll system and TeleportCharacter (see below); fly needs a CharacterMoverComponent (Debug tools). Its inputs are wired in the pawn: see Adding the debug tools to another pawn.

docs.title: Component settings
docs.text:
Set these on your pawn's components (class defaults do not reach existing component templates):

Component Setting AC_CoverSystem Enable Cover on (the class default, so a new component already has it). AC_TraversalLogic Is Mover Character on for Mover pawns. AC_FirstPersonSystem Third Person Mesh Name = your body mesh component's name (SkeletalMesh on the Mover sample, CharacterMesh0 on the CMC sample); Default Setup = your mannequin's PDA_FirstPersonSetup (the class default, DA_FirstPersonSetup_UEFN, is the one for the UEFN mannequin). AC_EquipmentSystem, AC_OverlaySystem, AC_VisualOverrideManager, AC_CameraSystem, AC_TraversalLogic Component Replicates on.

docs.title: 3. Interfaces
docs.text: Add the interfaces in Class Settings > Implemented Interfaces: BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn and BPI_ModularSystems on both pawn types, plus MoverInputProducerInterface on a Mover pawn (see Cover).

docs.title: BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn
docs.text:
Function Return Required by Get_PropertiesForAnimation S_CharacterPropertiesForAnimation Character, overlay and first-person Anim Blueprints, cover Get_PropertiesForCamera S_CharacterPropertiesForCamera Camera director Get_PropertiesForTraversal S_CharacterPropertiesForTraversal Traversal Get_AimRay the crosshair aim ray (from AC_CameraSystem) Cover (cover target, aim from cover). Unimplemented, it returns zeros and cover finds no target. TeleportCharacter whether it did something Debug tools teleport and rotate (see below) Set_CharacterInputState (sets the input state) AI StateTree tasks Get_PropertiesForRagdoll, Get_MMIResult, Get_MMIAnimContexts ragdoll and interaction data Mover Anim Blueprint (ragdoll and takedowns) AddTarget, RemoveTarget Target dummy (optional)

Copy the implementations from the sample pawn: they read your movement component and the system components.

docs.title: BPI_ModularSystems
docs.text:
Implement the event InitializeModularSystems with the initialization chain, in this order:

  1. UpdateFirstPersonVisuals: tell your AC_FirstPersonSystem which body is shown, with SetActiveBody(the visual override's child actor, else self; SkeletalMesh_FP). Copy the function and GetVisualMeshes (with GetVisualThirdPersonMesh and GetVisualFirstPersonMesh) from the sample.
  2. Overlay_Initialize(third-person mesh) > AC_OverlaySystem.InitializeSystem.
  3. Equipment_Initialize(self, third-person mesh, SkeletalMesh_FP, visual TP mesh, visual FP mesh) > AC_EquipmentSystem.InitializeSystem, with the visual meshes from GetVisualMeshes.
  4. AC_CameraSystem.InitializeSystem(self, visual TP mesh, visual FP mesh, GameplayCamera).
  5. Character only: Ragdoll_Initialize(self, mesh, capsule) > AC_RagdollSystem.InitializeSystem.
  6. FirstPerson_InitializePrimitives > AC_FirstPersonSystem.InitializePrimitives.
  7. AC_CoverSystem.InitializeSystem(self), then bind AC_CoverSystem.OnCoverVaultReady to your traversal call (see Traversal).

The _Initialize functions (category GASPALS > Integration) find the component by class and skip it when your pawn doesn't have it. Copy them from the sample rather than calling the component variables, so you can leave those components out (Turning systems on and off).

The event runs again when the visible character changes: keep it safe to call more than once.

docs.title: Ragdoll and teleport (optional)
docs.text:
So the debug tools and the TriggerRagdoll anim notify work on your pawn:

  • Teleport: implement TeleportCharacter from BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn (copy it from the sample pawn of the same movement type). It returns whether it did something.
  • Ragdoll: a Character pawn gets it from AC_RagdollSystem, which implements BPI_RagdollSystem. A Mover pawn ragdolls in its own graph: add BPI_RagdollSystem to the pawn and implement IsRagdollActive, RequestRagdoll, ApplyRagdollImpulse and RequestGetUp (copy them from SandboxCharacter_Mover). Implement RequestGetUp to support the get-up keys; unimplemented, it returns false and the character cannot get up with X or Space.
  • Get-up keys: X is handled by AC_RagdollSystem on a Character pawn, by the pawn on a Mover pawn (ragdolling: RequestGetUp, else start the ragdoll). For Space, call RequestGetUp from your jump input while ragdolling: copy the Character sample's Ragdoll_RequestGetUp wrapper (it finds the component by class, so the pawn still compiles without it), or on a Mover pawn call RequestGetUp from the jump input in the Ragdoll mode.
  • Physics Control (Mover): the PhysicsControl component holds its Physics Control Asset through a soft reference only, so in a packaged game the asset can be garbage-collected and the physics profiles stop applying. Keep the loaded asset in a variable from BeginPlay, as SandboxCharacter_Mover does with LoadedPhysicsControlAsset.

docs.title: 4. Startup
docs.text: When Do BeginPlay Mover: the mesh ticks after CharacterMover and after the actor. Character: CharacterMovement ticks after AC_PreCMCTick, and bind AC_PreCMCTick's Tick to your pre-movement event. Then call InitializeModularSystems (on self). Possessed (server) Call a reliable Client RPC on the owner that runs SetupCamera and SetupInput, then BPFL_GASPALS.CheckConsoleVariables (pass self; it shows an on-screen warning listing the DDCvar.* variables the project does not declare). Character: also AC_PreCMCTick.AddTickPrerequisiteActor(Controller). SetupCamera If DDCVar.NewGameplayCameraSystem.Enable: GameplayCamera.ActivateCameraForPlayerController(PC, true); else activate the legacy spring arm camera and make the pawn the view target. Copy the sample pawn's function. SetupInput For each entry of an Input Mapping Contexts map (context > priority, default IMC_Sandbox at 0): Enhanced Input Local Player Subsystem > Add Mapping Context. Copy the sample pawn's function.

docs.title: 5. Input
docs.text:
Handle in the pawn: move, look, sprint, walk, strafe, aim, crouch, jump, cover. The other actions are handled by the components and the controller (see Add or rebind inputs). Replicate the input state with a reliable Server RPC that sets a replicated S_PlayerInputState (the CMC sample replicates it skipping the owner). Copy the GASPALS > Input variables too: Input Mapping Contexts and the Hold Toggle settings (Toggle Crouch, Toggle Walk, Toggle Sprint, Toggle Aim, Toggle Strafe), which the sample handlers read through BPFL_GASPALS.GetHoldToggleInput.

N (next pawn), M (next character) and J (teleport) are not handled by the pawn: PC_Sandbox handles them, and the pawn and character switches go through GM_Sandbox. Keep PC_Sandbox and GM_Sandbox (or children of them) to use these keys with your pawn.

docs.title: 6. Cover
docs.text:
Character (CMC)Pawn with Mover

In the pre-movement event (from AC_PreCMCTick), first call AC_CoverSystem.UpdateCoverCMC(DeltaSeconds), then your rotation and speed updates. In cover, use the walk gait (sprint during a cover run).

In ProduceInput:

  1. RemapCoverMoveInput(move input) before setting the directional input.
  2. EvaluateCover(move input, delta seconds) after it; add its S_MoverCustomInputs_Cover output to the input collection.
  3. Crouch request = (wants to crouch or the cover's force crouch) and not IsCoverCrouchBlocked.
  4. Gait: walk in cover unless crouched, sprint during a cover run. Rotation offset 0 in cover.
  5. Orientation intent from GetCoverOrientationIntent.

Register BP_MovementMode_Cover as Cover, add BP_MovementTransition_Cover to the global transitions, and map Cover to OnGround in your Movement Mode Map (step 1). AC_CoverSystem_Mover ticks UpdateMoverCoverState, UpdateCoverVault and the cover marker itself.

Both: IA_CoverSticky Started calls RequestStickyCover; Completed and Canceled call ReleaseStickyCover. IA_CoverRun Started calls RequestCoverRun; Completed and Canceled call ReleaseCoverRun.

docs.title: 7. Traversal
docs.text:
Implement GetTraversalCheckInputs (copy from the sample) and on jump:

  1. If a traversal is possible (not already traversing; Mover: no montage playing), call AC_CoverSystem.RequestCoverVault.
  2. If it is not deferred, call AC_TraversalLogic.TryTraversalAction(GetTraversalCheckInputs, ...).
  3. If the traversal check or montage selection failed, jump.

OnCoverVaultReady (bound during initialization) calls TryTraversalAction when the character has turned to the wall.

docs.title: 8. Test
docs.text:
Run through the Quick start on your pawn: locomotion, traversal, cover (soft, sticky, run, corner, aim, vault), equipment in third and first person, overlays, perspectives, characters (M), and a listen server with a client (Networking).

While you play, watch for orange on-screen messages (missing console variables, an empty Input Mapping Contexts map, GASPALS First Person (...) setup warnings) and for "Accessed None" errors in the Output Log: each one points at a connection from the steps above. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Use GASPALS in your own project
Use GASPALS in your own project
docs.text:
There are two ways to start:

Start from When The template project (copy the project folder and rename the .uproject) A new game. Everything is configured. Your project + the plugin An existing project. Follow Installation, option B first: the plugin alone does not carry the collision channels, console variables and other project settings it needs.

Then make GASPALS yours without editing more of the plugin than needed. The plugin's assets are under GASPALS Content in the Content Browser (turn on Settings > Show Plugin Content if you don't see it).

docs.title: 1. Create your own game mode
docs.text:
In the Content Browser, right-click /GASPALS/Blueprints/GM_Sandbox > Create Child Blueprint Class, and save the child in your project's content, for example as GM_MyGame. Open it and set its Class Defaults:

Setting Value Default Pawn Class Your pawn (step 2), or a sample pawn. Pawn Classes Soft The pawns N cycles through (DDCvar.PawnClass indexes this list). Put your pawn in it if you keep the N key, or leave it empty to turn pawn switching off. Visual Overrides Soft The characters M cycles through (DDCvar.VisualOverride indexes this list). Player Controller Class PC_Sandbox or a child of it (it handles N, M and J).

Deriving from GM_Sandbox matters: the pawn switch and the visual override manager read their lists from it. In a game mode that does not derive from it, N and M do nothing and each pawn shows its own Default Visual Override (Characters, per pawn).

Always the same pawn

GM_Sandbox picks the pawn from DDCvar.PawnClass; at -1 (the default) it uses Default Pawn Class. If your game should always use the Default Pawn Class, keep the variable at -1 and empty Pawn Classes Soft: N then keeps the current pawn class. You can also remove the N mapping (step 3).

docs.title: 2. Create your pawn
docs.text:
Make a child Blueprint of SandboxCharacter_CMC or SandboxCharacter_Mover (right-click > Create Child Blueprint Class; see Mover and CMC pawns to choose). A child keeps every system wired, with every component setting of the sample, and lets you override what you need:

  • Tune the systems on your child's components (select the inherited component in the Components panel): cover, camera, first person and the others.
  • Override pawn functions (Get_PropertiesForCamera, GetTraversalCheckInputs...) for different behavior.
  • Add your gameplay: health, abilities, weapons firing.

Then set it as the Default Pawn Class of your game mode.

Your own character mesh goes in as a visual override (see Add a retargeted character); keep the UEFN mannequin on the pawn as the animation source.

To build a pawn from scratch instead, see Add the systems to your own pawn.

docs.title: 3. Use your own input mapping context
docs.text: The pawns add the contexts of their Input Mapping Contexts setting (class defaults, GASPALS > Input; default IMC_Sandbox) when a player possesses them. Rather than editing the plugin's IMC_Sandbox, duplicate it into your project's content, change the copy, and replace IMC_Sandbox with it in your pawn's Input Mapping Contexts. Keep the GASPALS input actions (IA_*) in it: the systems listen to those assets. See Add or rebind inputs.

docs.title: 4. Set up your levels
docs.text:
For each level, in World Settings > GameMode Override, pick GM_MyGame. Or set it once in Project Settings > Maps & Modes > Default GameMode.

Each level needs:

  • a Player Start;
  • a NavMeshBoundsVolume for cover runs and AI;
  • traversable obstacles on the Traversable channel (Make objects traversable);
  • cover geometry that blocks the Cover channel, as every profile that blocks Visibility does (Set up cover in a level).

Set your maps in Project Settings > Maps & Modes (Game Default Map, Editor Startup Map).

docs.title: 5. Remove demo features
docs.text:
Demo feature How to remove Pawn switching (N), character switching (M), teleport (J) Remove IA_NextPawn, IA_NextVisualOverride and IA_TeleportToTarget from your mapping context (step 3). Equipment and overlay menus (slow motion while open) Remove IA_Equipment, IA_Overlay_Pose, IA_Overlay_Body, IA_Select_Next and IA_Select_Previous from your mapping context, and select items and overlays from your gameplay (SelectNewEquipment on AC_EquipmentSystem, SelectNewOverlayPose / SelectNewOverlayBody on AC_OverlaySystem). Mover debug tools: demo shooting and spawning (aim + Left Button / E), debug flying (Z), the Mover pawn's teleport (J) Turn off Enable Debug Tools on the Mover pawn's AC_DebugTools component, or remove the component (the pawn reaches it through class lookups, so it still compiles). See Debug tools. On-screen debug prints The camera perspective change (1) prints the perspective name and the style change (2) prints "Camera change ..."; remove the two Print String nodes in the Event Graph of AC_CameraSystem.

To turn off a whole system (camera, cover, equipment, first person, overlay, ragdoll, traversal) or remove its component, see Turning systems on and off.

docs.title: 6. Check that it works
docs.text:
1. Open one of your levels and press Play. You control your pawn (not a sample pawn), with your input mapping context.
  2. Walk, sprint, crouch, and press Space at a low traversable obstacle: the character vaults or mantles. If it only jumps, the obstacle is not on the Traversable channel or the project settings are missing.
  3. Walk into a wall: the character takes cover. Hold T, scroll to the rifle and release: it is in hand.
  4. No orange message appears on screen. A message listing DDCvar.* names means the console variables from Installation are missing; InputMappingContexts is empty means your pawn's Input Mapping Contexts is empty.
  5. For a multiplayer game, play as a listen server with a client (Networking).

If something does not work, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: 7. Keep upgrades manageable
docs.text:
• Put your assets in your project's content, not in Plugins/GASPALS.
  • Prefer child Blueprints, duplicates and new data assets over editing the plugin's assets.
  • When you must edit a plugin asset, note it: you will merge it by hand when updating GASPALS.

docs.title: 8. Package
docs.text:
1. Add your maps to Project Settings > Packaging > List of maps to include in a packaged build.
  2. Keep the packaging settings from Installation.
  3. Install a C++ toolchain (Visual Studio 2022 on Windows): the engine plugins GASPALS needs make the packaging tool build a game target, even for a Blueprint-only project.
  4. Platforms > Windows > Package Project.

The demo's Game Animation Widget, Controls and Read Me panels are editor utility widgets: they do not exist in a packaged game.

docs.title: Add a retargeted character
docs.text:
This tutorial puts your own character on the GASPALS pawns. The pawns keep animating the UEFN mannequin; your character copies that animation through an IK Retargeter. Read Characters and visual overrides first if you want the background.

You need: a skeletal mesh with its skeleton and physics asset imported into the project. Time: 30 to 60 minutes, most of it spent on the retarget pose.

Fast path for UE5 mannequin and MetaHuman skeletons

If your character uses the UE5 mannequin skeleton (SK_Mannequin) or a MetaHuman body skeleton, the IK Rig, the retargeter, the VB Camera bone and the equipment sockets already exist. Skip to step 5 and use ABP_Retarget_UE5 or ABP_Retarget_Kellan as they are.

docs.title: 1. Prepare the skeleton
docs.text:
Open your character's Skeleton asset.

  1. Virtual bone. Right-click the root bone > Add Virtual Bone > pick head. Rename the new bone (VB root_head) to VB Camera, exactly. The first-person camera attaches to it.
  2. Check the bone names. The systems need root, pelvis, head, hand_l and hand_r. The first-person overlay modes also need spine_01 to spine_05, clavicle_l, clavicle_r and neck_01. If your skeleton names them differently, plan on the TrueFirstPerson mode (step 6) or rename the bones in your DCC tool.
  3. Equipment sockets. Equipment attaches to sockets on the skeleton. Open SK_Mannequin (/GASPALS/Characters/UE5_Mannequins/Meshes), select the seven sockets overlay_rifle, overlay_pistol, overlay_bow, overlay_box, overlay_barrel, overlay_binoculars and overlay_torch, right-click > Copy Selected Sockets, then in your skeleton right-click the matching hand bone > Paste Selected Sockets. On SK_Mannequin they hang from hand_r (rifle, pistol, binoculars, box) and hand_l (bow, torch, barrel).
  4. Save the skeleton.

You will fine-tune the socket transforms in step 8, with the items in hand.

docs.title: 2. Create the IK Rig
docs.text:
Content Browser > right-click > Animation > Retargeting > IK Rig, pick your skeletal mesh. Then:

  1. Set the Retarget Root to pelvis.
  2. Click Auto Create Retarget Chains (or add them by hand). Use the standard names: Root, Spine, Neck, Head, LeftClavicle, LeftArm, LeftLeg, finger chains, and the right-side mirrors.
  3. Add IK goals on the hands and feet (LeftHandIK, RightHandIK, LeftFootIK, RightFootIK) and assign them to the arm and leg chains.

Similar skeletons can start from a duplicate of IK_UE5_Mannequin_Retarget (/GASPALS/Characters/UE5_Mannequins/Rigs) or IK_Metahuman_Retarget (/GASPALS/MetaHumans/Common/Rigs).

docs.title: 3. Create the IK Retargeter
docs.text:
Right-click > Animation > Retargeting > IK Retargeter.

  1. Source IK Rig: IK_UEFN_Mannequin (/GASPALS/Characters/UEFN_Mannequin/Rigs). Target IK Rig: the rig from step 2.
  2. In the chain mapping, use Auto-Map Chains and check every chain.
  3. Retarget pose: edit the target's retarget pose until the arms, hands and fingers match the UEFN mannequin's pose in the viewport. This is the step that decides the quality of the result.
  4. Op stack: keep the default ops (pelvis motion, FK chains, IK). Make sure there is a Curve Remap op with Copy All Source Curves on: the hand IK weights travel as curves. The shipped retargeters have no Root Motion op: if the default ops added one, remove it (the character follows the pawn, so it needs no root motion).
  5. Preview a few animations from /GASPALS/Characters/UEFN_Mannequin/Animations (idle, walk, a rifle pose) and fix feet, hands and pelvis.

The same retargeter is used twice: for the third-person pose (step 4) and for the first-person overlays (step 6).

docs.title: 4. Create the retarget Anim Blueprint
docs.text:
1. Duplicate ABP_Retarget_UE5 (/GASPALS/Blueprints/RetargetedCharacters) and name it, for example, ABP_Retarget_MyHero.
  2. Open it and change its target skeleton to yours (Asset > Retarget to a different skeleton, or in the Class Settings).
  3. Select the Retarget Pose From Mesh node and set IK Retargeter Asset to your retargeter. Leave Retarget From on Parent Skeletal Mesh Component and the source pose pin unconnected.
  4. Keep the CR_Humanoid_HandIK node after it, and keep the Event Graph, which finds the pawn's equipment component for the hand IK targets.
  5. Compile and save.

docs.title: 5. Create the character Blueprint
docs.text:
Duplicate BP_RetargetedCharacter_Manny (quickest: every setting is already there) or create a child Blueprint of BP_RetargetedCharacter_Base. Name it, for example, BP_RetargetedCharacter_MyHero.

  1. Select the inherited SkeletalMesh component:
    • Skeletal Mesh Asset: your mesh.
    • Anim Class: your retarget Anim Blueprint (ABP_Retarget_UE5 for the UE5 mannequin skeleton, ABP_Retarget_Kellan for MetaHumans).
    • Keep Visibility Based Anim Tick Option = Only Tick Pose When Rendered.
  2. Clothing, hair, accessories: add them as children of SkeletalMesh. Everything attached under the body mesh is treated as part of the third-person character; no component tags are needed.
    • Same skeleton and no post-process Anim Blueprint: use Leader Pose (Kellan's construction script function EnableMasterPose shows how).
    • Own skeleton with a post-process Anim Blueprint that copies the pose from the parent (typical for MetaHuman clothing): leave the anim class empty.
  3. The base class returns SkeletalMesh as the body mesh (GetVisualBodyMesh, from the BPI_VisualOverride interface). Camera, equipment and first person use it, and the base class makes it tick after the pawn mesh, which keeps the pose in sync. If your body is another component, override GetVisualBodyMesh to return it.

docs.title: 6. Set up first person
docs.text:
Characters have no first-person component: the pawn's AC_FirstPersonSystem builds your character's first-person meshes from a first-person setup data asset.

  1. Duplicate DA_FirstPersonSetup_Manny (/GASPALS/Systems/FirstPersonSystem/Setups) and name it, for example, DA_FirstPersonSetup_MyHero (or create a Data Asset of the class PDA_FirstPersonSetup).

  2. Open it and fill it:

    Field Value Full Meshes Your body mesh first (it becomes the lead), then the clothing. Prefer a headless body; leave empty to reuse the third-person mesh with the head bone hidden. Arms Meshes / Body Meshes Only for FirstPersonOverlaySplit. Generate them with EUB_SplitFirstPersonMesh (see Configure first person). Retargeter Your IK Retargeter. Required for the overlay modes on any skeleton other than UEFN; without it your character uses TrueFirstPerson. Eye Offset Start with (0, 12, 0) (what Manny, Quinn and Kellan use): 12 cm forward of the head bone. Tune it in step 8. Camera Bone / Head Bone Keep VB Camera / head unless your skeleton names them differently.

  3. In your character Blueprint, open Class Defaults and set First Person Setup to your new asset.

Warning

A Blueprint duplicated from BP_RetargetedCharacter_Manny still points at DA_FirstPersonSetup_Manny. Set your own setup, or your character's first person uses Manny's meshes.

The first-person mode is not set on the character: the pawn's First Person Mode applies to every character. If your skeleton lacks the UE-standard spine names, set TrueFirstPerson on the pawn's AC_FirstPersonSystem. Without a setup, your character's body mesh is reused as the first-person mesh with the head hidden, and a warning is shown.

docs.title: 7. Register the character
docs.text:
Open /GASPALS/Blueprints/GM_Sandbox, Class Defaults, and add your Blueprint to Visual Overrides Soft. Its position in the array is its index (0 = first).

If you use your own game mode, derive it from GM_Sandbox so the manager finds the list.

docs.title: 8. Test and tune
docs.text:
1. Play. Press M until your character shows, or open the console (`) and type DDCvar.VisualOverride <index>.
  2. Third person: walk, run, crouch, jump, vault. Watch the feet (sliding means a chain or retarget pose problem) and the hands.
  3. Equipment: hold T, scroll to the rifle and release; then try the pistol and the bow (and the revolver, if you removed it from Hidden Equipment). If an item floats or sits in the wrong place, open your skeleton, select the overlay_* socket, right-click > Add Preview Asset with the item's mesh (/GASPALS/Systems/EquipmentSystem/Assets/Meshes) and adjust the socket.
  4. First person: press 1 until the camera is in first person. Look down, aim (Right Button), run. If the camera sits inside the head or in front of the face, adjust Eye Offset in your first-person setup (X right, Y forward, Z up, in cm, in mesh space at the reference pose). Aim with the rifle and check that the sights line up.
  5. Warnings: orange messages starting with GASPALS First Person (...) list missing setup (no first-person setup, no camera bone, no head bone, missing retargeter...). See Troubleshooting.
  6. Press N to switch to the other pawn and test again. For multiplayer, run a listen server with a client.

docs.title: 9. Make it the default character
docs.text:
Project Settings > Engine > Data Driven CVars: set the default value of DDCvar.VisualOverride to your index. Every pawn then starts with your character, and M cycles to the next character, back to the UEFN mannequin after the last one. To stop players from cycling, remove the M mapping of IA_NextVisualOverride from the input mapping contexts, or keep only your entry in the list. For one pawn only, or with your own game mode, set Default Visual Override on that pawn's AC_VisualOverrideManager and turn Follow Global Visual Override off (see Characters).

Keep the UEFN mannequin on the pawn

Do not replace the pawn's own mesh with your character. The character Anim Blueprints, overlay poses, traversal montages and Control Rigs expect the UEFN skeleton; your character gets all of it through the retargeter.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• Skeleton: VB Camera virtual bone, root/head/hand_l/hand_r, seven overlay_* sockets
  • IK Rig with standard chains and a pelvis retarget root
  • IK Retargeter from IK_UEFN_Mannequin, retarget pose matched, Curve Remap op
  • Retarget Anim Blueprint with your retargeter
  • Character Blueprint: body mesh and anim class, clothing attached under the body mesh
  • First-person setup (PDA_FirstPersonSetup): meshes, retargeter, eye offset; set as First Person Setup
  • Added to GM_Sandbox > Visual Overrides Soft
  • Tested: locomotion, equipment, first person, both pawns, listen server

docs.title: Make objects traversable
docs.text:
Traversal only considers geometry that blocks the Traversable trace channel. Everything else is jumped. Background: Traversal system.

Before you start

The Traversable channel and the TraversalObjectPreset profile come from the project's collision settings. In a project of your own, add them first: see Project settings.

docs.title: Option 1: use the grey-box block
docs.text: Place /GASPALS/Levels/LevelPrototyping/LevelBlock_Traversable and scale it. It is already set up, and is what the demo levels use.

docs.title: Option 2: set the collision preset
docs.text:
1. Select the static mesh actor in the level (or the mesh component in a Blueprint).
  2. In the Details panel, under Collision, set Collision Presets to TraversalObjectPreset.

The preset blocks everything, including Traversable.

docs.title: Option 3: custom collision
docs.text:
Use this to keep your object's other collision responses:

  1. Under Collision, set Collision Presets to Custom.... The responses of the previous preset are kept as the starting point.
  2. Under Trace Responses, set Traversable to Block.

To make every placement of a mesh traversable, do this in the static mesh asset itself (Static Mesh Editor, Details panel, Collision section) instead of on each actor. For Blueprint actors, set it on the mesh components in the Blueprint.

docs.title: Shapes that work
docs.text:
Obstacle Typical result Low and thin (a fence, a low wall) Hurdle or vault, depending on speed and what is behind it. Low and deep (a crate, a table) Vault or mantle up onto it. Chest height Mantle. Taller than the character can reach Jump. Narrower than 70 cm Jump (Min Ledge Width on AC_TraversalTracer).

Simple collision that matches the visible top edge gives the best results: the warp targets are placed on the measured ledge. The character also needs room: the space on top of the obstacle (and behind it, for a vault or hurdle) must be free of anything that blocks Visibility.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Press Play, run at the obstacle and press Space (gamepad A). The character vaults, hurdles or mantles instead of jumping.
  2. Try it on both pawns (Mover and CMC), walking, running and standing in front of it.

docs.title: Debug
docs.text:
1. Type DDCvar.Traversal.DrawDebugLevel 3 in the console during Play, then jump at the obstacle: the traces, ledges and room checks are drawn and the measured data is printed. DDCvar.Traversal.DrawDebugDuration sets how long the shapes stay.
  2. Drop a BP_TraversalTester (/GASPALS/Systems/TraversalSystem) in front of the obstacle in the editor, its forward (X) arrow toward it: it draws the ledges the tracer finds without playing. Its Initial Trace Distance (600) sets how far it looks. It finds the obstacle with the Pawn collision profile, not the Traversable channel, so use step 1 to check the channel.
  3. show collision shows whether the obstacle's collision is what you expect.
Symptom Fix The character always jumps The obstacle does not block Traversable, or it is narrower than Min Ledge Width. If no obstacle traverses at all, check that the project has the Traversable channel and that Traversable Trace Channel on AC_TraversalLogic names it. The hands or feet miss the edge The collision top is not where the visible edge is. The character jumps although the obstacle blocks Traversable Something that blocks Visibility is in the way on top of or behind the obstacle (the room checks failed), or no chooser row matches the obstacle's height and depth. A traversal plays into a wall behind the obstacle The room check found space; add collision for the wall, or block Visibility on it.
